records.themeTitle: The covenantal root disclosed on Yom Kippur
records.themeSummary: The day reveals a deeper holiness that does not erase the need for present concern.
records.explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the siman's link between Yom Kippur, the world to come, and the designation ‘righteous’ as guarding the covenant. Its claim concerns what is disclosed from the depth of the heart. It should therefore be read alongside, rather than in place of, the siman's repeated qualification ‘sometimes’ and its instruction that the person remain concerned during the year.
records.targetEnglish: This is the meaning of Yom Kippur: ‘On this day He will atone for you, to purify you’ (Leviticus 16:30). Then there is an awakening of the understanding in the heart, which is the world to come, where there is neither eating nor drinking; then Israel's sin will be sought and not found. Then all Israel have a share in the world to come, as it says, ‘Your people are all righteous’ (Isaiah 60:21), as the Mishnah teaches at the beginning of Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a). ‘Righteous’ means one who guards the covenant. Those who transgressed in damaging the covenant were not excluded there from a share in the world to come, for in truth, from the depth of the heart that will then be revealed, they are all so. This revelation occurs on Yom Kippur as well: ‘The goat shall bear their iniquities with it to an isolated land’ (Leviticus 16:22), to Azazel.
records.originHebrew: וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִקָּרוֹ לְכַפָּרַת פְּגַם הַבְּרִית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא ס"ו לְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עוּזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם): "מֻבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא", וּבֶן עוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא צַדִּיק בַּמִּשְׁנָה דְּרֵישׁ חֵלֶק, וְהַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית.  וּלְכָךְ יִדְאַג כָּל הַשָּׁנָה (שָׁם), לְפִי שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה לִכְאוֹרָה בַּהֲפֶךְ, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נ, א): "עוֹלָם הָפוּךְ רָאִיתִי", עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נֶגֶד עוֹלָם הַבָּא.  וּפְעָמִים הוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּפְרֶה וְיִרְבֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא שָׁם: "סָגֵי וּמַסְגֵּי".  וּפְעָמִים שֶׁהוּא לְהַצְלָחָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כִּדְמַסַּיֵּים קְרָא דְּ"יִרְאֶה זֶרַע יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים" – "וְחֵפֶץ ה' בְּיָדוֹ יִצְלָח", וּבִבְרָכוֹת (ה, א) דָּרְשׁוּ "חֵפֶץ ה'" דְּהַאי קְרָא אַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קפז, א).
records.originEnglish: And the essence of Yom Kippur is for the atonement of the blemish of the covenant, as brought in Yoma (67b) that the scapegoat comes to atone for the deeds of Uzza and Azael, and this is why they stated (there): 'he is assured that he is a son of the World to Come,' and a possessor of the World to Come is termed righteous (tzaddik) in the Mishnah at the beginning of Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a), which signifies one who guards the covenant.  And therefore let him worry all year long (there), because the event superficially appears to be the complete opposite, yet in truth they said (Pesachim 50a): 'An inverted world have I seen,' this physical world standing opposite to the World to Come.  And at times it is in order that he be fruitful and multiply, as brought there: 'he will increase and multiply' (Yoma 88a).  And at times it is a sign for success in words of Torah, as the verse which begins 'he shall prolong days' concludes: 'and the desire of Hashem shall prosper in his hand' (Isaiah 53:10), and in Berakhot (5a) they expounded 'the desire of Hashem' in this verse as referring to words of Torah, see there, and so is it expounded in the Zohar (Part I, 187a).
records.targetHebrew: וזהו ענין יום הכפורים ד״ביום הזה יכפר [עליכם לטהר אתכם]״ (ויקרא ט״ז:ל׳) שאז התעוררות הבינה שבלב שהוא העולם הבא שאין בו אכילה ולא שתיה שאז יבקש עון ישראל ואיננו ואז כל ישראל יש להם חלק לעולם הבא, שנאמר: ״ועמך כלם צדיקים״ (ישעיה ס:כא), כדתנן [ריש פרק חלק, סנהדרין צ׳ עמוד א׳] ו״צדיק״ היינו שומר הברית ולא הוציאו שם עוברי עבירה בפגם הברית מחלק לעולם הבא דבאמת מצד עומק הלב שיתגלה אז הם כולם כן וכן ביום הכפורים הוא התגלות זה, ״ונשא השעיר [אתו] עונתם [אל ארץ גזרה]״ (ויקרא ט״ז:כ״ב) לעזאזל

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 10
records.themeTitle: Favorable judgment and responsibility for appearances
records.themeSummary: A hidden good intention calls for care both in judging and in being understood.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach supplies a concrete case of the good hidden beneath an apparently adverse act: Yosef sits apart because of a genuine conflict about precedence, and the brothers read it as hatred. The source holds both sides to a standard—the brothers should judge favorably, and Yosef should avoid leaving them room to err. This develops the siman's lesson without making hidden good intentions a reason to disregard the effect of one's conduct on others.
records.targetEnglish: ‘You intended evil against me; God intended it for good.’ Here Hashem showed how the tribes could be brought into Egyptian exile. The principal cause was their beginning to separate, for when Israel are united nothing can rule over them. Yosef separated from the tribes in this way. While Yaakov was alive it was not clear who was greatest among the tribes: sometimes he drew one closer and sometimes another, according to what was right in his eyes then. Before his death, however, when he blessed them and told Yehudah, ‘Your father's sons will bow to you,’ everyone recognized Yehudah's superiority. Yosef therefore did not know how to act. If he seated Yehudah at the head, he himself was king, and a king may not be slighted. If he sat at the head himself, he knew that Yehudah was the head. He therefore sat apart. The brothers judged that he did so from hatred, and were punished with exile because they should have judged him favorably. Yosef too was held at fault for leaving them room to err: he should actually have sat at the head, since he was king then, while knowing in his heart that Yehudah was greater. Since the brothers erred about him, some trace of the matter was present in human eyes. A person should therefore always pray not to judge his fellow adversely, and that his fellow not judge him adversely. The brothers were punished for failing to judge him favorably.
records.originHebrew: וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁזֶּה עַצְמוֹ הָיָה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ מֵעִנְיַן לָדוּן לְכַף זְכוּת, אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֹפֶן זֶה שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה לִכְאוֹרָה מוֹרֶה בְּבֵירוּר לְחוֹב, וְלֹא יָדַע זֶה מִקּוֹדֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּתַלְמִיד שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק וְדִבְּרָה תּוֹרָה לָשׁוֹן נְקִיָּה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה חָשׁוּד אֶצְלוֹ עַל זְנוּת; וּמִדְּאָמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק מַשְׁמָע דְּבֶאֱמֶת כָּשֵׁר הָיָה, רַק שֶׁהוּא לֹא דָּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת, וְהָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט עֲבוּר זֶה רְאִיַּת הַקֶּרִי.
records.originEnglish: And it appears that this itself was what is related there afterward regarding judging favorably, even in a case where the outward action seemingly points clearly to guilt, and he did not know this beforehand, as stated there regarding "a student who was not vetted," where the Torah employed clean language, meaning that he was suspected by him of licentiousness; and from the phrasing "not vetted," it implies that in truth he was worthy, only that the master had not judged him favorably, and the resulting judgment for this was the nocturnal emission.
records.targetHebrew: וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹקִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטוֹבָה. בָּזֶה הָעִנְיָן הֶרְאָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵיךְ הָיָה בְּאֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִיא הַשְּׁבָטִים בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְעִיקָּר הָיָה הַפֵּירוּד שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ לְהִפָּרֵד, כִּי בְּעֵת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּאַחְדוּת לֹא יוּכַל לִשְׁלוֹט עֲלֵיהֶם שׁוּם דָּבָר. וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה הָיָה שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ יוֹסֵף מִן הַשְּׁבָטִים, כִּי בְּעוֹד שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיָה קַיָּים לֹא הָיָה נִיכָּר מִמֶּנּוּ מִי הוּא הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבַּשְּׁבָטִים כִּי לִפְעָמִים הָיָה מְקָרֵב אֶת זֶה יוֹתֵר וְלִפְעָמִים זֶה יוֹתֵר, אֵיזֶה שֶׁהָיָה יָשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, אַךְ קוֹדֶם לִפְטִירָתוֹ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבֵּרְכָם וְאָמַר לִיהוּדָא "יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ" אָז הִכִּירוּ כֻּלָּם כִּי יְהוּדָא גָּבַר בְּאֶחָיו, וּלְכָךְ לֹא הָיָה יוֹסֵף יוֹדֵעַ אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג, בְּאִם לְהוֹשִׁיב אֶת יְהוּדָא בָּרֹאשׁ הֲלֹא הוּא מֶלֶךְ וְאָסוּר לְזַלְזֵל בַּמֶּלֶךְ, וּבְאִם שֶׁיֵּשֵׁב הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ בָּרֹאשׁ הֲלֹא יוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמוֹ כִּי יְהוּדָא הוּא הָרֹאשׁ עַל כֵּן יָשַׁב בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְלֹא עִם הַשְּׁבָטִים, וְהַשְּׁבָטִים דָּנוּ אוֹתוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה זֹאת מֵחֲמַת שִׂנְאָה וּלְכָךְ נֶעֶנְשׁוּ לִהְיוֹת בְּגָלוּת כִּי הָיָה לָהֶם לְדוּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת, וְגַם לְיוֹסֵף נֶחְשַׁב לְחֵטְא עַל אֲשֶׁר הִנִּיחַ לָהֶם מָקוֹם לִטְעוֹת בּוֹ, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה לוֹ לְהִתְנַהֵג שֶׁהוּא יֵשֵׁב בָּרֹאשׁ מֵאַחַר שֶׁלְּעֵת עַתָּה הוּא מֶלֶךְ, אַךְ בְּלִבּוֹ הָיָה צָרִיךְ לֵידַע כִּי יְהוּדָא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ. וּבֶאֱמֶת מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים טָעוּ בּוֹ הָיָה נִמְצָא בַּדָּבָר שֵׁמֶץ מֶנְהוּ לְעֵינֵי אָדָם, וְעַל זֶה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תָּמִיד לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא בְּדַעְתּוֹ לָדוּן אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ לְחוֹב, וְגַם שֶׁחֲבֵרוֹ לֹא יְדוּנוֹ לְחוֹב וְעַל זֶה נֶעֶנְשׁוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁעָבְרוּ עַל שֶׁהָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְדוּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת.

records.themeTitle: Immersion and the inward attitude of study
records.themeSummary: The discussion concerns readiness to receive Torah with awe, including after an involuntary event.
records.explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the siman's pairing of water with awe in study. It explicitly discusses an involuntary event and rejects attributing frivolity to the holy person's waking conduct; its concern is the remaining bodily state and readiness for attachment to Torah. This preserves the difference between the account of purification and an accusation of a chosen offense.
records.targetEnglish: The reason for immersion before words of Torah is explained in Berakhot there: one must learn with awe, fear, trembling, and perspiration. See Rashi there, under ‘From here,’ who says that the condition of a baal keri comes only from levity and an unrestrained state of mind. If immersion is required even for an involuntary event, that too must in some sense belong to this category. Yet Heaven forbid that the supremely holy should have even a moment of levity or an unrestrained mind while awake. Nevertheless, so long as they have not been completely freed from the serpent's effect, to become a heart of flesh as in the future and as Yaakov was, even an involuntary event in sleep was not free of bodily pleasure at that moment. This too is counted in that category and gives rise to powers of impurity, Heaven forbid. For this the Sages instituted immersion or washing with nine kav of water: through this one is purified from that spirit of impurity and unrestrained state of mind that proceeds from it, and can cleave to the light and holiness of Torah, which is a tree of life.
records.originHebrew: וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בִּדְחִילוּ, שֶׁזֶּה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ, דְּאֵימָה וְיִרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב עַמּוּד א), וְהוּא דּוּגְמַת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל: בְּרוֹתְחִין קִלְקְלוּ, בְּרוֹתְחִין נִידּוֹנוּ. וּלְכָךְ עֶזְרָא תִּקֵּן טְבִילָה לְבַעֲלֵי קְרָיִין כְּדֵי לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה בְּאֵימָה כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּתַקֵּן עַצְמוֹ קוֹדֶם, וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:): תּוֹרָה בְּטָהֳרָה, וְאָמְרִינַן עֲלַהּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (כט:): הָא לַן וְהָא לְהוּ.
records.originEnglish: And for this, one requires words of Torah studied with reverence (b'dchilu), which is the exact opposite of complacency—characterized by dread and awe as written in Berakhot 22a, and this mirrors what they said in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 108a) regarding the Generation of the Flood: through boiling passion they corrupted, and in boiling waters they were judged. And therefore Ezra instituted ritual immersion for those who experience seminal emission so that they engage in Torah with awe, as brought there, meaning that one must purify himself first, along the lines of Yoma 72b: Torah studied in purity, and we said concerning this in Kiddushin 29b: this applies to us (in Babylonia) and that applies to them (in the Land of Israel).
records.targetHebrew: וטעם טבילה לדברי תורה מבואר בברכות שם: לפי שצריך ללמוד באימה, ביראה, ברתת ובזיעה ועיין שם ברש״י דבור המתחיל ״מכאן״, שבעל קרי אינו אלא מתוך קלות ראש וזחות הדעת ואם כן, דגם לאונסו צריך על כרחך [לומר] דגם זה מקלות ראש ואף דחלילה לקדושי עליון שיהיה להם שום רגע קלות ראש חס ושלום בהקיץ ולא זחות דעת מכל מקום, כל זמן שלא ניצולו מעטיו של נחש לגמרי להיות ״לב בשר״ כלעתיד וכיעקב אבינו עליו השלום גם במה דחזא לאונסיה בשינה לא ניצול מהרגשת הנאה גופנית בשעתו בשנתו, וגם זה נחשב לקלות ראש וזחות דעת וגורם תולדת כחות טומאה רחמנא ליצלן ועל זה תיקנו חכמים הטבילה או רחיצה בט׳ קבין, שבכך הוא נטהר מאותו רוח הטומאה וזחות דעת הנמשך מזה, ויוכל לידבק במאור וקדשת התורה שהוא עץ חיים

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 22:1
records.themeTitle: Grafting souls and the different assignments of generations
records.themeSummary: The shared image of grafting does not require an identical mapping of historical generations.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov makes the siman's botanical interpretation of ‘venivrekhu’ explicit: souls are planted into Avraham's holiness. The historical allocation differs, however. This passage links the generation of the dispersion to the Egyptian exile and its bricks, whereas Rav Tzadok here associates Sodom with the Exodus and the dispersion with the later return from Shinar. The comparison supports the meaning of grafting while preserving the distinct schemes of repair.
records.targetEnglish: ‘All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you’ (Genesis 12:3). ‘Venivrekhu’ is an expression like the Talmud's layering of a tree. This accords with the holy Ari (Gate of Verses, Shemot, under ‘A new king arose’): the generation of the dispersion was reincarnated in the generation of the wilderness, those who left Egypt. Because the dispersion generation sinned by building the tower with mortar and bricks, the Egyptians enslaved Israel with mortar and bricks in crushing labor. Thus ‘All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you’ means that they themselves will be layered and planted into your holiness.
records.originHebrew: כִּי כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁיָּצְאוּ עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נוֹטְעוּ בְּזַרְעוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת סג.) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כָּל גּוֹיֵי הָאָרֶץ" – לְשׁוֹן הַבְרָכָה וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר לְטַעַם עַל הַהוֹדָעָה מִסְּדוֹם שֶׁגַּם הֵם נִתְבָּרְכוּ בוֹ וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים הֲכָנָה יְתֵירָה לְשֶׁיְּתוּקְנוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם. וְנוֹדַע דְּרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כג) עַל פָּסוּק "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי". וְגַם יָדוּעַ דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה בַּעֲבוּר אַבְרָהָם, לְכָךְ הוּא הִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקְנוּ בֶּעָתִיד. וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם" – אַב מַמָּשׁ לְכָל הַגּוֹיִם. וְהַיְינוּ כִּי ב' אֲלָפִים הוּא סִבּוּב שָׁלֵם בַּבְּרִיאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: בְּבֵי"ת נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דְּתוֹרָה קָדְמָה ב' אֲלָפִים שָׁנָה לָעוֹלָם. וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז.): ב' אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁבְּכָל חֵלֶק הָיוּ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָרְאוּיוֹת לָצֵאת: דְּתֹהוּ – עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם; וּדְתוֹרָה – בְּזַרְעוֹ עַד מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (סב.); וְיִהְיֶה פַּעַם שְׁלִישִׁית בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ הַמַּתְחִיל בִּב' אֲלָפִים הַשְּׁלִישִׁיִּים. וְהִנֵּה ג' דּוֹרוֹת שֶׁקָּדְמוּ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מָנוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְהַיְינוּ לְתוֹקֶף הָרַע שֶׁנִּתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם, וְזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה כַּאֲשֶׁר יְתוּקְנוּ הֵם גַּם כֵּן בְּתוֹקֶף גָּדוֹל. וּסְדוֹם הֵם דּוֹר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל; וְדוֹר הַפְלָגָה הֵם דּוֹר עוֹלֵי גוֹלָה גַּם כֵּן מֵאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ד.) שֶׁהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן רְאוּיִים לְנֵס כְּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה; וְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הֵם דּוֹר מָשִׁיחַ, בַּעֲלֵי בִּיאָה שְׁלִישִׁית, וּלְכָךְ מִתְגַּבֵּר עָוֹן דִּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל בְּיוֹתֵר וְג' אֵלּוּ הֵם גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד כְּלַל ג' סִדְרֵי ב' אֲלָפִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ]:
records.originEnglish: For all souls that emerged prior to our father Abraham, peace be upon him, were subsequently replanted into his seed, as our Sages expounded (Yevamot 63a) on the verse "and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed (venivrekhu)"—an expression of grafting (havrakhah) and this was stated as the rationale for informing Abraham regarding the destruction of Sodom, for they too were grafted through him and required intense preparation to be rectified, as the Ari wrote that they were the generation of the Exodus. And the rabbinic exposition (Vayikra Rabbah 23) on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation" is well known. And it is also known that the Egyptian exile occurred on account of Abraham; therefore he prayed for them, and through this they were rectified in the future. And therefore he was called "the father of a multitude of nations"—a literal father to all nations. That is, because two thousand years constitute a complete cosmic cycle in Creation, as written: with the letter Beit (equaling two) the world was created, and as I wrote elsewhere on the rabbinic dictum that the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years. And therefore our Sages said (Sanhedrin 97a): two thousand years of Desolation, two thousand of Torah, etc., wherein in each epoch all the souls destined to emerge came forth: Desolation—extending until our father Abraham, peace be upon him; and Torah—among his seed until the Messiah, until all souls in the Heavenly reservoir (Guf) are exhausted, as written in Yevamot 62a; and it will recur a third time in ultimate perfection in the generation of the Messiah, which commences in the third epoch of two thousand years. And behold, the three corrupt generations that preceded our father Abraham were enumerated in chapter Chelek as having no share in the World to Come, and that was due to the overwhelming power of evil that overpowered them; and corresponding to this, when they are rectified, it unfolds likewise with tremendous power. And Sodom corresponds to the generation of the Exodus from Egypt, as noted above; and the Generation of the Dispersion corresponds to the generation that returned from the Babylonian Exile, who also came from the land of Shinar, concerning whom our Sages stated (Berakhot 4a) that they were worthy of an overt miracle like the first entry into the Land; and the Generation of the Flood corresponds to the generation of the Messiah, the bearers of the third arrival, which is why the sin of the Generation of the Flood surges with supreme intensity and these three generations also correspond to the overarching three epochs of two thousand years mentioned above, and this is not the place to lengthen.
records.targetHebrew: "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, ג). "וְנִבְרְכוּ" הוּא מִלְּשׁוֹן הַשַּׁ"ס: "מַבְרִיכִין אֶת הָאִילָן", וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה דְּאִיתָא בְּהָאֲרִ"י הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שַׁעַר הַפְּסוּקִים פָּרָשַׁת שְׁמוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וַיָּקָם"): שֶׁדּוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה נִתְגַּלְגְּלוּ בְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם, וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁחָטְאוּ דוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה בִּבְנוֹתָם הַמִּגְדָּל בְּחֹמֶר וּלְבֵנִים, לָכֵן הֶעֱבִידוּ הַמִּצְרִים אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחֹמֶר וּבִלְבֵנִים עֲבוֹדַת פָּרֶךְ. וְזֶה הוּא "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה" – שֶׁהֵם עַצְמָם יִהְיוּ נִבְרָכִים וְנִשְׁתָּלִים בְּךָ בִּקְדֻשָּׁתְךָ.

records.themeTitle: Awe united with love and joy
records.themeSummary: Reverence need not remain the fear that opposes joy.
records.explanation: Kometz HaMinchah explicitly defines the perfection of love by its union with awe and quotes the same tradition about rejoicing through fear. This clarifies the siman's transformation: recognizing ‘You are with me’ redirects the fear toward Hashem and His greatness, allowing awe and joy to coexist. The outcome remains reverence that restrains sin, as the siman's last verse states.
records.targetEnglish: Love reaches its perfection when it is mixed with awe. As Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 3, says: ‘I rejoiced from within my fear, and feared from within my joy.’ At the beginning of Berakhot's chapter Ein Omdin (30b), it says, ‘Rejoice with trembling’ (Psalms 2:11). This is service for the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, as I explained elsewhere.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל יְדֵי "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" נִתְהַפֵּךְ לְיִרְאַת ה' וְיִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת הַמְּבִיאָה אַדְּרַבָּה לְשִׂמְחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה" (תְּהִלִּים ב, יא);
records.originEnglish: and through "for You are with me" it is transformed into the fear of Hashem and awe of His exalted majesty which leads, on the contrary, to holy joy, as written in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 3) and: "and rejoice with trembling" (Psalms 2:11);
records.targetHebrew: שלימות האהבה – כאשר מעורבת עם היראה, כמו שכתוב בתנא דבי אליהו רבה פרק ג: "אני שמחתי מתוך יראתי, ויראתי מתוך שמחתי"; ובריש פרק אין עומדין ברכות ל:: "וגילו ברעדה" תהלים ב, יא כתיב. וזה עסק לשם יחוד קודשא בריך הוא ושכינתיה, כמו שכתבתי במקום אחר.

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 52:10
records.themeTitle: Inherited deficiency and a present deliberate act
records.themeSummary: An inherited condition is distinguished from a person’s current chosen action.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov invokes the same verse about conception while distinguishing an inherited deficiency from a defiant act committed in the present. This qualification helps read the siman’s parent-and-child account as a description of transmitted conditions and shared repair, without making ancestry a substitute for judging the person’s present action.
records.targetEnglish: Therefore, although a person has sins that come from birth, as it is written (Psalms 51:7), ‘In sin my mother conceived me,’ and a person cannot clarify himself of those sins, Hashem in His abundant kindness and goodness suspends judgment concerning a person’s sin and judges him as he is now, in the present. As long as it is possible to turn the matter toward a person’s merit, that he did not act defiantly, He suspends judgment concerning his sins. Likewise, we see how many precious words of Torah come into being from this imaginary and temporal world; those words of Torah are eternal, standing at the height of the world forever.
records.originHebrew: קיב] תַּאֲוַת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁל הָאָדָם הוּא מִתֹּקֶף הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁל אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ בְּעֵת הֶרְיוֹנוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּמִּזְמוֹר כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא וְכוּלֵי: "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם וַיֵּרָא (קיב עַמּוּד א) שֶׁהַמְּקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁעַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ לָא מִסְתָּפוּ בָּנָיו מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע. וּלְכָךְ בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁזִּנְתָה – "אֶת אָבִיהָ הִיא מְחַלֶּלֶת" (וַיִּקְרָא כא, ט), וַאֲפִילּוּ הוּא בְּגַן עֵדֶן דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ עַל דָּבָר זֶה. וּלְכָךְ נִרְאָה לְיוֹסֵף דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא. וּכְשֶׁהָאָב קִבֵּל עָנְשׁוֹ וְנִתְקַן שָׁם, אָז הַבֵּן מִתְעוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה; וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבַת הַבֵּן וְתִיקּוּנוֹ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה, מַנִּיחִים לְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן. וּלְכָךְ בְּעֵת הַמִּילָה שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן הַבְּרִית וְהַתַּאֲוָה, אוֹמְרִים: "יִשְׂמַח אָבִיךָ וְאִמֶּךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כג, כה). וְזֶה בִּכְלַל "הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה", כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת:
records.originEnglish: A person's passionate lust derives from the intensity of the desire of his father and mother at the time of his conception, as King David, peace be upon him, expressed in the psalm composed when Nathan came to him: "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, etc." (Psalms 51:7), and as written in Midrash HaNe'elam (Vayeira 112a) that whoever sanctifies himself at the time of marital intimacy, his children do not fear the evil inclination. And therefore, regarding a priest's daughter who commits adultery Scripture states: "she profanes her father" (Leviticus 21:9), and even if he is in Gan Eden, he is judged for this matter. And therefore the image of his father appeared to Joseph so that he would not sin (Sotah 36b). And when the father has received his retribution and is rectified there, then the son is awakened to repentance in this world; and likewise conversely: through the son's repentance and his conquering of the impulse to sin, relief is granted to his father and mother in Gan Eden. And therefore at the circumcision ceremony, which is the rectification of the Covenant and passion, we recite: "Let your father and your mother be glad, etc." (Proverbs 23:25). And this falls under "a father endows his son with wisdom" (Eduyot 2:9), for a person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters him (Sotah 3a).
records.targetHebrew: וּלְזֶה, אַף שֶׁנִּמְצָא חֲטָאִים בָּאָדָם שֶׁהֵם מֵהַתּוֹלָדָה, וְכִדְכְתִיב (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז): "וּבְחֵטְא יֶחֱמַתְנִי אִמִּי", וּמֵאוֹתָן הַחֲטָאִים לֹא יוּכַל אָדָם לְבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ; אָכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב חַסְדּוֹ וְטוּבוֹ תּוֹלֶה עַל חֵטְא הָאָדָם וְדָן אוֹתוֹ בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא שָׁם בַּהֹוֶה, שֶׁכָּל עוֹד שֶׁיּוּכַל לַהֲפוֹךְ בִּזְכוּת הָאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה פְּעֻלָּה בִּשְׁאָט נֶפֶשׁ, תּוֹלֶה לוֹ עַל חֲטָאָיו. וְכֵן אָנוּ רוֹאִים שֶׁכַּמָּה וְכַמָּה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יְקָרִים מִתְהַוִּים מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדִּמְיוֹנִי וְהַזְּמַנִּי, וְהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָאֵלֶּה הֵמָּה נִצְחִיִּים, עוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם לָעַד וּלְעוֹלָם.

records.themeTitle: When wisdom supplies power to a wrong direction
records.themeSummary: The initial purity of wisdom does not prevent its misuse by the heart and body.
records.explanation: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet explains why Torah’s power does not guarantee a good immediate result. Wisdom can give the heart and body greater power to pursue a wrong direction; falsehood itself can become persuasive through the truth it initially borrows. This clarifies the siman’s warning that a learner’s unresolved captivity can draw other souls downward, even though eventual repair remains possible.
records.targetEnglish: Nevertheless, the body’s and heart’s power to sin comes through the wisdom within them. As it says (Hosea 14:10), ‘Transgressors stumble through them,’ and the Sages said (Shabbat 88b) that for those who turn it to the left, it becomes a potion of death. Through wisdom itself a person stumbles and dies, for without it the body could not sin so greatly. One cannot speak falsehood unless one says something true at the beginning. That is, something wholly imaginary is nothing, just as an animal has no sin because it has no wisdom and is entirely imagination. What is wholly imagination has no place for sin; only someone who first has a foundation of truth can afterward say something false. This is clear to one who understands.
records.originHebrew: וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא עב:): לֹא זָכָה – נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת וּמַכְנִיסָם גַּם כֵּן בְּעֹמֶק רַע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן. אַף דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לַסּוֹף כְּשֶׁיְּתַקֵּן הוּא מַרְוִיחַ, דְּעוֹלֶה וְעוֹלִים עִמּוֹ; אַךְ לְפִי שָׁעָה נֶאֱמַר עַל זֶה: "וּפֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י) דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָרַע מִתְגַּבֵּר.
records.originEnglish: and likewise they said (Yoma 72b): if he did not merit, it becomes a deadly potion to him, such that through his words of Torah he gathers souls and drags them likewise into the depth of evil, may the Merciful One preserve us. Even though ultimately when he rectifies he gains, for he ascends and they ascend with him; yet for the immediate present it is proclaimed: "and transgressors shall stumble in them" (Hosea 14:10), whereby through this evil is temporarily intensified.
records.targetHebrew: כי מכל מקום כח הגוף והלב לחטא הוא על ידי החכמה שבו, וכמו שנאמר (במשלי [הושע י״ד:י׳]): "ופשעים יכשלו בם", ואמרו זכרונם לברכה (שבת פ״ח עמוד ב׳): למשמאילים בה — סמא דמותא; שבחכמה עצמה ועל ידה הוא נכשל ומת, כי לולי הוא לא היה הגוף חוטא כל כך, שאי אפשר לומר שקר אלא אם כן אומר דבר אמת בתחלתו. פרוש: שדבר שכלו דמיון אינו כלום, וכמו שאין חטא לבהמה כי אין בה חכמה והיא כלה רק דמיון, ומה שהוא רק דמיון גמור אין מקום לחטא, רק מי שיש לו יסודא דקשוט בקדמיתא אחר כך יכול לומר דבר שקר; ודבר ברור הוא למבין.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, Shabbat Chol HaMoed Sukkot 19:1
records.themeTitle: A teaching held as private property or returned to its source
records.themeSummary: Momentary possessiveness calls for a return to being a conduit for Torah.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim describes a subtler form of attachment to one’s teaching: forgetting for a moment that one is a conduit and therefore wanting to defend one’s own words. It also describes the teaching returning rather than remaining trapped in that private claim. This is a qualified comparison with Rav Tzadok’s distinction: a passing lapse during transmission is not identified with deliberately deriving an argument from envy or personal interest, but it too requires the teacher to relinquish ownership of the truth.
records.targetEnglish: Concerning words of Torah, however, the Midrash concludes: lest you say that after a person gives his learning to another it no longer returns to him, Scripture says, ‘There they return to go.’ At the completion of every transmission there must be a little forgetting in the giver. This forgetting is the completion through which a new birth occurs, for every birth must first have forgetting before the birth can come from it. So too in transmitting Torah, when it moves from thought into speech, a person cannot always maintain a clearly illuminated awareness that he is only a conduit. Because he then forgets that he is only a conduit, he acquires a personal interest and wants to maintain his own statement, as the Talmud says, a person is inclined to maintain his statement. Thus the Midrash says: after a person gives his learning to another, when a little forgetting at the completion of transmission is unavoidable, lest you think those words of Torah are lost from him and remain in the isolated detail, Scripture says, ‘There they return to go.’ Since a person cannot avoid that little forgetting at the completion, they return to him; they do not, Heaven forbid, remain in the isolated detail.
records.originHebrew: [קטו] כְּשֶׁמְּחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר בַּתּוֹרָה, צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מִצַּד שׁוּם נְגִיעָה בַּלֵּב שֶׁרוֹצֶה כָּךְ, אוֹ לְהִתְפָּאֲרוּת, אוֹ לַחְלוֹק עַל דִּבְרֵי זוּלָתוֹ וְכַיּוֹצֵא, רַק מִצַּד הַתְּשׁוּקָה לֵידַע הָאֱמֶת, וְאָז אֲפִילּוּ טוֹעֶה נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, שֶׁהֲרֵי נִזְכַּר בַּתַּלְמוּד דִּבְרֵי הַטּוֹעִים וְשֶׁנִּדְחוּ מֵהֲלָכָה, שֶׁגַּם הַהֲוָא אָמֵינָא הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁכָּךְ יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: מוּשְׂכָּל רִאשׁוֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַגָּעָה לָאֱמֶת, וְגַם הַמּוּשְׂכָּל רִאשׁוֹן הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.
records.originEnglish: When a person innovates an insight in the Torah, it must not stem from any personal bias in the heart that desires it to be so, nor for self-aggrandizement, nor to dispute the words of another, or the like; but solely from the pure yearning to know the Truth. And then, even if he errs, it is termed words of Torah and the words of the living God, for behold, the Talmud explicitly records the words of those who erred and opinions that were rejected from practical halakhah, showing that even the initial hypothesis (hava amina) is words of Torah; for thus the Blessed Name established the process: first an initial conception, and only subsequently arriving at the truth; and that initial conception is likewise from the Blessed Name and constitutes the words of the living God.
records.targetHebrew: אבל על דברי תורה מסיק שם במדרש שמא תאמר מאחר שאדם מוציא תלמודו לאחר שוב אינה חוזרת עליו ת"ל שם הם שבים ללכת. היינו כי בהגמר מכל ההשפעות מוכרח שיהיה להמשפיע מעט שכחה. וזה השכחה הוא הגמר שנתהווה ממנה הולדה כי בכל הולדה מוכרח להיות מקודם שכחה ואח"כ יתכן שיהיה מזה הולדה וככה הוא בהשפעת דברי תורה בהגמר היינו כשיוצאת מכח המחשבה אל הדבור אז א"א שיהיה להאדם תמיד חשבון מבורר בבהירות שהוא אינו רק צינור. וזהו יען ששוכח אז שהוא רק צינור לזה נעשה נוגע בדבר וחפץ להחזיק דיבורו כמאמרם ז"ל בגמרא אדם עשוי להחזיק דיבורו לזה איתא כאן במדרש מאחר שאדם מוציא תלמודו לאחר ואז א"א שלא ישכח מעט בגמר ההשפעה שהוא רק צינור שמא תאמר שוב אינה חוזרת עליו היינו שנאבדו אותן הדברי תורה ח"ו מאתו ונשארת בהפרט לזה נאמר שם הם שבים ללכת היינו מאחר שא"א שלא יהיה להאדם בהגמר מעט שכחה לכן הם חוזרים עליו ולא יהיו נשארים ח"ו בהפרט אלא שם הם שבים ללכת:

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 6
records.themeTitle: Returning the lost understanding to the heart
records.themeSummary: Correction after a stumbling can give Torah a stronger inward hold.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach explains what is gained through the return after a stumbling: Torah enters the heart with greater desire than before. The interpretation of ‘I will return you’ as both returning a lost thing and teshuvah gives a concrete image for the siman’s raising of the stumbling through the later discovery of truth. The direction is toward correction, rather than seeking an error for its own sake.
records.targetEnglish: ‘The land upon which you lie, I will give to you.’ This blessing means that even while lying down and sleeping your thoughts will be clear and pure. ‘All the families shall be blessed through you’ means that all the nations will praise you for your Torah, as it says (Deuteronomy 4:6), ‘For it is your wisdom and understanding.’ ‘Behold, Anokhi is with you’: it does not say Ani, because the letter kaf points to the inexhaustible source of life, as the Sefer Yetzirah teaches (chapter 4, mishnah 1, according to the Ari’s text). Hashem then showed him the clarifications through which he would still have to be clarified and suffer. Concerning this He promised, ‘I will guard you wherever you go and return you to this ground.’ ‘Return you’ is an expression of returning a lost thing: a person does not stand upon words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them (Gittin 43a). Through the stumbling that comes to a person, words of Torah enter his heart with greater desire than before. Thus ‘I will return you’ is an expression of teshuvah.
records.originHebrew: רַק הוּא כְּדֵי לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל. וְאָז דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "מַכְשֵׁלָה" – נוּקְבָא לְגַבֵּי "מִכְשׁוֹל" דְּכַר, וּמְקַבֶּלֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הָעֲשׁוּקָה הַהוּא שֶׁהוּא הַמִּכְשׁוֹל, וּמוֹצִיאָתוֹ לָאוֹר וְלִקְדוּשָׁה, שֶׁגַּם בָּהּ נֶאֱרַע מַכְשֵׁלָה וְהַעֲמָדָה עַל הָאֱמֶת אַחַר כָּךְ דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶעֱלָה הַמִּכְשׁוֹל.
records.originEnglish: but rather it occurs so that one subsequently masters words of Torah to extract the precious from the vile. And then words of Torah are called a makhshelah (feminine noun) relative to the masculine mikhshol, receiving that oppressed captive soul which was the stumbling block and delivering it into light and holiness, for in the Torah study there likewise occurred an initial stumbling and an arrival at the truth specifically through it—since a person does not master Torah in any other way—and through this he elevates the stumbling block.
records.targetHebrew: הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה שֹׁכֵב עָלֶיהָ לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה. עִנְיַן הַבְּרָכָה הַזֹּאת הִיא שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַשְּׁכִיבָה וְהַשֵּׁינָה יִהְיוּ רַעְיוֹנוֹתֶיךָ בְּרוּרִים וּנְקִיִּים. "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כָּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת" וְכוּלֵי, הַיְינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁלְּךָ יְפָאֲרוּךָ כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים דָּלֶת, וָאו) "כִּי הִיא חָכְמַתְכֶם וּבִינַתְכֶם". "וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ", וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר "אֲנִי" כִּי אוֹת הַכָּ"ף מוֹרָה עַל מְקוֹר הַחַיִּים בְּלִי דַּי כִּדְאִיתָא בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה [פֶּרֶק דָּלֶת מִשְׁנָה אָלֶף לְגִירְסַת הָאֲרִיזַ"ל], וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָז הַבֵּירוּרִין שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ עוֹד לְהִתְבָּרֵר וְלִסְבּוֹל, וְעַל זֶה הִבְטִיחַ לוֹ "וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלֵךְ וַהֲשִׁיבוֹתִיךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה הַזֹּאת", וַהֲשִׁיבוֹתִיךָ הוּא לְשׁוֹן הֲשָׁבַת אֲבֵידָה, כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל בָּהֶם (גִּיטִּין מֵם גִּימֶל עַמּוּד אָלֶף), וְהַיְינוּ כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַמִּכְשׁוֹל שֶׁבָּא לָאָדָם יִכָּנְסוּ הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם בְּחֵשֶׁק גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר מִמִּקֹּדֶם, וְזֶהוּ "וַהֲשִׁיבוֹתִיךָ" הַיְינוּ לְשׁוֹן תְּשׁוּבָה.

records.themeTitle: The narrative that prepares a soul and opens the heart
records.themeSummary: Eliezer’s conversation carries the work of bringing the future Torah soul into the world.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik explains why Eliezer’s ordinary account can be treated as Torah with power to draw forth a soul. His mission prepares the birth of Yaakov, the attribute of Torah, by taking Rivkah from the surrounding forces of Lavan and Betuel. Reading that narrative is then connected with the learner’s own heart opening to Torah. This develops the siman’s transition from a story to the repair and birth of souls.
records.targetEnglish: Afterward the holy Zohar (132a) says: come and see how many hidden supernal secrets there are in Torah. When David looked and knew how many wonders issue from Torah, he began, ‘Uncover my eyes, that I may behold wonders from Your Torah.’ The Zohar gives this introduction to Eliezer’s mission to bring Rivkah because it prepared the birth of Yaakov’s soul, the attribute of Torah. The principal wonder—‘wonders from Your Torah’—is that through this we merit ‘He will open our heart in His Torah.’ It says that this passage contains supernal secrets, as the Midrash says (Bereishit Rabbah 60:8), ‘The conversation of the servants of the patriarchal households is more beautiful than the Torah of their children.’ Certainly no letter in Torah is superfluous, Heaven forbid. Rather, in this passage of Eliezer’s conversation are secrets and many hidden treasures, to bring Yaakov’s soul out from the forces of Lavan and Betuel; through these words of Torah we merit the opening of the heart to Torah.
records.originHebrew: כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס): יָפָה שִׂיחָתָן שֶׁל עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת מִתּוֹרָתָן שֶׁל בָּנִים [וְלֹא הָיְתָה מַעֲלַת אֱלִיעֶזֶר רַק מַעֲלַת אַבְרָהָם, לְכָךְ קְרָאוֹ עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא כח:): דַּמֶּשֶׂק – דּוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה מִתּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ, כִּי מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עֶבֶד קָנָה רַבּוֹ, וְכָל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ הַכֹּל נִקְרָא תּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ].
records.originEnglish: as written in Bereishit Rabbah 60:8: "More beautiful is the casual speech of the servants of the Patriarchs than the Torah of their children" and this was not Eliezer's independent virtue but Abraham's, which is why they were termed 'servants of the Patriarchs,' and in Yoma 28b: Dammasek—he draws and gives drink from the Torah of his master, for what a servant acquires his master acquires, and all Torah he possessed was termed his master's Torah.
records.targetHebrew: וְאַחַר כָּךְ (קלב עַמּוּד א) אָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "תָּא חֲזֵי, בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא כַּמָּה רָזִין עִלָּאִין סְתִימִין אִית בַּהּ וְכוּלֵי, וְעַל דָּא כַּד אִסְתַּכַּל דָּוִד וְיָדַע כַּמָּה פִּלְאָן נָפְקִין מֵאוֹרַיְיתָא, פָּתַח וְאָמַר: גַּל עֵינַי וְאַבִּיטָה נִפְלָאוֹת מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ וְאָמַר הַזֹּהַר פְּתִיחָה זוֹ לִשְׁלִיחוּת אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְהָבִיא אֶת רִבְקָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָז הָיָה הַהֲכָנָה לְלֵידַת נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב (שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַתּוֹרָה), וְעִיקַּר הַפִּלְאָן – "נִפְלָאוֹת מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ" – הוּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְ"וְהוּא יִפְתַּח לִבֵּנוּ בְּתוֹרָתוֹ וְאָמַר שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ יֵשׁ סוֹדוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים, וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס, ח): "יָפָה שִׂיחָתָן שֶׁל עַבְדֵי בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת מִתּוֹרָתָן שֶׁל בָּנִים וּבוַדַּאי אֵין אוֹת מְיוּתֶּרֶת בַּתּוֹרָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, רַק שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ דְּשִׂיחַת אֱלִיעֶזֶר יֵשׁ סוֹדוֹת וְכַמָּה גְּנִיזִין טְמִירִין בָּהּ (לְהוֹצִיא נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב מִבֵּין הַקְּלִיפּוֹת דְּלָבָן וּבְתוּאֵל), שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָאֵלּוּ זוֹכִין לִפְתּוֹחַ הַלֵּב בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה

records.targetRef: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:21
records.themeTitle: Approach that makes restraint possible
records.themeSummary: Drawing near and holding back can cooperate in directing the inclination.
records.explanation: Dover Tzedek interprets the two hands as a coordinated response rather than competing alternatives: the right draws near so that the left can effectively restrain. Its image of a little leaven being beneficial helps explain why Rav Tzadok distinguishes complete subduing from transformation and relates the appropriate response to the person’s level. The source does not dispense with the need for restraint.
records.targetEnglish: Concerning this they said (Sotah 47a): with the inclination and the other cases, let the left hand push away and the right hand draw near. One may explain that the right draws near so that the left will push away; this is ‘very good.’ I heard that the Sages compared the inclination to leaven in the dough (Berakhot 17a), and leaven improves the dough. It is taught (Berakhot 34a) concerning leaven that a little of it is beneficial.
records.originHebrew: וְאָמְרוּ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ שָׁם דְּגַם הַיֵּצֶר כֵּן יִהְיֶה: שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֶּאֱלִישָׁע הָיָה גַּם יָמִין דּוֹחָה. וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע, יָדוּעַ דְּהַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם, וְיֵשׁ מִדָּתוֹ לְאַכְפַּיָּא וְלִהְיוֹת דּוֹחֶה לְגַמְרֵי, וְיֵשׁ מִדָּתוֹ לְאַהְפָּכָא:
records.originEnglish: And immediately afterward they said there that with the inclination it should be likewise: the left pushes away and the right draws close, whereas with Elisha the right pushed away as well. And even though they said in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination," it is known that all depends on each person's unique spiritual path: there is one whose task is to suppress (le-akpaya) and reject completely, and there is one whose task is to transform (le-ahpakha).

records.themeTitle: Derekh eretz and the Torah point already in the person
records.themeSummary: Ordinary decent conduct can disclose a Torah inheritance before formal learning is visible.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim explains why derekh eretz can stand before Torah without being detached from it. In the story of Rabbi Yannai, the guest's conduct expresses a Torah point he cannot yet identify through formal learning. The scholar is challenged to recognize it. This develops the siman's image of a path toward the tree of life: preparation can already carry the inward relation to what it prepares one to receive.
records.targetEnglish: Since Torah was apportioned to the whole congregation of Yaakov, even the lowest soul, a true Torah scholar must recognize from the garment of derekh eretz he sees in an unlearned person the precious depth of the Torah point within him. This is why the man seized Rabbi Yannai and said, ‘My inheritance is with you’: it is not written ‘the congregation of Yannai,’ but ‘the congregation of Yaakov.’ Hashem apportioned Torah to all the souls of Israel, so that even the lowest soul of Israel is not completely devoid of Torah, Heaven forbid. In the Torah point within each one, he is distinguished and elevated above all Israel. Thus the man seized Rabbi Yannai and said, ‘My inheritance is with you.’ That is: although I myself do not recognize the words of Torah in the depth of my heart because I am unlearned, you, Rabbi Yannai, are a Torah scholar. You should have discerned from my derekh eretz the precious Torah point within me from which all that conduct branches. These true words awakened Rabbi Yannai; he immediately acknowledged them, regretted his act, and said, ‘You have all this derekh eretz, and I called you a dog.’
records.originHebrew: וְהִנֵּה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ קָדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה, וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק א נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ "דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים" עַיֵּין שָׁם וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "פְּרִי צַדִּיק" דַּיְיקָא "עֵץ חַיִּים", וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ אֶל הַתּוֹרָה]:
records.originEnglish: And behold, derekh eretz preceded the Torah, and in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 1) derekh eretz is called "the way to the Tree of Life," see there and therefore the fruit of the righteous specifically is titled a 'tree of life', and one who lacks derekh eretz cannot attain the Torah.
records.targetHebrew: כיון שנתחלק הד"ת לכל קהלת יעקב אפילו להנפש הנמוך ביותר לכן מי שהוא באמת ת"ח צריך שפיר להכיר מגוון הלבוש של הדרך ארץ שרואה אצל עם הארץ את עומק היקרות מהנקודה של ד"ת הנמצא בו וזה הוא שתפסיה ואמר לו ירותתי גבך וכו' קהלת ינאי לא כתיב כאן אלא קהלת יעקב וכו' היינו שחילק השי"ת את הד"ת לכל נפשות ישראל עד שאינו בנמצא כלל אפילו בהנפש היותר נמוך מישראל שיהיה משולל לגמרי ח"ו מדברי תורה ובזאת הנקודה מד"ת הנמצא גבי כל אחד ואחד הוא באמת מדוגל ומנושא בה יותר מכל ישראל לזה תפסיה לר' ינאי ואמר לו ירותתי גבך כלומר אף שאני בעצמי אינו מכיר הדברי תורה הנמצא בעומק לבי מפני שאני עם הארץ. אבל אתה ר' ינאי הלא תלמיד חכם אתה היה לך להבחין ולהוכיח מהדרך ארץ שיש בי את היקרות מהנקודה של ד"ת הנמצא בי שממנה נסתעף אצלי כל אותו הדרך ארץ ומאלו הדברים האמיתיים נתעורר ר' ינאי והודה מיד לדבריו והתחרט ואמר כל הדא דרך ארץ גבך וקריתך כלבא וכו':

records.themeTitle: Atonement while the matter is not yet fully known
records.themeSummary: Protection before knowledge is distinguished from the later work of clarification.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim gives a conceptual account of the uncertainty that Rav Tzadok mentions through the asham talui. Some actions can still be clarified through human service; other matters remain beyond a person's present understanding. The scapegoat waits while the first kind of work is still possible. This clarifies why lack of knowledge need not mean abandonment of repair, while keeping this explanation distinct from the siman's particular inference about one atonement drawing others with it.
records.targetEnglish: This was the meaning of the scapegoat, which the Zohar describes as a collective asham talui. An asham talui comes for what is not known, to protect the person from suffering until he knows and brings a sin offering. Likewise, acts that can be clarified only from Hashem's side, because their repair is wholly outside human understanding, require an asham talui; this was the scapegoat. It therefore had to remain alive until the blood of its fellow was applied. As long as it was possible to clarify from it actions that could be included in the goat whose lot was for Hashem, transforming deliberate sins into merits, they did not send it away. They delayed sending it into the wilderness until no more could be gathered from it and turned into merits through service. Then they sent it to Azazel, into the wilderness.
records.originHebrew: וְשָׁם אִיתָא בְּלֹא יוֹדֵעַ דְּחַיָּיב אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בְּחַטָּאת עַל זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (פֶּרֶק ל), וְנִזְכַּר הָעִנְיָן גַּם כֵּן בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת, כִּי הֶחְמִירָה תּוֹרָה בְּסָפֵק דְּאָשָׁם תָּלוּי חָמִיר מֵחַטָּאת, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה הַטַּעַם: כִּי הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁנּוֹדַע לוֹ מְכַפֶּרֶת מִקְצָת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא מִתְחָרֵט, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכֵי בִּגְרִירָה נִתְכַּפְּרָה, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְכָל כַּפָּרַת חֲטָאִים בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
records.originEnglish: And there it is stated that if he does not know, he is liable for a provisional guilt-offering (asham talui), meaning he cannot attain atonement through a sin-offering, as in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 30); and this concept is also cited by Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah in the first chapter of Berakhot, for the Torah was more stringent regarding doubt—an asham talui being more demanding than a chatat—the reason being that the definite knowledge of the sin provides partial atonement because through it he experiences genuine remorse, see there. And even so, through the principle of dragging (grirah) it is atoned, and the same applies to all atonement of sins through repentance.

records.themeTitle: Torah labor as a purification that gives life
records.themeSummary: The tent and water images describe effort in Torah leading from impurity to purity.
records.explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim places the figurative dying in Torah within an expressly life-giving sequence. Personal effort in Torah is described as the dew that revives and the water that purifies. This supplies the positive mechanism of the siman’s image: the exertion of study becomes the path to renewed life and purity.
records.targetEnglish: Afterward comes the portion of Parah, to purify the impure through an awakening of holiness from the person's own side and effort. Through this, the impurity of death is purified by the dew of Torah that gives him life (Ketubot 111b), through his “putting himself to death” over words of Torah. For it is written, ‘A person who dies in a tent’ (Numbers 19:14; Berakhot 63b; Shabbat 83b), and Scripture compares tents to streams (Numbers 24:6; Berakhot 16a), which likewise raise a person from impurity to purity.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן מִיתָה כִּדְרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת סג:) עַל פָּסוּק "אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל", וְאָז נִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמַת מִיתָה וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (תָּמִיד לב.): מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִחְיֶה? יָמִית עַצְמוֹ].
records.originEnglish: And through words of Torah, wherein a person slays himself over words of Torah—which is likewise termed death, as our Sages expounded (Berakhot 63b) on the verse "when a man dies in a tent" (Numbers 19:14)— he is thereby atoned through this form of spiritual death and therefore they stated in Tamid 32a: "What shall a man do to live? Let him slay himself".
records.targetHebrew: ואחר כך פרשת פרה: לטהר טמאים בהתעוררות קדושה שמצד עצמו ובהשתדלותו שבזה הוא טהרת טומאת מת על ידי טל תורה המחייהו (כתובות קי״א עמוד ב׳) על ידי מה שממית עצמו על דברי תורה, ד״אדם כי ימות באהל״ (במדבר י״ט:י״ד) כתיב (ברכות ס״ג עמוד ב׳; שבת פ״ג עמוד ב׳) ומקיש ״אהלים״ ל״נחלים״ (במדבר כ״ד:ו׳; ברכות ט״ז עמוד א׳), דגם הם מעלין האדם מטומאה לטהרה.

records.themeTitle: A mitzvah sanctifies the faculty through which it is performed
records.themeSummary: Repair concerns the inward quality of the same power, rather than multiplying acts mechanically.
records.explanation: Et HaOchel states the general principle behind the siman's inference: a mitzvah adds holiness especially to the organ and power through which it is performed. Its use of the same bundles-of-mitzvot teaching explains how the corresponding positive act can repair a damaged faculty. Rav Tzadok's explicit qualification here remains decisive: the proposed increase is in holiness and quality, within human ability.
records.targetEnglish: The mitzvah of eating matzah gives holiness to eating. Every mitzvah, particularly one over which we bless ‘Who sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us,’ adds holiness to a person, especially to the organ and power through which it is performed. As the Sages said in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5): ‘If you have made bundles of transgressions, make corresponding bundles of mitzvot,’ continuing with the example of the hands and the other faculties.
records.originHebrew: כִּי כָּל לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה – הָעֲשֵׂה הוּא תִּיקּוּן הַלָּאו. וְגַם בְּלָאו הָכִי אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כא): כִּי בָּאֵבֶר שֶׁעָשָׂה בּוֹ חֲבִילוֹת עֲבֵירוֹת – יַעֲשֶׂה בּוֹ חֲבִילוֹת שֶׁל מִצְווֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם; וְכֵן כָּאן, בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר חֲבִילוֹת מִצְווֹת הַיְינוּ פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וּמִצְוַת עוֹנָה [וּמִיהוּ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר נַמֵּי "יָשַׁב וְלֹא עָבַר עֲבֵירָה" כִּדְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפָּא שֶׁנִּזְדַּמְּנָה לְיָדוֹ, מִקְרֵי גַּם כֵּן מִצְוָה כִּדְאִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (לט:)]. וְאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר חֲבִילוֹת בְּרִבּוּי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, דְּעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.): שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מְצוּיִין וְכוּלֵי, וְאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת: "אַל תַּרְבֶּה שִׂיחָה" כַּנּוֹדָע; רַק אֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּכַמּוּת אֶלָּא בְּאֵיכוּת, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה, דִּבְלָאו הָכִי מִקְרֵי בְּעִילַת זְנוּת וּכִבְהֵמוֹת כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים. רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בִּקְדוּשָׁה כְּפִי אֶפְשָׁרוּת הָאָדָם [דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא, וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "בֶּעָווֹן מָלֵא" – דַּאֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ)],
records.originEnglish: for in every negative prohibition derived implicitly from a positive commandment, the positive performance serves as the rectification of the prohibition. And even without this, they stated in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5): with the very limb wherewith one performed bundles of transgressions, let him perform bundles of mitzvot, see there; and so here, with that same physical organ the "bundles of mitzvot" are procreation and marital intimacy though one may also say that passive restraint—"he sat and did not commit a sin" when an opportunity presented itself, like Rav Chanina bar Pappa—is likewise credited as a mitzvah, as brought in Kiddushin 39b. And "bundles" does not mean excessive physical frequency, for regarding this they taught in Berakhot 22a: so that Torah scholars should not be constantly engaged in marital intimacy like roosters, and in Avot: "Do not converse excessively with a woman," as is known; rather "bundles" refers not to quantity but to spiritual quality: that it be conducted in profound holiness and purity, for otherwise it is considered an act of licentiousness and animalistic behavior, as stated repeatedly in the Zohar. Only when it is carried out in holiness according to human capacity for the Holy One does not act tyrannically, and our Sages noted: "in total iniquity"—meaning even the most pious of the pious cannot entirely avoid some subtle base element (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria 14:5),
records.targetHebrew: מצות אכילת מצה נותנת קדושה באכילות, כי כל מצוה, בפרט אותה שמברכין עליה "אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו", מוספת קדושה באדם, וביחוד באותו אבר וכח שעל ידו נעשית, כמו שאמרו זכרונם לברכה בויקרא רבה [פרשה כ״א:ה׳]: "עשית חבילות עברות — עשה נגדן חבילות מצות... ידים וכולי"

records.themeTitle: An occasional revelation and an enduring dwelling
records.themeSummary: Recognition of Hashem before oneself concerns a changed readiness, not merely an isolated experience.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik asks why circumcision is said to make revelation possible when Avraham had already received revelations before it. Its answer distinguishes an appearance for a particular prophetic message from the body becoming an enduring dwelling for the Shekhinah. This develops the siman's own definition of seeing as recognizing Hashem before oneself, read with its requirement of a lasting return.
records.targetEnglish: The principal difference appears to be that the earlier revelation was for speech; this does not require circumcision, and there were prophets among the nations as well. Here it says ‘He appeared’ without recording any speech afterward to explain its purpose. The Sages therefore explained it as visiting the sick. But the plain meaning appears to be that, until then, revelation had occurred only for a prophetic message, occasionally, when Avraham prepared himself. Now he had become whole, his body always ready for it. ‘He appeared to him’ means that He now appeared to be with him continually. Thus, at the last speech before circumcision at the end of Lech Lecha, it says, ‘He finished speaking with him, and God ascended from Avraham’ (Genesis 17:22). This is a model for all the earlier speeches: the revelation was only during the speech and departed immediately afterward. Scripture states it here to explain the difference between seeing before circumcision and seeing afterward. The latter was not for a speech or another particular purpose and did not depart at all, for his body had already been sanctified to be a dwelling for the Shekhinah in his heart continually, as with Israel. Concerning ‘My heart is awake,’ Shir HaShirim Rabbah asks: from where is it known that the Holy One is the heart of Israel? From ‘The Rock of my heart.’
records.originHebrew: רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁרוֹאֶה וּמַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִכְחוֹ, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה נִקְרָא אֵצֶל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם "רוּחַ קָדְשְׁךָ" וּ"שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ"; כִּי אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא עַל פָּסוּק "מִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ" (אִיּוֹב יט, כו), דִּלִשְׁמִירַת בְּרִית בָּשָׂר תֵּיכֶף מַגִּיעַ מַחֲזֶה: "וַיֵּרָא וְגוֹמֵר". וְהִנֵּה בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר חַיֵּי שָׂרָה (קכט סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דִּבְשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא זוֹכֶה לְכָל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת וְשָׁמַעְתִּי בְּשֵׁם הָרַב הַמַּגִּיד מִמֶּזְרִיטְשׁ זַ"ל כִּי דָּבָר זֶה מִיגִיעַת רַשְׁבִּ"י עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם], וְדָבָר זֶה עִיקָּרוֹ עַל בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה מֵעָוֹן קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית כִּדְאִיתָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז.) עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדְּיָא; וּבְלָאו הָכִי סְתָם תְּשׁוּבָה בְּעָוֹן זֶה כִּדְמַשְׁמָע בְּפֶרֶק יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים (יוֹמָא פו:): הֵיכִי דָּמֵי בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה? מַחֲוֵי וְכוּלֵי בְּאוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה. וּכְשֶׁמְּתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה הָרְאוּיָה [שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם לֹא יַחֲזוֹר לְדָבָר זֶה אֲפִילּוּ יַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו מָה, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּעִיד עָלָיו יוֹצֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית עַל כָּךְ כִּלְשׁוֹן הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהִגִּיעַ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ לְכָךְ], אָז תֵּיכֶף מַגִּיעַ לוֹ הָרְאִיָּה הָרְאוּיָה לְשׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
records.originEnglish: meaning that he perceives and recognizes that the Blessed Name is directly before him, which King David, peace be upon him, titled "Your holy spirit" and "the joy of Your salvation"; for they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Vayeira) on the verse "from my flesh shall I see God" (Job 19:26), that for guarding the covenant of the flesh there immediately follows divine vision: "And Hashem appeared unto him, etc." (Genesis 18:1). And behold, regarding a penitent (ba'al teshuvah), the Zohar states (Chayei Sarah 129a end) that in one hour, in a single instant, he merits to ascend to all spiritual rungs and I heard in the name of the Maggid of Mezritch that this achievement was unlocked through the spiritual toil of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, and this concept applies primarily to a penitent repenting from the sin of blemishing the Covenant, as brought in Avodah Zarah 17a concerning Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya; and even generally, standard repentance is framed around this sin, as implied in Yoma 86b: "Who is a true penitent? One to whom the same woman presents herself in the same situation, etc." And when one rectifies through proper repentance which means that he will never return to this act no matter what befalls him, such that the Creator of the universe can testify concerning him as formulated by Maimonides in Hilkhot Teshuvah, then there immediately reaches him the divine vision appropriate to the guardian of the Covenant as noted above

records.themeTitle: Knowing Hashem after a failure
records.themeSummary: The availability of teshuvah preserves responsibility and prevents despair.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef gives an explicit reading of the same rabbinic phrase, ‘even in a matter of transgression’: a person must not despair after stumbling, because return remains open. It is a useful qualification beside the siman's insistence that a higher purpose does not remove the need for repair. The possibility of continuing mitzvot before complete purification supplies a route back, rather than a justification for repeating the failure.
records.targetEnglish: So the holy Zohar says (Shemini 35b): when the Holy One wished to create the world, Torah said before Him, ‘This person whom You are about to create is destined to sin before You.’ The Holy One replied, ‘Was I called long-suffering for nothing?’ The Midrash (Devarim Rabbah, Vaetchanan 2) compares prayer to a mikveh and repentance to the sea. A mikveh is sometimes open and sometimes closed; so too prayer is sometimes open and sometimes closed. Repentance is like the sea: just as the sea is always open, the Holy One's hand is always open to receive those who return. All this teaches that even if a person, Heaven forbid, has stumbled in a bad act, repentance is not withheld from him. This is the meaning of ‘Know Him in all your ways,’ upon which the substance of Torah depends. As Rava concludes, ‘Even in a matter of transgression’: the person should not despair after stumbling in sin, because repentance is always available. This is the general principle of the substance of Torah.

records.themeTitle: Why joy surrounds the broken sound
records.themeSummary: Confidence in acceptance accompanies the bitterness of repentance.
records.explanation: Resisei Layla explains why the broken cry is surrounded by notes of joy: they awaken the Father's kindness and compassion toward His children. The comparison develops the siman's instruction to hold both confidence and inward bitterness together. Joy here concerns the relation that makes return possible, while the broken sound still gives expression to the work of repentance.
records.targetEnglish: Therefore two sounds were required, before it and after it, in a blast of joy: to awaken Hashem's joy toward His children through His attributes of kindness and compassion, to hear the voice of their Torah of kindness and the voice of prayer, which is mercy. Through these they are called His children. It is part of the nature of creation that a father has compassion on his son and accepts his return.

records.themeTitle: A new heart and humility toward the convert
records.themeSummary: An unseen root is not a basis for denying Hashem’s power to create anew.
records.explanation: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik applies the same new-heart principle to Hillel's receiving converts. Humility measures one's own deficiency against Hashem's greatness and leaves no basis for contempt toward the person arriving from outside. This gives a practical consequence to the siman's warning that the root is hidden from every creature: the human task remains welcome, prayer, repentance and good deeds, rather than a verdict about an allegedly fixed inner nature.
records.targetEnglish: This is the convert's claim in Shabbat's chapter Bameh Madlikin (31a), and Shammai's strictness in distancing him. Shammai is the level of awe, from which come strength and strictness, the level of Yitzchak, with whom Israel begins as explained above; therefore he distanced the converts there. From the side of awe, its complete attainment is the opposite of that request, as explained above. Hillel's humility brought them near, like Moshe, who was exceedingly humble (Numbers 12:3) and therefore brought near the mixed multitude and argued concerning Michah, as explained above. Avraham too was humble, as Berakhot 6b teaches that the humble person is Avraham's disciple; therefore he is the father of converts, as taught in Bikkurim 1:4. Humility is measuring one's deficiency against Hashem's greatness, leaving no place for superiority over the convert who comes with his staff and bag. The One who said [that oil should burn] can say that vinegar should burn as well (Taanit 25a), and can place light in vinegar too, like ‘Create a pure heart for me, God’ (Psalms 51:12). Creation is something from nothing; this is not the place to explain further.

records.themeTitle: The higher root is reached through return and work
records.themeSummary: The retrospective revelation does not replace the path by which it becomes accessible.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim places the higher connection and the required human path in the same complete thought. The wealthy traveler may own abundant resources at home, yet without provisions he will not reach them. So the deeper root and its retrospective clarification do not exempt a person from repentance and service. This develops the siman's insistence on chosen return alongside divine knowledge beyond time.
records.targetEnglish: Although it is true that every soul of Israel has a bond and connection in the divine root above the reach of its service, without repentance and service it is impossible to reach that higher root: the person's capacity would be annulled before arriving there. My holy grandfather compared this to a very wealthy person traveling in the wilderness far from home. Though he has great wealth and property at home, if he lacks food on the road he certainly will not reach his home, for he will die of hunger first. Through repentance and service, however, one can reach the illumination of the higher union that no sin or iniquity touches. When a person gives his entire understanding over to Hashem's will on this day, even what occurred with him earlier without awareness is clarified retrospectively as having been His will as well.

records.themeTitle: Wanting what lies within the garment
records.themeSummary: The heart receives Torah when the learner seeks its inward content rather than resting in its outer form.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same verse about a fool possessing the price of wisdom but lacking a heart. The defect is satisfaction with the garment while not wanting its inward content. This clarifies the positive side of Rav Tzadok's thirst: the learner feels that outward possession alone has not yet given him what he needs, and seeks the divine life within what he learns.
records.targetEnglish: My holy grandfather explained that a heart signifies inwardness. The principal thing in every matter is its inward content and the utterance of Hashem's mouth within it. Even the inward content of the 613 commandments is Torah, as the Zohar says (Shemini 35b), through Torah the Holy One created the world. The purpose of every matter is words of Torah. Thus the verse says (Proverbs 17:16), ‘Why is there a price in a fool's hand to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart?’ The fool does not want the inward content of the matter and is at rest with the garment itself. Israel, however, do not rest in any garment of this world; in every matter they want its inward content, and do not want things in which they do not see Heaven's honor. Even their intention in worldly benefit and pleasure is to be able to serve Hashem with that strength. Their whole aim is to fulfill His will. Hashem therefore says that all their worldly benefits are included in His will, since they serve Him with that strength.
records.originHebrew: וְאֵיזֶה נִכְנָס לַלֵּב? כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא צָמֵא וּמִשְׁתּוֹקֵק מְאֹד, כְּדִבְרֵי שַׁמַּאי: "וָאֹכְלָה וַתְּהִי בְפִי כִּדְבַשׁ לְמָתוֹק" (יְחֶזְקֵאל ג, ג), שֶׁהוּא כְּעִנְיַן: "וְתוֹרָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָי" (תְּהִלִּים מ, ט), פֵּירוּשׁ נִבְלָעָה בְּכָל הָאֵבָרִים. וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא (פֶּרֶק יד): אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִבְלָעִים בְּלֵב הָאָדָם אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁהוּא עָיֵיף לָהֶם. וְהָעֲיֵיפוּת וְהַצִּמָּאוֹן הוּא מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ שֶׁחָסֵר בַּדָּבָר וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ.
records.originEnglish: and which words penetrate the heart? When a person is deeply thirsty and intensely yearns, matching: "and I ate it, and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness" (Ezekiel 3:3), which is as: "and Your Torah is within my inward parts" (Psalms 40:9), meaning absorbed throughout all the limbs. And so it is stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 14): words of Torah are not absorbed into the heart of man unless he is weary for them. And weariness and thirst emerge from the perception of lack, feeling deficient in a matter and recognizing that words of Torah are needed to complete him.
records.targetHebrew: אמר בזה כבוד אזמו"ר זללה"ה, שלב מורה על פנימיות. והענין בזה, דהנה עיקר מכל דבר הוא הפנימיות והמוצא פי ד' שיש בהדבר ואפילו מהתרי"ג מצות הפנימיות שלהם הוא ד"ת, כדאיתא בזוה"ק (שמיני לה:) באורייתא ברא קוב"ה עלמא. היינו שמכל דבר התכלית הוא ד"ת, ועל זה אמר הכתוב (משלי י״ז:ט״ז) למה זה מחיר ביד כסיל לקנות חכמה ולב אין, היינו שהכסיל אינו רוצה הפנימיות מהדבר ויש לו נייחא מהלבוש עצמו, שאני ישראל שהם אינם בנייחא משום לבוש מעוה"ז, ורק מכל דבר רוצים הפנימיות, ומהדברים אשר אינם רואים כבוד שמים לא יחפצו. ואפילו טובת והנאת עוה"ז הכל כוונתם כדי שיהיה ביכולתם בכח זה לעבוד את השי"ת, וכל מגמתם הוא רק לקיים רצונו של השי"ת, וממילא אומר השי"ת שכל טובות עוה"ז שלהם נכללו ברצונו ית', כיון שבכח זה עובדים את השי"ת.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 21:1
records.themeTitle: Receiving the vessel together with the gift
records.themeSummary: Prayer can ask for the heart’s capacity to receive, as well as the benefit itself.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim makes explicit what the siman means by Hashem preparing the heart: He gives both the good and the vessel through which it can be received at its proper time. The rest of the passage identifies that vessel with joy in a mitzvah, inward Torah and a purified heart. This develops the prayer for desire while preserving Rav Tzadok's prior requirement to turn away from wrongful deeds.
records.targetEnglish: ‘Grant us, Hashem our God, the blessing of Your appointed times.’ Every festival has its particular blessing. On this festival the principal blessing is the receptive vessel that Hashem builds in Israel's heart to receive all good. Therefore we pray ‘Grant us’: that Hashem arrange within us this vessel to receive every good at its time, when He too is occupied in bestowing it upon us. This is like ‘Prepare their heart; incline Your ear’ (Psalms 10:17): Hashem gives the vessel together with the good. That is the principal matter of this festival. ‘As You desired and promised to bless us’ means that on the festival Hashem stands in great favor toward creation. ‘Sanctify us through Your commandments’ means that all the benefits should be for us only the joy of a mitzvah, through which it will be easier to serve Hashem. ‘Give us our portion in Your Torah’ means that He open the mitzvah's inward content, and it will shine like Torah, as in a mitzvah at its time, as the Gemara teaches (Kiddushin 33). ‘Purify our heart to serve You in truth’ means removing all the barriers from the heart's inner point, leaving only service of You in truth.
records.originHebrew: כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "תַּאֲוַת עֲנָוִים [שָׁמַעְתָּ ה' תָּכִין לִבָּם וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם י, יז), שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא תַּאֲוַת הָעֲנָוִים וּמַכִּירִים שִׁפְלוּתָם שֶׁלֵּב אָיִן – הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵכִין לִבָּם; כִּידוּעַ "ה' צִלְּךָ", כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת "אַיִן", מַשִּׂיג מַעֲלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן בְּמַדְרֵגַת "אַיִן", וְיָכוֹל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ וּלְהוֹלִיד יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן כְּעִנְיַן "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא", וְהוּא חָכְמָה בַּמּוֹחַ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יֵשׁ מִיֵּשׁ – רָצוֹן וְחֵשֶׁק בַּלֵּב; פֵּירוּשׁ, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לוֹ שֶׁאֵין זוּלָתוֹ כְּלָל עַכְשָׁו כְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ, וּכְשֶׁדָּבָר זֶה מֵאִיר לְעֵינֵי הָאָדָם, אָז תֵּיכֶף נוֹלָדִים רְצוֹנוֹת בְּמוֹחַ וָלֵב. אֲבָל צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מִקּוֹדֶם "אָבְדוּ גוֹיִם מֵאַרְצוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים י, טז) פֵּירוּשׁ, תְּשׁוּבָה עַל הָעֲבֵירוֹת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בָּאוּ גוֹיִם בְּנַחֲלָתֶךָ" (שָׁם עט, א), כִּידוּעַ שֶׁאֶרֶץ רוֹמֵז לַגּוּף וְכֹחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וְגוֹיִם הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַהָפְכִיִּים מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וַאֲבִידָתָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים, שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת, וְאָז מִתְדַּבֵּק בַּמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשׁוֹת דִּתְנַן בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּכֵלִים, שֶׁהִיא קְדוּשַׁת הָאָרֶץ.
records.originEnglish: as written: "You have heard the desire of the humble, Hashem; You will direct their heart, etc." (Psalms 10:17), for this very longing is the desire of the humble who recognize their lowliness and lack of heart—and the Holy One prepares their heart; for as is known, "Hashem is your shadow": when a person is at the level of Ayin (Nothingness), he grasps the transcendence of the Blessed Name likewise at the level of Ayin, and is empowered to draw down and generate substance from nothingness (yesh me'ayin, matching "Create in me a clean heart"), which is wisdom in the brain, followed by substance from substance (yesh mi-yesh)—will and desire in the heart; meaning that the Blessed Name illuminates for him that there is none beside Him now just as before the world was created, the glory of Hashem filling the entire earth; and when this reality radiates before a person's eyes, holy desires are immediately born within mind and heart. But prior to this there must be "the nations are perished out of His land" (Psalms 10:16)— meaning repentance over transgressions in physical deed, concerning which it is said: "the nations are come into Your inheritance" (Psalms 79:1); for "land" alludes to the physical body and faculties of action, and "nations" are the forces opposing the will of the Blessed Name, and their perishing is achieved through at least lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah), wherein willful sins become like inadvertent errors, and then one attaches himself to the lowest of the ten sanctities enumerated in the first chapter of Kelim, which is the sanctity of the Land.

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:34
records.themeTitle: Present judgment and the later outcome
records.themeSummary: A present judgment is not identical with knowledge of how the whole life will end.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov distinguishes Avraham's present view of Yishmael from the later outcome: Hashem directs attention to how he stands now. This is a qualified comparison with the siman's account of temporary success and final disclosure. It cautions against treating the visible present as proof of a permanent spiritual state, while also refusing to condemn a person now on the basis of a supposed knowledge of his future.
records.targetEnglish: Even Avraham's statement (Genesis 17:18), ‘If only Yishmael would live before You,’ corresponds to ‘Do not bear false witness against your fellow.’ ‘Your fellow’ means the Holy One, as the Zohar teaches (Beshalach 55b). Hashem had promised him (Genesis 17:16), ‘I will bless her and also give you a son from her.’ Why then did he say, ‘If only Yishmael would live before You,’ which appears like false testimony? Hashem told him not to say so: rather, what I have counseled will stand, ‘Sarah your wife will bear you a son.’ Hashem illuminated this statement for him until he himself afterward sent Yishmael out of his house. Yet, because Yishmael was righteous at that time, Hashem showed him not to fix his gaze on what would occur with him later. ‘As he is there,’ he is righteous and must not be judged adversely, as taught in the Talmud (Rosh Hashanah 16b) and the Midrash.

records.originEnglish: And this demands profound discernment to recognize what is merely temporary and later revealed retroactively never to have been truly so and on the contrary, mitzvot operate inversely, where penitents overturn judgment into mercy while the wicked overturn mercy into judgment, and as written: 'the kindness of the nations is sin,' see Bava Batra 10b that temporarily it counts against Israel, but ultimately against them, even though he currently succeeds in Torah and mitzvot according to human sight.

records.themeTitle: Trust accompanied by prayer and effort
records.themeSummary: Recognizing the Giver does not make the person’s chosen response unnecessary.
records.explanation: Kometz HaMinchah develops the same casting-burden verse while requiring both natural action and prayer for success. This qualifies the siman's dependence on help from above: casting the burden concerns recognition of the source and relief of distress, while Torah, prayer and chosen effort remain the means through which the person responds.
records.targetEnglish: This is the measure, as the Sages said (Niddah 70b): he should increase his business activity and seek mercy, and so on. He asks for mercy that Hashem grant him success through the natural course, for one without the other is insufficient; the Holy One does not perform a miracle for falsehood.

records.themeTitle: David’s labor and the Temple’s enduring holiness
records.themeSummary: The inward work can establish what remains even when the visible result comes through another.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef identifies David's suffering, effort and prayer as the basis for the Temple's enduring holiness. His son builds it, and later sin conceals its light, yet neither fact erases what David's work established. This develops Rav Tzadok's distinction between a visible lack of completion and an inward desire that truly brought the work into being.
records.targetEnglish: This is the meaning of the Talmud's statement that He caused His Shekhinah to dwell in Shiloh and the other places. In Shiloh and Gilgal He caused His presence to dwell from His side without Israel's prior suffering; concerning this it says, ‘Zion said, He has forsaken me,’ and ‘Even these may be forgotten’—their holiness ceased. See Aggadat Bereishit, chapter 71, cited in Sidrei Taharot, Kelim 72. The eternal Temple is different: there His presence dwelled through David's suffering and labor, and he prayed for it with self-giving, until Hashem said to him (I Kings 8:19), ‘Your son who will come from your loins will build the house for My name.’ Concerning this the verse says, ‘I will not forget you.’ Through the suffering associated with that holiness it is fixed; all the prayers and offerings were there. Although sin concealed this light, He promises us that through our prayer that He return to dwell in Jerusalem, He will certainly rebuild Jerusalem and return His presence as before to the eternal Temple. This is what we say here: like a woman in her period who awaits her return to her former permitted state, Jerusalem too will have a repair.

records.originEnglish: and in this realm King David never saw manifest good, such as his passionate desire to build the Temple, concerning which it was told him: "Only you shall not build the house, etc." (I Kings 8:19). And in truth David represented the dimension of action, as is known, and whatever a person is destined to complete appears to him as constantly lacking so that he intensifies desire and fortitude in it, and all the desire he adds does not serve to bring him peace, because he sees that he does not visibly succeed. For tranquility exists only when something is fully completed, and this occurs only after the soul has rested, as our Sages stated (Shabbat 30a): "During your lifetime I will not reveal it; during the lifetime of your son Solomon I will reveal it"; and ultimately the Temple was called by the name of David (Bemidbar Rabbah 12), and it became known that in truth he actualized everything into reality, even though the Blessed Name did not grant him visible success in his actions during his lifetime.
