Their concealment does not merely obstruct the light; it makes the illumination approachable as nourishment. This illuminates the present siman's movement from heavenly life to Torah received through eating, while preserving the need for a suitable form of reception rather than identifying food with unbounded divine light without mediation.
records.originHebrew: וּמִסְּתָמָא כָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הָעוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לָהֶם, הֵם אוֹכְלֵי מָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: כָּל הַמְּקַבֵּל עוֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וּפַרְנָסָתוֹ הוּא דּוּגְמַת מָן, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ וַדַּאי אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה לְהַכְנִיס בַּלֵּב חַיּוּת מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַשִּׂיג דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאֲמִיתַּת חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ [וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמָּן בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי: "לֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כב), נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁפַע כָּפוּל, וְהוּא טְעִימָה מֵהַשְׁפָּעַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם הַמַּאֲכָלוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת; וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד ב, עַיֵּין שָׁם]:
records.originEnglish: And presumably all Torah scholars who engage in Torah, to whom the Torah was given, are eaters of manna, as it is written: Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, the yoke of the government and the yoke of worldly occupation are removed from him, and his livelihood is like manna; and it certainly contains that holiness to instill in the heart vitality from the truth of Hashem, blessed be He, by which he grasps the words of Torah from the truth of His wisdom, blessed be He and from the double portion of manna on Friday, it appears that on Friday a double influx of Torah descends, tasting of Shabbat, just as one tastes Shabbat foods on Friday; and I subsequently found this in Zohar Beshalach 61b, see there.
records.targetHebrew: וז"ש בזוהר פ"א א' דנו"ה הם לבושי דקודשא בריך הוא כמו הלבוש שמכסה ומאפיל קצת תוקף בהירות הנלבש כדי שנוכל על ידי להסתכל בגוף הנלבש והם נקראים גם כן בזוהר ויקרא כ"ו ריש ע"א שחקים ששוחקים מן פירוש מזון הצדיקים שהוא ההני' בהשגת זיו השם יתברך כמ"ש ברכות י"ז א' וז"ש בפ' יוה"כ (ע"ה) מן לחם שמאה"ש אוכלין כמ"ש בשמות רבה פ' ל"ב על מלאכי השרת אותו לשון דברכות שם ניזונין מזיו השכינה וההני' הזו רק כאשר מתיחדת עם דודה ובאה על ידי השוקיים המצמצמין ההשגה וטוחנין עד אשר דק וראוי למאכל ומזון
records.targetEnglish: The Zohar therefore describes Netzach and Hod as garments of the Holy One. A garment covers and somewhat dims the strength of what is clothed, so that through it we can look upon what is clothed. They are also called the heavens that grind manna: the nourishment of the righteous, their delight in apprehending Hashem's radiance, as described in Berakhot. Thus Yoma calls manna the bread eaten by ministering angels, and Shemot Rabbah says that they are nourished by the radiance of the Shechinah. This delight occurs when the Shechinah is joined with her Beloved, and comes through the supporting powers that limit apprehension and grind it finely until it is fit as food and nourishment.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: An enclosing garment does not exhaust the soul's identity
records.themeSummary: Outward concealment can coexist with an inward connection that still calls for disclosure and repair.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef describes the land acquiring eyes to recognize inward service rather than judging by the garment alone. This clarifies the distinction behind ‘rescue me from an evil man’: the obstructing configuration of thoughts is real, but it does not exhaust the soul's root. The enduring inward connection supplies the possibility of release; it does not make the work of removing the garment unnecessary.
records.originHebrew: וּכְדִבְרֵי שַׁמַּאי בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): וְקָיְימֵי עֲלַן וְכוּלֵי, כָּל חַד מִינַּן אַלְפָּא מִשְּׂמָאלֵיהּ וְרִבְבָתָא מִימִינֵיהּ. "מִימִינוֹ" – פֵּירוּשׁ: תַּאֲווֹת וְחֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, זֶהוּ "רִבְבוֹת" לְשׁוֹן רִבּוּי, שֶׁהוּא בְּתוֹקֶף עָצוּם, כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבְּלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּטַעַם דִּמְצוֹרָע מִשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא הַזָּב.
records.originEnglish: And as in Berakhot 6a: they stand around us, a thousand at our left and ten thousand at our right. "At his right"—the lusts of this world, designated as "ten thousand" (rivavah), multitude, surging with vast power, this being the primary inclination in Jewish hearts (which is why a leper is expelled beyond the camp and not a zav).
records.targetHebrew: והיינו שגם הארץ ירגיש לעומק ויהיה לה עינין מי שבאמת עובד להשי"ת, ממילא לא יאבד שום נפש מישראל, כי בעומק לב ישראל המה מלאים רצון ועבודה. אף שבאמת נמצא לפעמים הסתר גדול אצל ישראל, זה הוא רק על הלבוש, אבל בעומק הלב שם ישראל המה נקיים. ולזה יבין הארץ ג"כ, שאף שנמצא לפעמים אצל ישראל טומאה והסתר, אבל הוא רק על הלבוש, ובעומק המה מקושרים באור רצונו ית'. וזה ולא תקיא הארץ אתכם, ששום פרט נפש לא יאבד מישראל:
records.targetEnglish: The land too will perceive the depth and have eyes to recognize who truly serves Hashem. No soul of Israel will consequently be lost, for in the depth of Israel's heart they are full of willingness and service. Although great concealment is sometimes found within Israel, it is in the garment; in the depth of the heart they are pure. The land will therefore understand that even when impurity and concealment appear within Israel, these concern the garment, while inwardly they are connected with the light of His will. This is ‘the land will not vomit you out’: no individual soul of Israel will be lost.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 4
records.themeTitle: Restraint needs a positive direction for the heart
records.themeSummary: Removing one desire without redirecting the heart can leave room for anger or another desire.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach gives an exact example of the problem: a heart emptied of a lustful thought can next fill with anger. When turning away is directed by love of Hashem, that love remains within the heart. This helps explain why the present siman places the chief work in drawing desire into Torah rather than trusting anger to defeat anger. The sources describe related forms of positive direction, while the siman retains its demanding conditions for any use of anger.
records.originHebrew: וּמִמֵּילָא מִתְפּוֹצֵץ גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִצְרָא דְּכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם תַּאֲוָה וְחֵשֶׁק רַק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֵינוֹ כּוֹעֵס אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מְרַתְּחָא לֵיהּ (תַּעֲנִית ד.), כְּעִנְיַן "מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ ה' אֶשְׂנָא" (תְּהִלִּים קלט, כא). וְאָמַר: "וּרְבָבָה מִימִינֶךָ" (שָׁם צא, ז) – עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבַּיָּמִין, שֶׁמַּכְנִיס כָּל חֶשְׁקוֹ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
records.originEnglish: and automatically through this the inclination for anger and bloodshed is likewise shattered, since when one harbors no desire and passion except for words of Torah, he becomes angry only where the Torah itself inflames him (Ta'anit 4a), in the manner of: "Do I not hate them, Hashem, that hate You?" (Psalms 139:21). And Scripture states: "and ten thousand at your right hand" (ibid. 91:7)—achieved through the Torah which is at the right, directing all his desire toward words of Torah.
records.targetHebrew: דרך עצל הינו אף שאדם מונע את עצמו ממעשים רעים וממחשבות רעות ורצונות רעות, אף שאינו עושה זאת מחמת אהבת השם יתברך רק עושה כעצל, כגון שמבין שבעולם הזה לא יצלחו לו דברים כאלה, או באפן אחר שאינו מאהבת השם יתברך, אז דרכו הוא כמשכת חדק, כי הלב לא יוכל להיות פנוי ממחשבות ורצונות אף רגע אחת, וכאשר יסור מחשבות תאוה מלבו יבא ללבו מחשבת כעס וכדומה, וכל דרכיה המה כמשכת חדק, כי לעולם יצטרך לסגוף ועבודה קדם שיסור דבר אחד מלבו יבא ללבו דבר אחר שאינו הגון. אבל "ארח ישרים" הינו שפונה מכל דבר מחמת אהבת השם יתברך, זה הוא דרכו סלול לטוב, כי כאשר יסור מלבו איזה דבר רע ישאר בלבו אהבת השם יתברך, וממילא לא יבא ללבו שום דבר אחר שלא כהוגן.
records.targetEnglish: ‘The way of the lazy person’ means that even if a person refrains from bad actions, thoughts and desires, when he does not do so from love of Hashem but for a merely passive reason—for example, because he understands that such things will not succeed for him in this world—his way is like a thorny hedge. The heart cannot be empty of thoughts and desires for even a moment. When a thought of desire departs, a thought of anger or something similar enters. He continually needs discipline and work: before one improper thing leaves, another arrives. ‘The path of the upright,’ however, means turning from everything out of love of Hashem. That path is paved toward good. When something bad leaves his heart, love of Hashem remains, and no other improper thing consequently enters.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 3:4
records.themeTitle: Understanding makes a mitzvah a lasting Torah acquisition
records.themeSummary: The enacted mitzvah can become inward Torah through attention to its details and meaning.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov develops the same distinction from Sotah with which this siman concludes. The person does not only perform a momentary act; attention to its particulars and meaning allows its Torah light to be grasped within him. This explains why the siman connects wisdom in the mitzvah with something that remains his beyond the moment of performance. The particular root described by Beit Yaakov deepens general observance rather than exempting the person from other mitzvot.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (יז.): הַנָּחַת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה – לוֹמַר: קִיֵּים זֶה וְכוּלֵי; וּבַחַיִּים מוֹעִיל לְהַכְנִיס בֶּאֱמֶת בַּלֵּב קִיּוּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בָּזֶה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ שֶׁהוּא תַּבְלִין לִכְלָלוּת הַיֵּצֶר כֻּלּוֹ שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ. וְסִיֵּים: "כִּי לְעוֹלָם הִיא לִי", לְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (כא. לְרַב יוֹסֵף) דְּרַק בְּעִידָּנָא דְּעָסֵיק בְּמִצְוָה מַצְּלָא;
records.originEnglish: and along these lines they said in Bava Kamma 17a: placing a Torah scroll upon his bier means proclaiming: this one fulfilled, etc.; and in life it avails to instill within the heart the fulfillment of all written therein, namely the entire Torah which serves as the seasoning against the collective inclination of the whole world. And he concluded: "for they are ever with me," because in Sotah 21a Rav Yosef states that only while actively engaged in a mitzvah does it protect;
records.targetHebrew: והוא שבעידנא דלא עסיק בה אזי לא נשאר בגוף מקדושת המצוה, לפי שאין הגוף מבין שרשה. אבל מצוה ששייכת לאדם, בפרט אם ירבה בדקדוקיה ובהבנתה, יאיר לו השם יתברך שיבין את המצוה באור תורה, שכל עיקר המצוה תהיה דברי תורה, ויהיה לו הבנה בכוונתה, ויראה שהלבוש והפעולה מהמצוה הוא רק בעולם הזה. וזה הוא שאנו מתפללין (בקדושא דסדרא) הוא יפתח לבנו בתורתו, בוא״ו, וזה מרמז על הדברי תורה ומצות ששייכים לכל אדם מיוחד בפרט לעיקר השורש שלו:
records.targetEnglish: When he is not engaged in it, the body's share in the mitzvah's holiness does not remain, because the body does not understand its root. But with a mitzvah related to a person—especially when he increases his care for its details and his understanding—Hashem illuminates for him an understanding of the mitzvah in Torah's light. The mitzvah's very substance becomes Torah for him; he understands its intention and sees that the garment and action of the mitzvah belong to this world. This is our prayer, ‘May He open our heart in His Torah’: it alludes to the Torah teachings and mitzvot particularly related to each person's essential root.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:11
records.themeTitle: The search becomes different when Torah is needed as life
records.themeSummary: Seeking the call's particulars requires more than treating Torah as an optional increase in one's possessions.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov explains Eliyahu's challenge to a fisherman who said he lacked the understanding for Torah. The intelligence he found for necessary livelihood illustrated what a search driven by actual need could accomplish. This develops the present siman's quotation from Proverbs: hearing the general call leads to a search through the heart's particulars when Torah is recognized as needed life, not merely added information.
records.originHebrew: וְלָכֵן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב נִקְרָא "קוֹל" וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה "דִּבּוּר", וְכֵן הַהַשְׁמָעָה לַלֵּב הוּא רַק בְּדֶרֶךְ כְּלָל לָדַעַת אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו: "אִם [תְּבַקְשֶׁנָּה כַכָּסֶף וְכוּלֵי] תַּחְפְּשֶׂנָּה, אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, ד–ה) בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבְּלֵב הָאָדָם בְּפִרְטֵי פְּרָטוֹת כְּפִי הַצָּרִיךְ לוֹ.
records.originEnglish: hence the Written Torah is Voice and the Oral Torah is Speech, and the calling to the heart is general, to know Godliness and search for Him: "If you seek her as silver... then shall you understand the fear of Hashem" (Proverbs 2:4–5) in the heart's Binah in detail.
records.targetHebrew: היינו, מחמת שהיה דחוק לפרנסה היה בו דעת להמציא לעצמו סבה להפרנסה; וכן אם יצרך אדם לדברי תורה ויבקש אחריהם ויחפשם כמטמונים – אזי יבוא עליהם, וכדכתיב (משלי ב, ד): "אם תבקשנה ככסף וגומר". וזה ודאי אדם גדול היה שנתגלה לו אליהו זכור לטוב; אכן הודיעו שצריך לבקש ולחפש אחרי הדברי תורה, לא כאדם שרוצה להרויח הון רב, היינו מותרות, רק שיראה חסרונו: שבלא דברי תורה חסר חיים הוא, וזהו שאמר לו שיבקשם כפרנסתו, אז ימצא לך.
records.targetEnglish: Because he was pressed for livelihood, he had the understanding to devise a means of livelihood. Similarly, if a person needs words of Torah, seeks them and searches for them like hidden treasures, he will attain them, as it says, ‘If you seek it like silver.’ This was certainly a great person, since Eliyahu appeared to him. Yet Eliyahu taught him that he must seek Torah not like someone who wants to gain a great fortune—that is, luxuries—but by recognizing his lack: without Torah he is lacking life. He must seek it as his livelihood, and then he will find it.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: An effect of prayer may emerge through another path
records.themeSummary: Avraham's prayer bore fruit in Lot's rescue even though Sodom was not saved.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik discusses the very morning prayer at the place of Avraham's earlier standing. It points out that the prayer's result was not exhausted by the failure to save Sodom: it rescued Lot, from whom David's root of prayer would emerge. The example gives substance to continued prayer when the visible outcome remains dark. It illustrates a real effect without identifying that partial result with the complete salvation for which this siman continues to ask.
records.originHebrew: אָז בָּא לְמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בֶּאֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה, שֶׁמִּתְחַזֵּק בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁוַּדַּאי יוֹשִׁיעַ וְהַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָאֱמֶת הַגָּמוּר. וְהוּא חִבּוּר שְׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, דְּהַיְינוּ הַיִּרְאָה בַּהֹוֶה וְהַבְּטִיחוּת וְהַשִּׂמְחָה בֶּעָתִיד, וּתְפִלָּתוֹ אָז נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן "פְּגִיעָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יא; בְּרָכוֹת כו:). וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל לְשׁוֹן "מַפְגִּיעַ בִּתְפִלּוֹת", וּ"מַפְגִּיעַ אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ", וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּתַעֲנִית (ח.) עַל פָּסוּק "וַיְצַו עָלָיו כִּמְפַגִּיעַ" (אִיּוֹב לו, לב), דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּמוֹ פָּגַע, שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב וְלָלֶכֶת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן רַק שֶׁיַּעֲנֵהוּ, וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּאוֹחֵז בִּבְגָדוֹ וְאוֹמֵר: אֵינִי מַנִּיחֲךָ. וְזֶהוּ תְּפִלַּת הַלַּיְלָה בְּעֵת הַחֹשֶׁךְ הַגָּמוּר, אַחַר שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲנָה זֶה פַּעֲמַיִם, הֲגַם שֶׁהָיָה בְּאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה וּבְלֵב נִשְׁבָּר גַּם כֵּן; צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כִּמְפַגִּיעַ עַד שֶׁיּוּכְרַח לְהֵיעָנוֹת וּלְהַשִּׂיג בְּמִדַּת אֱמוּנָה מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת, הַיְינוּ הַבֵּירוּר לָעַיִן שֶׁהוּא כֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בּוֹטֵחַ בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ:
records.originEnglish: then he arrives at the attribute of Jacob in truth and faith, strengthening himself in faith that Hashem will surely save and all is for the best, which is absolute truth. And this is the synthesis of Abraham and Isaac: awe in the present, and confidence and joy regarding the future; and his prayer then is termed "encounter" (pegiah, Genesis 28:11; Berakhot 26b). And as I heard on the term "importuning (mafgiah) in prayer," and Ta'anit 8a on "and commands it to strike the mark (kimefgiah)" (Job 36:32), meaning one who refuses to depart from Hashem until answered, like one seizing His garment and saying: I will not let You go. And this is the night prayer in pitch darkness, having seen he was not answered twice, even though he prayed with love, fear, and a broken heart; he must importune until answered, attaining through the attribute of Faith the attribute of Truth—manifest verification before his eyes, just as he trusted in his faith.
records.targetHebrew: ואף שידע השם יתברך שלא יפעול בתפלתו להציל את סדום, שלא ימצא שם אף עשרה צדיקים, מכל מקום הועילה תפלתו להציל את לוט
records.targetEnglish: Although Hashem knew that his prayer would not save Sodom, since even ten righteous people would not be found there, his prayer nevertheless availed to save Lot.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Night of Pesach 24:1
records.themeTitle: Practice can hold the person before understanding is complete
records.themeSummary: Yosef's bones signify awe that anchors observance while the newly received good still needs clarification.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim expands the very received teaching cited here. Moshe recognizes an unresolved connection to Egypt and takes Yosef's bones as an image of holding to straightforward mitzvah observance before every reason has become clear. This explains why awe preceding wisdom is needed precisely when the route seems puzzling: the heart's attachment to the command keeps newly gained understanding from becoming detached knowledge.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מח.): זָב – מֵרְחַבְעָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "הִתְאַמֵּץ לַעֲלוֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה" (מְלָכִים א יב, יח). וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף" (שְׁמוֹת יג, יט), שֶׁהָעַצְמוּת שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הוּא: יִרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ. וְזֶה צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח בְּעֵת שֶׁרוֹאֶה שִׁינּוּי בְּהִתְנַהֲגוּת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵבִין, כְּהָךְ דְּ"וְלֹא נָחָם אֱלֹהִים דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים]" (שָׁם, יז).
records.originEnglish: And this is what our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 48b): one afflicted with zivah issued from Rehoboam, of whom it is said: "made speed to get him up to his chariot" (I Kings 12:18). And as I heard regarding "And Moses took the bones (atzmot) of Joseph," that the essence (atzmut) of Joseph is: his fear of sin precedes his wisdom. And this one must seize when beholding an anomalous shift in divine direction that one cannot comprehend, as in "God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines."
records.targetHebrew: ויקח משה את עצמות יוסף עמו וגו' ביאר בזה אזמו"ר הגה"ק יען שראה משה רבינו שפרעה ליוה את ישראל מזה הבין שיש להם עדיין חיבור עם מצרים לזה הי' העצה לאחוז בפשוטי המצות ועל זאת העצה רומזין עצמות יוסף שיראת חטאו קודמת לחכמתו היינו כי אחר שינצלו את מצרים ועשאן כמצילה שאין בה דגן ולקחו ישראל כל הטובות הנמצאים בהם וכל עוד שלא ביררו ישראל התשוקה מאלו הטובות ע"י עבודתם זה נקרא שיש להם עדיין חיבור עם מצרים
records.targetEnglish: ‘Moshe took Yosef's bones with him.’ My holy grandfather explained: When Moshe saw that Pharaoh accompanied Israel, he understood that they still had a connection to Egypt. The counsel was therefore to hold to the straightforward mitzvot. Yosef's bones allude to this counsel: his fear of sin preceded his wisdom. After Israel emptied Egypt and took all the good found there, their desire for those good things still required clarification through their service. As long as that clarification was unfinished, they still had a connection to Egypt.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Aharon's role preserves a living recipient of holiness
records.themeSummary: Preparing the recipient includes sustaining embodied life for further service.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same description of Aharon as the escort of the bride: he safeguards the recipient's living capacity for continued service, alongside Moshe's disclosure of divine nearness. This gives substance to the siman's image of an awakening from below that carries divine presence. The eightfold correspondence here is conceptual: the actual Yom Kippur entry into the Holy of Holies is in four linen garments, specified in Leviticus 16:4, rather than the eight garments of the ordinary high-priestly service.
records.originHebrew: וְיֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁמוֹנָה דְּבָרִים, וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּנֶגְדָּם רוֹמְזִים שְׁמוֹנָה בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְפוֹרָשִׁים בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר. וְהַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הוּא הָעוֹבֵד וִיסוֹד הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא אַהֲרֹן "שׁוֹשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, כ עַמּוּד א). וְהַשְּׁמוֹנָה בְּגָדִים הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, שֶׁהוּא בִּקְבִיעוּת הַמָּקוֹם, דְּאָז יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא וְלֹא בְּמֶרְכָּבָה, רַק עַל יְדֵי הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הַחַיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים נוֹשְׂאִים וְסוֹבְלִים הַכִּסֵּא כָּבוֹד, וְאָז הוּא עִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה בִּשְׁמוֹנָה מַדְרֵגוֹת דִּלְהָבִין וְכוּלֵי.
records.originEnglish: And there are eight verbs in that prayer, and I heard that corresponding to them are the eight garments of the High Priest, explained elsewhere. And the High Priest is the servant embodying the foundation of awakening from below, which is why Aaron is titled "the groomsman of the Matronita" (Zohar III:20a). And the eight garments pertain to entering the Holy of Holies, the fixed place, where He sits upon a Throne and not a moving Chariot, the living creatures below bearing the Throne through the lower awakening, which is the core attainment in the eight rungs of "to understand, etc."
records.targetHebrew: ואז צריך להשושבינא דמטרוניתא, היינו שיראה שלא יבטל עצמו לגמרי, כי אם להשאר בחיים של עוה"ז, כי מאחר שאדם רואה איך שעבודתו יש לו מקום אצל השי"ת ואיך שהשי"ת חפץ בעבודתו, ממילא צריך להשאר בחיים כדי שיעבוד את השי"ת עוד, כי אם שיבטל אדם עצמו לגמרי ולא ישאר בחיים כלל, זה אינו ברצון השי"ת.
records.targetEnglish: Then the escort of the bride is needed: he must see that the person does not nullify himself completely, but remains alive in this world. Once a person sees that his service has a place with Hashem and that Hashem desires it, he must remain alive so that he can serve Hashem further. A complete nullification in which no life remains in this world is not Hashem's will.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Permitted things can still require clarification
records.themeSummary: Lot's mixed root illustrates why nogah is neither simply discarded nor automatically holy.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov interprets Lot's rescue through the mixed category of nogah. Its conclusion precisely identifies the sphere at issue: worldly matters that are genuinely permitted, yet whose direction still needs clarification. This makes the siman's counsel against indiscriminate rejection intelligible while keeping its distinction between this mixed sphere and the three prohibited shells.
records.originHebrew: וּכְשֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִתְגַּבֵּר יוֹתֵר עַד הַמּוֹחַ, לְהַחְכִּים בְּכָל יוֹם בְּחָכְמוֹת חִיצוֹנִיּוֹת, תַּאֲווֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת לְרַע וּלְהַשְׁכִּיחַ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – זֶה נֶגֶד יָוָן, שֶׁנּוֹדָע מֵחָכְמַת יְוָנִית שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ חָכְמוֹת חִיצוֹנִיּוֹת, וְלָכֵן מְנֻמֶּרֶת בִּגְזֵירוֹתֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יג). זֶהוּ "אֵשׁ מִתְלַקַּחַת", דְּ"מִתְלַקַּחַת" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמּוֹסֶפֶת בְּכָל רֶגַע הִתְלַהֲבוּת חָדָשׁ וְאֵין כָּבָה כְּלָל, וְזֶהוּ נַרַ"נ דְּרַע.
records.originEnglish: And when, Heaven forbid, evil surges higher into the brain, scheming daily in alien philosophies, conceiving new lusts and perverse desires to cause the will of the Blessed Name to be forgotten—this corresponds to Greece, known for Greek wisdom which is the root of external disciplines, which is why Greece is compared to a spotted leopard in its variegated decrees, as our Sages taught (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5). This is the "flashing fire" (esh mitlakachat), where mitlakachat denotes constantly igniting fresh intellectual fervor without ever subsiding, and these constitute the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah of evil.
records.targetHebrew: וַיְהִי בְּשַׁחֵת אֱלֹהִים אֶת עָרֵי הַכִּכָּר וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת אַבְרָהָם וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת לוֹט מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה וְגוֹמֵר. וְהַטַּעַם מֵהַשַּׁיָּיכוּת מִזְּכִירַת אַבְרָהָם לְהַצָּלַת לוֹט הוּא, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ דַּף פ) שֶׁשֵּׁם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא לוֹט וְאַבְרָהָם הוּא הַנְּשָׁמָה, וּבְכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (שַׁעַר הַפְּסוּקִים פָּרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ עַל הַפָּסוּק וַיְהִי בִּימֵי אַמְרָפֶל) אִיתָא שֶׁלּוֹט הוּא מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ שֶׁהוּא מִתַּעֲרוֹבוֹת טוֹב וָרַע, כִּדְכְתִיב (יְחֶזְקֵאל א׳:ד׳) וְנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא חֹשֶׁךְ וְהָאוֹר חוֹנֶה סָבִיב לוֹ. וְעִיקַּר בִּיאַת הַנְּשָׁמָה לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא לְבָרֵר זֹאת הַקְּלִיפָּה וּלְהַעֲלוֹתָהּ עַד רוּם הַמַּעֲלוֹת. וְהַבֵּיאוּר בָּזֶה הוּא, כִּי קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ מְרַמֶּזֶת לְכָל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת, וְהַאֻמְנָם כִּי הֵמָּה הֶיתֵּר גָּמוּר, בְּכָל זֹאת צָרִיךְ בֵּירוּר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: קַדֵּשׁ עַצְמְךָ בַּמּוּתָּר לָךְ.
records.targetEnglish: ‘When God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Avraham and sent Lot out of the overthrow.’ The relation between remembering Avraham and saving Lot is explained by the Zohar: Lot represents the inclination and Avraham the soul. The writings of the Ari identify Lot with the shell of nogah, a mixture of good and evil, as it says, ‘and brightness around it’—it is darkness, with light encamped around it. The soul chiefly comes to this world to clarify this shell and raise it to the highest levels. Nogah signifies all permitted worldly matters. Although these are entirely permitted, they nevertheless require clarification, as the Sages taught: Sanctify yourself within what is permitted to you.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The different members still form one complete stature
records.themeSummary: Distinctions of role belong within a collective in which each member has a particular service.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef interprets the same list used in this siman, from the leaders through the woodcutters and water-drawers. It emphasizes that the completed stature includes each member's particular service. This helps distinguish the present classification of spiritual capacities and appointments from the separate question of belonging to the covenantal whole; one member's role need not be identical to another's for both to participate in its completion.
records.originHebrew: וּבַזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם מְכֻוָּונוֹת נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין לִימִינָא וְה' לִשְׂמָאלָא הַנִּזְכָּר בְּפָרָשַׁת "אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים": "רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים כט, ט), מְבוֹאָרִים נֶגֶד ה' מַעֲלוֹת בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּזְכָּר: דְּכָל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים; וְשׁוֹטֵר הוּא מִצַּד הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב;
records.originEnglish: And in Zohar Yitro 82a the Ten Commandments align with five rungs to the right and five to the left mentioned in Nitzavim: "your heads, etc." (Deuteronomy 29:9), reflecting the five levels of divine perception: all Israel are believers, children of believers; officers (shoter) reflect the feeling of the heart;
records.targetHebrew: וזה ראשיכם שבטיכם וגו' מחוטב עציך עד שואב מימיך. ונחשב כאן קומה שלמה מן הגדול שבישראל עד הפחות שבפחותים, ובמקום שנמצא קומה שלימה שם מכיר האדם אשר כל אחד ואחד משלים רצונו ית', וכעין דאיתא בש"ס (ראש השנה כה:) יפתח בדורו כשמואל בדורו, והיינו שמכיר האדם אשר הולך בעבודה, אשר כל אחד משלים רצונו ומבוקשו ית' מאתו.
records.targetEnglish: This is ‘your heads, your tribes … from your woodcutter to your water-drawer.’ A complete stature is counted here, from the greatest in Israel to the least. Where a complete stature is present, a person recognizes that every individual fulfills His will. This resembles the teaching that Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation: one who proceeds in divine service recognizes that each fulfills the will and purpose Hashem seeks from him.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Rav Tzadok offers two readings of the same report
records.themeSummary: The earlier interpretation emphasizes attained spontaneity; this siman expressly considers the report in its plain sense.
records.explanation: In Siman 209 Rav Tzadok finds it difficult to attribute ordinary distraction to such great sages and suggests that ‘I did not direct my heart’ means they normally had no need for a separate act of concentration. Here he explicitly says the Yerushalmi can be understood in its plain sense: even their prayer could include a fleeting other thought. These are distinct interpretive proposals. The earlier explanation should not erase the qualification about a flicker of thought stated in the present siman.
records.originHebrew: כִּי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כָּל הַיּוֹם, לֹא יִמָּלֵט גַּם כֵּן מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד.) דְּעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל, וּמַשְׁמָע דְּעַל כָּל אָדָם קָאָמַר. וְאָתָאן דִּבְרֵי הַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז:): "אֲנָא מִן יוֹמָא לָא כַּוְּונִית" כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִמָּלֵט בְּכָל הַתְּפִלָּה כֻּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם נִצְנוּץ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה.
records.originEnglish: for one who is not clean of alien thoughts throughout the day will not escape alien thoughts during prayer either, as written in Bava Batra 164b that from calculating expectation in prayer no man is saved, implying every person. And this brings us back to the Yerushalmi cited by Tosafot (Rosh Hashanah 16b): "In all my days I never achieved full concentration," according to its literal sense, that it was impossible to escape throughout the entire prayer from some spark of extraneous thought.
records.targetHebrew: וּבֶאֱמֶת עַל אֲנָשִׁים גְּדוֹלִים כָּאֵלֶּה רָחוֹק מִלִּשְׁמוֹעַ זֶה, בִּפְרָט רַבִּי חִיָּיא דְּאָמְרוּ עָלָיו בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פה:) שֶׁאָמַר: מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ – נָשֵׁיב זִיקָא וְכוּלֵי. וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ: "לָא כַּוְּונִית" – לֹא הוּצְרַךְ; דְּכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב שַׁיָּיךְ בְּבַעַל דִּמְיוֹן וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת, שֶׁהַלָּשׁוֹן מְשׁוּלָּח לְדַבֵּר אַף שֶׁלִּבּוֹ בַּל עִמּוֹ, וְצָרִיךְ לְכַוֵּין לִבּוֹ. וְהוּא לֹא הוּצְרַךְ מֵעוֹלָם לָזֶה, שֶׁמֵּעוֹלָם לֹא הָיָה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ דָּבָר אַחֵר, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹכַח עֵינָיו, וְלֹא הָיָה מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא כִּמְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים לְעוֹלָם. וְ"יוֹמָא חַד בָּעֵי כַּוְּונִית וְכוּלֵי" – פֵּירוּשׁ הוּצְרַךְ לְכָךְ, שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת מַטְרִידִים, וְאוּלַי הַיְינוּ עוּבָדָא דְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (שָׁם) דְּאֵלִיָּהוּ טַרְדִינְהוּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וְאָז הוּצְרַךְ לְכַוֵּין הַלֵּב לְהַעֲמִיד מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו כָּרָאוּי, וְלֹא הוֹעִיל מֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּן הַשָּׁמַיִם הִטְרִידוּהוּ.
records.targetEnglish: It is difficult to understand such a statement about people of this greatness, particularly Rabbi Chiyya, of whom it is said that when he said ‘He causes the wind to blow,’ the wind blew. One may therefore interpret ‘I did not direct my heart’ to mean that he did not need to. Directing the heart applies to someone subject to imagination and thoughts, whose tongue speaks while his heart is elsewhere. He never needed this, for no other thing was in his thought: Hashem was before his eyes, and he always spoke as someone speaking before the King of kings. ‘One day I wanted to direct my heart’ means he then needed to because troubling thoughts had arisen; perhaps this was the occasion when Eliyahu disturbed them. Then he needed to direct his thoughts properly, but it did not help, since the disturbance had come from Heaven.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: A trained body can carry the bond into action
records.themeSummary: The spontaneous bow is understood as embodied service that has become established through practice.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef concludes its distinction between inward willingness and the body's training with the same Yerushalmi statement about the head bowing at Modim. The involuntary motion is thus not offered as a reason to dispense with service; it is the fruit of a bond carried into actual conduct. This clarifies why the present siman can recognize good in the head's response while still examining the other thoughts that accompanied the prayer.
records.originHebrew: וְהַמְקַנֵּא הֲרֵי חָסֵר וְאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל טוֹבוֹתָיו, אַדְּרַבָּה מִתְרָעֵם עַל שֶׁנּוֹתֵן טוֹבָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ.
records.originEnglish: and one who envies feels deficient and does not thank Hashem for His goodness, rather resenting that He bestows favor upon his fellow.
records.targetHebrew: וזה לעברך בברית ד' אלהיך ובאלתו, היינו שאם אתה בדעתך תהיה נקשר בהשי"ת, וגם בפעולה תקבל עליך יראת עונש, וממילא תהיה אתה נקשר בהשי"ת אפילו בפעולה ג"כ, שאפילו שלא מדעת תהיה אתה נמשך אחר רצון השי"ת, וכדאיתא בירושלמי (ברכות) בואו ונחזיק טיבותא לרישא דכד מטי למודים מנפשיה קא כרע:
records.targetEnglish: This is ‘to bring you into the covenant of Hashem your God and its oath’: if your understanding is bound to Hashem, and in actual conduct you also accept the awe of punishment, you will consequently be bound to Hashem in action as well. Even without conscious direction you will be drawn after His will. As the Yerushalmi says: Let us acknowledge the goodness of the head, for when it reaches Modim it bows of itself.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 7:12
records.themeTitle: The repair gives speech a worthy occupation
records.themeSummary: David's response to a generation of harmful speech was a tongue filled with songs and praise.
records.explanation: Ohr Zarua places David's covenant of speech beside Yosef's trial of covenantal purity. The positive content matters: David's tongue was filled with songs and praise. This illustrates the present siman's counsel to redirect the power of speech toward Torah rather than imagine that a person must have no use for speech at all. The corrective occupation reaches the faculty through which the person is being tested.
records.originHebrew: רַק עַל דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים יֵשׁ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (יט:). כִּי בְּדִבּוּר יֵשׁ מִצְוַת תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא תְּמִידִי: "לֹא יָמוּשׁ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ א, ח), וְיוּכַל לִהְיוֹת כָּל דִּבּוּרָיו תּוֹרָה;
records.originEnglish: Only regarding idle speech is there a positive and negative commandment, as written in Yoma 19b. For in speech exists the mitzvah of Torah study which is continuous: "it shall not depart, etc." (Joshua 1:8), and all of one's words can be Torah;
records.targetHebrew: וכמו שיוסף נתן במצרים ובבית אדונתו כדי לצרפו, כך דוד המלך עליו השלום נתן בדור המלא לשון הרע, כמו שאמרו זכרונם לברכה בירושלמי דפאה (פרק א׳ הלכה א׳) ובשוחר טוב על פסוק: "תשמרם מן הדור זו לעולם" [תהלים י״ב:ח׳], עין שם. והוא היה לשונו מלא שירות ותשבחות.
records.targetEnglish: Just as Yosef was placed in Egypt and in his mistress's house in order to refine him, so King David was placed in a generation full of harmful speech, as the Yerushalmi in Peah and Midrash Tehillim teach on ‘You will preserve them from this generation forever.’ His tongue, however, was filled with songs and praises.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Speech joins the heart's life to actual action
records.themeSummary: Spoken Torah can affect inward will because speech belongs to both inward life and bodily action.
records.explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains why the lips have a distinctive role: their movement is an action, while their speech emerges from the heart's living spirit. The same verse about righteous lips is therefore read as teaching and joining the will. This gives the present siman's counsel a precise structure; the learner speaks in order that mind and heart also become involved, rather than treating an utterance without any intention to change as sufficient.
records.originHebrew: וְכֵן בְּלָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה, כַּאֲשֶׁר מְקַיֵּים הָעֲשֵׂה דְּ"וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם" – תִּיקֵּן הַלָּאו דִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, וְהוּא מוֹעִיל גַּם כֵּן לְעִנְיַן מַחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי י, לב), שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר מוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו דְּבָרִים הַמְּצוּדָּקִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְלִבּוֹ בַּל עִמּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם יֵדְעוּן – מוֹדִיעִים וּמְלַמְּדִים רָצוֹן לַלֵּב, לִהְיוֹת רְצוֹן הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן. וְהָרָצוֹן מוֹלִיד מַחֲשָׁבָה, לִהְיוֹת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בָּזֶה לְבַד. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין נד.): "חַיִּים הֵם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כב) – לְמוֹצִיאֵיהֶם בַּפֶּה,
records.originEnglish: And so when one fulfills the positive command "and you shall speak of them," he rectifies the negative prohibition of idle speech, which avails likewise to heal idle thoughts. And as I heard on "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Proverbs 10:32): when one articulates righteous words with his lips, even if from the lip outward while his heart is not fully present, they inform and teach will to the heart, causing the heart's will to align with them in truth. And will generates thought, focusing his thoughts on this alone. And this is what they expounded (Eruvin 54b): "'they are life unto those that find them'—unto those who articulate them with the mouth,"
records.targetHebrew: ועל זה נאמר: ״כי קרוב אליך הדבר מאד בפיך ובלבבך לעשתו״ (שם ל:יד) ופה הוא הכולל ומחבר שניהם, דעקימת שפתיו הוי מעשה ועיקרו מרוח החיים שבלב, ותרגום ל״נפש חיה״ (בראשית ב:ז) — ״לרוח ממללא״, שהוא המחבר נפש ורוח ו״שפתי צדיק ידעון רצון״ (משלי י:לב) ו״ידעון״ לשון חיבור ודביקות, וגם לשון לימוד דעת להרצון שבלב שעל ידי הדבור פה הוא נכנס גם כן ללב, ואחר כך לעשותן
records.targetEnglish: It therefore says, ‘The matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.’ The mouth includes and joins the two: moving the lips is an action, while its essential source is the living spirit within the heart. ‘A living soul’ is translated as ‘a speaking spirit,’ joining nefesh and ruach. ‘The lips of the righteous know desire’ means connection and attachment, and also teaching understanding to the will within the heart. Through spoken words it enters the heart as well, and afterward is carried into action.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 16:1
records.themeTitle: The last point can disclose the purpose of the whole work
records.themeSummary: The six stages lead to a disclosure in which the lowest point is recognized as part of the original purpose.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim develops the same verse about the Hebrew servant's release. The movement through six stages culminates in recognizing divine kingship precisely where it had seemed absent. This explains the present siman's use of the seventh point as a return to freedom and Torah. The source's discussion of optional matzah after the first night is an analogy for that freedom; it does not make Shabbat observance optional.
records.originHebrew: וְיֵשׁ מִצְוֹת הַמּוֹעִילוֹת לְמִי שֶׁנִּפְסַק מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ, שֶׁגָּבְרוּ עָלָיו אֵיזֶה יָמִים מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֲבָלִים, וְנִיתַּק מִקְּבִיעוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּלֵּב
records.originEnglish: and there are commandments that are efficacious for one who has fallen away from his spiritual level, such that for several days vain and frivolous thoughts overwhelmed him, and he became detached from the permanent fixture of words of Torah within the heart –
records.targetHebrew: היינו כי כן הציב השי"ת רצון שכפי שאדם עובד ומצמצם א"ע מתתא לעילא שהם שית דרגין כן לעומת זה מנהיר לו השי"ת שית דרגין מעילא לתתא עד ובשביעית יצא לחפשי חנם שאין מהצורך לו עוד שום צמצום כי מאחר שצמצם עצמו האדם מצדו בנקודה האחרונה דלית בה עיינין ונראה שעולם כמנהגו נוהג והוא הכניס שם עיינין להכיר גם שם הנהגת מלכות שמים לעומת זה מנהיר השי"ת שזאת הנקודה האחרונה והנמוכה הוא עיקר התכלית וראשית המכוון מרצון השי"ת. וזו ההארה נקראת ובשביעית יצא לחפשי חנם
records.targetEnglish: Hashem established this order: according to the person's work and self-limitation from below to above through six levels, Hashem illuminates corresponding levels from above to below, until ‘in the seventh he goes free, without payment.’ Further constriction is no longer needed. The person had limited himself at the last point, where there are no eyes and the world appears merely to follow its course, and introduced eyes there to recognize the governance of Heaven. Correspondingly, Hashem shows that this last and lowest point is the chief purpose and original intention of His will. This illumination is called ‘in the seventh he goes free, without payment.’
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 8:3
records.themeTitle: A good act leaves more than a passing moment
records.themeSummary: What a person acquires through Torah and service retains a trace that can continue to act within him.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov explains the lasting trace of good service through the account of resurrection: the person rises with the Torah truly acquired through his own work. Its explicit statement that no good action, will or thought is lost gives depth to the siman's assertion that a deed generates a continuing spiritual power. This complements the present distinction between the influence of an angel and the felt contribution of a soul, without collapsing those two descriptions.
records.originHebrew: רמא] הַמִּצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁל הָאָדָם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מְבִיאִים בְּלִבּוֹ הִרְהוּרִים טוֹבִים, וְהַהֵיפוּךְ מֵעֲבֵירוֹת,
records.originEnglish: The commandments and good deeds of a person, and it goes without saying words of Torah, bring into his heart worthy ruminations; and conversely from transgressions,
records.targetHebrew: וזה הוא ענין תחיית המתים, שנשאר באדם הבלא דגרמי, כדאיתא בזוהר הקדוש (שלח קסט), והוא מזה שנקבע בגוף האדם דברי תורה אמיתיים כל חד כפום יסודא דיליה שקנה לעצמו ביגיע כפיו בעבודות וסבלנות, ובזה הכח יעורר אותו השם יתברך לתחיה. כי כל פעולה ורצון ומחשבה טובה צפון וגנוז אצל השם יתברך ולא יאבד שמץ מהם, וכדאיתא בזוהר הקדוש (תרומה קנ.) ולית רעותא טבא דיתאביד מקמי מלכא קדישא. ובזוהר הקדוש (משפטים ק:) אפילו הבל דפומא אתר ודוכתא אית ליה וכולי.
records.targetEnglish: This is the meaning of resurrection: a breath remains in the bones, as the Zohar teaches. It comes from the true Torah established within a person's body, each according to his own root, which he acquired through his labor, service and endurance. Through this power Hashem will awaken him to resurrection. Every good action, will and thought is stored and hidden with Hashem, and not the smallest part is lost. As the Zohar teaches, no good will is lost before the holy King; even the breath of the mouth has its particular place.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Deep damage does not exhaust the possibility of purification
records.themeSummary: The distinction among kinds of damage and repair retains a path of return even when all three lower levels are affected.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik states the distinction between the three impure shells and mixed nogah, then expressly preserves hope for the person who has damaged mind, heart and action. This helps the reader follow the present siman's several levels of repair without treating a limitation on one form of restoration as the end of all purification. The source reads the teaching about purifying a creeping creature allegorically; it does not alter that creature's halakhic status.
records.originHebrew: רַק מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה וּבְטֵילָה לְגַמְרֵי אוֹ לְתַאֲווֹת הֶיתֵּר וּרְשׁוּת, כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בִּפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים שַׁעַר קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁעַל הַמִּטָּה.
records.originEnglish: rather an alien and completely idle thought or toward permissible and mundane desires, as is known from the Ari of blessed memory in Pri Etz Chayyim, Sha'ar Kriyat Shema She'al HaMitah.
records.targetHebrew: והנה אם פגם האדם וקילקל גם בג' בחי' שלו היינו במוחו ולבו וכלי המעשר שהמה מבחי' נר"נ בכל השבע מדות הק' שיש בכל אחד מזוקק שבעתים היינו מ"ט שערים בכל אחד עכ"ז יש לו עוד תקוה להטהר ע"י התשובה מעומקא דלבא שהוא שער החמשים שיש בכל אחד. וזהו שרמזו חז"ל בגמ' הנ"ל בתלמידו של ר"מ שהי' יכול לטהר השרץ שהוא מרמז על ג' קליפות הטמאות בכלל גם אם נטמא האדם ח"ו בכולם ביכלתו אעפ"כ ליטהר ע"י שער החמשים שיש בכל אחד. וזהו הפי' בק"ן טעמים היינו בג' שערי החמשים שיש תקוה מכל השלש קליפות ליטהר.
records.targetEnglish: Even if a person has damaged and corrupted his three levels—mind, heart and organs of action, corresponding to nefesh, ruach and neshamah—within all seven holy qualities, the forty-nine gates in each, he still has hope of purification through repentance from the depth of the heart, the fiftieth gate within each. The Sages alluded to this in the disciple of Rabbi Meir who could purify the creeping creature: it symbolizes the three impure shells together. Even if a person has become impure through them all, Heaven forbid, he can nevertheless be purified through the fiftieth gate within each. This explains the hundred and fifty reasons: the three fiftieth gates, through which there is hope of purification from all three shells.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The lower disclosure and the hidden root are not separate
records.themeSummary: The different levels of recognition concern one divine reality disclosed in different ways.
records.explanation: Divrei Chalomot interprets ‘I am He and no other’ through the same vocabulary of the lowest indwelling disclosure and the highest hidden root. Its conclusion guards the present hierarchy from being mistaken for separate divine sources. The difference belongs to how the person apprehends the presence, while the reality recognized at the root remains one.
records.originHebrew: זֶה הוּא כְּבָר נוֹשָׁע בִּישׁוּעָה שְׁלֵימָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הָאֵר פָּנֶיךָ וְנִוָּשֵׁעָה" (תְּהִלִּים פ, ד). כִּי מְעַט מִן הָאוֹר דּוֹחֶה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
records.originEnglish: This person is already redeemed with complete salvation, and as it is written: 'Cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved' (Psalms 80:4). For a little bit of light dispels much darkness,
records.targetHebrew: פעם אחת ביום טוב ראשון של פסח חלם לי פרוש לשון ההגדה: "אני הוא ולא אחר": רצה לומר דרגא ד"אני", שהוא מדרגה היותר תחתונה, סוד השכינה [השוכן בתוך הלבבות דבני ישראל עד שיכול לומר בשם ה' לשון "אני"] כנודע, הוא עצמו דרגא ד"הוא", שהוא מדרגה היותר עליונה הנעלמת, סוד כתר עליון [ובזהר הקדוש פרשת קרח קע״ח ריש עמוד ב׳: "הוא" — דא עתיקא, שלמעלה מקומת אדם והשגתו בחכמה שבמחו, דעל זה אמרו: "במפלא ממך וגומר" כידוע], ואינו דבר אחר, רק הכל אחד
records.targetEnglish: Once, on the first festival day of Pesach, I dreamed an explanation of the Haggadah's words, ‘I am He and no other.’ The level called ‘I’ is the lowest level, the secret of the Shechinah dwelling within Israel's hearts. It is itself the level called ‘He,’ the highest hidden level, the secret of the supernal crown. The Zohar calls ‘He’ Atika, beyond the human stature and intellectual grasp. It is not another thing; all is one.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 1
records.themeTitle: The acquired Torah can rekindle its own desire
records.themeSummary: The relation between longing and wisdom runs in both directions.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach first describes silver as longing that acquires the gold of Torah. Its later reversal explains why the acquired Torah must itself kindle further longing as the person's natural energy changes. This develops the siman's account of a power impressed on possessions into a reciprocal process: the desire seeks wisdom, and the wisdom received can renew that desire. The siman's opening condition concerning divine judgment remains in force.
records.originHebrew: וּלְכָךְ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דִּבְיָמָיו סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא וְלֹא הָיָה שׁוּם מוֹנֵעַ, נֶאֱמַר: "כִּכְלוֹת וְגוֹמֵר כָּל חֵשֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹה וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א ט, א), שֶׁכָּל חֶשְׁקוֹ הָיָה נִשְׁלָם וּמוּבָא לוֹ.
records.originEnglish: Therefore regarding King Solomon, in whose days the moon was full and there was no obstacle, it is said: 'When Solomon had finished... all the desire of Solomon, etc.' (I Kings 9:1), for his entire desire was completed and delivered unto him.
records.targetHebrew: אבל בזקנה צריך האדם לבקש שלא יוסר ממנו החשק לדברי תורה, כי לעת הזקנה כל כחות התשוקה של האדם מתחלשין, על כן שינה לו הזהב קונה את הכסף, והוא תפלה שהתפלל להשם שעל ידי דברי תורה יבא בלבו חשק להוספת עוד דברי תורה, והוא למשל לאדם ששבע מאכילה ואף על פי כן אם בא לפניו מאכל טוב המאכל הזה ממשיך לו תאוה וחשק לאכול יותר, וכן הוא הענין בדברי תורה. וזה שאנו מתפללין בכל יום, והערב נא השם אלקינו את דברי תורתך בפינו, היינו שימתקו לנו הדברי תורה, שיהיה לנו בכל פעם תשוקה יותר אליהם. וזה פירוש הפסוק (יואל בית, כף ואו) "ואכלתם אכול ושבוע" וכפילת הלשון מורה על זה, דעל ידי האכילה יבא לך חמדה יותר והוא למשל לדברי תורה כמו שנתבאר.
records.targetEnglish: In old age a person must ask that his longing for Torah not depart, since the powers of desire weaken. Rabbi therefore changed the teaching to ‘gold acquires silver’: he prayed that through Torah a longing for still more Torah should enter his heart. It resembles someone already satisfied by food who is offered a good dish that awakens further appetite. So it is with Torah. We therefore pray daily, ‘Make the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths,’ so that their sweetness awakens ever more longing. This explains ‘You shall eat, eating and being satisfied’: the doubled expression indicates that the eating itself brings further desire, as an image for Torah.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: A holy root does not settle every use of severity
records.themeSummary: The right person, occasion and measure remain necessary even where severity has a place in service.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik distinguishes Moshe's slight lapse into anger from the particular zeal fitting to Pinchas. This is an important qualification beside the present account of Gilead and Ahab's attempt to vindicate his use of force: recognizing that severity can have a holy root does not by itself establish that a given act expresses it. The distinction is consistent with the siman's opening condition that desire's force remains subject to judgment.
records.originHebrew: אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה יא.): בִּקְדֵירָה שֶׁבִּשְּׁלוּ וְכוּלֵי,
records.originEnglish: our Sages of blessed memory explained (Sotah 11a): in the pot wherein they cooked, etc.,
records.targetHebrew: וגם בבחינת הכעס היה משה רבינו ע"ה נקי מכל נדנוד ושמץ מנהו לכן בפרשה זו כאשר נראה על הגוון ממנו מעט קפידא ויצא מגדרו במשהו שנאמר ויקצוף משה וגו' נתעלמה ממנו הלכה דייקא בגיעולי מדין ובזה הראו לו שצריך להזהר בזה אפילו בדקות מאוד כענין שנצרך טהרה וטבילה אפילו הכלי שהיה רק איזה שעות ברשות הנכרי. ובמעשה זמרי הראו לו שלפעמים לאיזה צורך נצרך דייקא להשתמש במדת הכעס וקנאה לכן נתעלמה ממנו הלכה זו דקנאין פוגעין בו מפני שהדבר הזה לקנאות אין שייכות כלל אליו רק בא פנחס ונטל את הראוי לו.
records.targetEnglish: Moshe was clean of every trace of anger. Therefore, when even a slight strictness appeared and he went a little beyond his boundary, ‘Moshe became angry,’ the law concerning Midian's absorbed forbidden matter was specifically hidden from him. He was shown the need for care even in the finest degree, like a vessel requiring purification even after only a few hours in another's possession. In Zimri's case he was shown that a particular need can sometimes require anger and zeal. That law was hidden from him because this act of zeal did not belong to his particular service; Pinchas came and took the role fitting to him.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Equal belonging and different measures of striving
records.themeSummary: The equal contributions mark the common root and end; the varied contribution concerns work within concealment.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef distinguishes the same three contributions. The sockets signify the equality reached after clarification, and the public offerings the common root before individual service. The freely given Mishkan contribution concerns the intervening work of breaking through concealment. This makes the siman's contrast precise: different intensity of longing describes the person's present reception without cancelling Israel's shared foundation or eventual equality.
records.originHebrew: וְיֵשׁ עוֹד תְּרוּמַת הָאֲדָנִים וּדְקָרְבָּנוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ: "הֶעָשִׁיר לֹא יַרְבֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת ל, טו), שֶׁבֵּין הֶעָשִׁיר בְּדַעַת וּבְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְתִגְבּוֹרֶת הַחֵשֶׁק, וּבֵין הֶעָנִי – שָׁוִים בַּחֲלָקִים; כִּי הוּא "לְכַפֵּר עַל נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם" כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב, וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד): דִּלְכַפֵּר אַעֵגֶל; פֵּירוּשׁ: לְקַנֵּחַ לִכְלוּךְ דְּחֶשְׁקוֹת רָעוֹת מִן הַלֵּב. וְכֵן בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פִּינְחָס): "תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר מְכַפֵּר וְכוּלֵי"; וּבְעִנְיַן הַרְחָקָה מִן הָרַע כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁוִים, שֶׁכֻּלָּם יוּכְלוּ לִינָּקוֹת מִן הָרַע בְּתַכְלִית, רַק חִלּוּק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוּא בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַטּוֹב.
records.originEnglish: And there is furthermore the offering of the sockets and of the communal sacrifices, concerning which it is said: 'The rich shall not give more, etc.' (Exodus 30:15), wherein both the one rich in understanding, emotional perception, and surging desire, and the poor man—are entirely equal in their shares; because it is 'to make atonement for your souls,' as explicitly stated in Scripture, and as our Sages of blessed memory stated in the Yerushalmi, Shekalim (2:4): that it comes to atone for the Golden Calf; meaning: to wipe away the filth of wicked desires from the heart. And so regarding communal offerings our Sages said (Midrash Rabbah, Pinchas): 'The morning continual offering atones, etc.'; and regarding distancing from evil all Israel are equal, in that all are capable of being thoroughly cleansed from evil, the variance in spiritual levels applying only to the attainment of the good.
records.targetHebrew: תרומת האדנים מורה כמו שמצינו (סנהדרין צ'.) כל ישראל יש להם חלק לעולם הבא. והיינו שלעתיד אחר הבירור, אז כל ישראל יהיו בשוה, ולזה היה התרומה הזאת כל אחד בשוה, כי בזה לא שייך שום יתרון אחד על חבירו. ותרומת המזבח מורה על ישראל עלה במחשבה תחלה, ובזה ג"כ לא שייך שום יתרון אחד על חבירו, כי שם כל ישראל בשוה, ולפיכך גם התרומה הזאת היה כל אחד נדבתו שוה. ותרומת המשכן מורה מה שכל אחד בוקע את ההסתר להיות השי"ת שוכן אצלו. וזה מורה מן ישראל עלה במחשבה תחלה עד כל ישראל יש להם חלק לעולם הבא, שאדם צריך לברר עצמו על מה בחר בו השי"ת בהתחלה קודם עבודתו. ועל מה השי"ת קובע את הדברי תורה אצלו בקביעות, לזה היה התרומה הזאת איש אשר ידבנו לבו, את זה הציב השי"ת לפום צערא אגרא, היינו עד כמה שאדם בוקע את ההסתר כן שוכן השי"ת אצלו בקביעות.
records.targetEnglish: The contribution for the sockets indicates what we find: all Israel have a share in the World to Come. After the clarification, all Israel will be equal, so this contribution was equal; no one has an advantage over another in this. The altar contribution indicates that Israel arose first in divine thought; there too all are equal. The Mishkan contribution indicates how each person breaks through concealment so that Hashem dwells with him. Between the first choice of Israel and their share in the World to Come, a person must clarify why Hashem chose him before his service and why He establishes Torah with him permanently. Therefore this contribution is according to the willing heart: according to the effort is the reward. To the extent that a person breaks through concealment, Hashem dwells with him permanently.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The two unifications describe two recognitions
records.themeSummary: Unity is apprehended as the one presence and as the kingship acknowledged by distinct creatures.
records.explanation: Dover Tzedek supplies a complementary definition of the terms used here. Upper unity recognizes that no place is empty of the divine presence; lower unity recognizes His kingship through the powers that appear distinct. The present siman applies these recognitions to the movement between received wisdom and the willing heart. Its later insistence on the actual limits of bodily action remains part of that account.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה סוֹד יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה הַנִּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם (קלד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב). דְּזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי" (פְּסָחִים נו.), דְּיִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה בְּלֵב יַעֲקֹב, וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה בְּלֵב בָּנָיו. פֵּירוּשׁ: יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה – דְּ"גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ", וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלָה וְהָרֵאשִׁית, וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל", דְּצָרִיךְ לָזֶה שְׁמִיעָה וְקַבָּלָה: אַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַשָּׂגַת אֱלֹהוּת תֵּדַע דַּ"ה' אֶחָד", וְגַם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתְךָ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.originEnglish: And this is the mystery of the Higher Unity and Lower Unity mentioned in the Zohar, see there (134b). For this is what the brothers said: 'Just as there is in your heart only One, etc.' (Pesachim 56a), the Higher Unity being in Jacob's heart, and the Lower Unity in the hearts of his sons. The explanation is: the Higher Unity affirms that 'all our works You have wrought for us', and this is the outset and the beginning; and concerning this Scripture states: 'Hear, O Israel', for this requires attentive hearing and acceptance: you, Israel, who exerts yourself in striving to perceive divinity— know that 'Hashem is One', and your very exertion originates from Hashem.
records.targetHebrew: וְהֵן הֵם שְׁנֵי יִחוּדִים: עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה, דִּ"שְׁמַע" וּ"בָרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳, דַּף רס״ד עַמּוּד א׳): דִּ"שְׁמַע" הוּא אַחְדוּת מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁמְּלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ וְלֵית אֲתַר פָּנוּי מִינֵּיהּ בְּכָל גּוּפִים וּבְרוּאִים, זֶהוּ יִחוּד עֶלְיוֹן וּ"בָרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד" הוּא יִחוּד תַּתָּאָה בְּמַדְרֵגַת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁאֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם וְיֵשׁ כֹּחוֹת נִפְרָדִים, רַק שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם כְּהוֹרָאַת שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים, וְהוּא אָדוֹן וּמֶלֶךְ לָהֶם
records.targetEnglish: These are the two unifications, upper and lower, of ‘Shema’ and ‘Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever.’ The Zohar explains that Shema is actual unity: the whole earth is filled with His glory, and no place in any bodies or creatures is empty of Him. This is upper unity. ‘Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever’ is lower unity, at the level of His kingship: there is no king without a people, and there are distinct powers, but He is the master of them all, as the name Elokim indicates, and He is their lord and king.

records.themeTitle: Why the Kohen Gadol prays for Judah
records.themeSummary: The inward service reaches Israel through a living common root.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim explains the precise prayer quoted here: Judah is the common root, so blessing the root sustains the branches. The surrounding discussion says that the Kohen Gadol's inward service must be followed by prayer that the light become perceptible in ordinary human life. This clarifies why the siman places the Kohen Gadol and the prayer for kingship together within the sanctity of a particular soul, whose service bears upon the whole people.
records.originHebrew: וּבַמָּקוֹם: יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם; וַעֲזָרוֹת – נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַן הַנִּבְנֶה עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ; וְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים – נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וּבוֹ אֵין נִכְנָס אֶלָּא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, נֶפֶשׁ מְיוּחָד, וּמְבַקֵּשׁ: "לָא יַעֲדֵי עָבֵיד שׁוּלְטָן מִדְּבֵית יְהוּדָה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא נג:) גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַּׁת נֶפֶשׁ, וְנִבְנֶה עַל יְדֵי "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ", כְּטַעַם: "יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים" (בְּרָכוֹת ל.),
records.originEnglish: And in space: Jerusalem embodies the sanctity of space; and the Temple Courtyards correspond to the sanctity of time, built through the sacrificial services conducted therein; and the Holy of Holies corresponds to the sanctity of the soul, wherein none enters except the High Priest, a unique soul, who prays: 'May rulership not depart from the house of Judah' (Yoma 53b), which likewise pertains to the sanctity of the soul, and is constructed through 'with all your heart', mirroring: 'He shall direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies' (Berakhot 30a),
records.targetHebrew: כי זאת התפלה שלא יעדי עביד שולטן מבית יהודה הוא ג"כ מכוון כזה כמו שאמר אאמו"ר הגה"ק זצללה"ה שהתפלל להשי"ת שישגיח תמיד ביחוד על השורש ושבט יהודה הוא שורש החיים מכל ישראל וממילא כשיתברך השורש לא יהיה נחסר ברכה להענפים ג"כ
records.targetEnglish: The prayer that the rule of authority not depart from the house of Judah has this same intention. My holy father explained that he prayed to Hashem to attend continually and especially to the root. The tribe of Judah is the root of the life of all Israel; when the root is blessed, blessing will consequently not be lacking for the branches either.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:27
records.themeTitle: A desire whose proper object has no end
records.themeSummary: The impulse to seek ever more finds a positive use in Torah.
records.explanation: Dover Tzedek identifies the proper use of a desire that is never satisfied: increasing in Torah. This helps explain why the siman relates endless longing to teshuvah and to never considering oneself complete. The constructive direction is renewed attachment and growth; the cited paragraph does not make committing a transgression a method of acquiring that growth.
records.originHebrew: וְהַתְחָלָה זוֹ הוּא גֶּדֶר "טוֹב מְאֹד" כַּאֲשֶׁר מוֹשְׁכוֹ לְעִנְיַן חֶשְׁקוֹת דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מַדְרֵגַת: "אוֹהֵב כֶּסֶף] לֹא יִשְׂבַּע כֶּסֶף]" (מַכּוֹת י:). וְהַנִּסָּיוֹן הוּא הַבֵּירוּר שֶׁכְּבָר הוּא מְבוֹרָר וּבְתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת, וְאִם כֵּן הוּא שְׂבִיעָה שֶׁכְּבָר שָׁלֵם; אֲבָל זֶה אֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה וְהוּא חָסֵר לְעוֹלָם.  וּלְכָךְ הוּא הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מוֹעֵד קָטָן טז:), כִּי לְהַשִּׂיג בְּכָל פַּעַם יוֹתֵר וְשֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם עַל הַשְּׁלֵימוּת הוּא רַק בְּדַרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה;
records.originEnglish: And this inception is defined as 'very good' when one channels it toward desires for Hashem, blessed be He, on the level of: 'He that loves Torah/silver shall not be satisfied with it' (Ecclesiastes 5:9; Makkot 10a). And a trial serves as clarification that one is already refined and in complete perfection, and if so, it implies satiety, having achieved completeness; yet this desire knows no satiety and remains forever yearning.  Therefore David established the yoke of repentance (Moed Katan 16b), for to attain ever greater heights each time and never rest in static perfection belongs solely to the spiritual plane of repentance;
records.targetHebrew: [דַּף ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳] "לֹא חָסִיד אֲנִי" וְכוּלֵי פֵּרוּשׁ: "חָסִיד" הוּא הַנִּבְדָּל מִקִּנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה, וְכָבוֹד, שֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין [אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם] וּכְנֶגְדָּן שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁהָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד כִּי תוֹרָה הִיא תִּקּוּן לְתַאֲוָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְעֵץ חַיִּים תַּאֲוָה בָאָה" כִּי תַּאֲוָה — דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רוֹצֶה יוֹתֵר — עִקָּרָהּ נִבְרְאָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת דַּף י׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "אֹהֵב כֶּסֶף [לֹא יִשְׂבַּע כָּסֶף]" וְכוּלֵי וּכְשֶׁמֵּשִׂים תַּאֲוָתוֹ בָּהּ, נִיצָּל מִתַּאֲוַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (סוֹף הִלְכוֹת אִסּוּרֵי בִּיאָה): כִּי לֹא תִּמְצָא תַּאֲוָה אֶלָּא בְּלֵב פָּנוּי מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
records.targetEnglish: “Am I not devoted?” A devoted person is separated from envy, desire and honor, which take a person out of the world. Corresponding to them are the three things on which the world stands. Torah repairs desire, as in “a tree of life is a desire fulfilled.” Desire—the condition of always wanting more than one has—was principally created for Torah, as the Sages interpreted “one who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver.” When a person places his desire in Torah, he is saved from worldly desires. Rambam writes that desire is found only in a heart empty of Torah.
