records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 1
records.themeTitle: A particular account of Judah and David
records.themeSummary: Ishbitz contrasts the rigor demanded of Yosef with the particular divine vindication of Judah.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach discusses the same words, “so that You be justified,” through the contrast between Yosef and Judah. It first stresses that Yosef was given the power to overcome his desire and was therefore judged with exceptional rigor; only then does it discuss the distinct account of Judah. This provides context for Rav Tzadok's difficult conclusion about David. Both are particular expositions of these figures and their divine clarification, rather than a general instruction to choose sin or dispense with the restraint demanded at the siman's opening.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה טַעַם טַעֲנָתוֹ: "לְמַעַן תִּצְדַּק בְּדָבְרֶךָ" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ו), כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קז.), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא חָטָא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָרָאוּי נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רַק יִהְיֶה תָּמִיד מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק וְעֵינָיו צוֹפִיּוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲזוֹר לוֹ, וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁזָּכָה בָּהּ.
records.originEnglish: And this is the meaning of his plea: 'That You may be justified when You speak' (Psalms 51:6), as our Sages of blessed memory explained (Sanhedrin 107a), namely that he fell so as not to remain in static perfection before Hashem, but rather be constantly yearning with eyes gazing toward Hashem to help him; and this is the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty) which he merited.
records.targetHebrew: ויהודא הוא נגד שר המשקה כי דוד המלך עליו השלום נקרא בדחנא דמלכא (זוהר שמות קוף זין עמוד אלף) ועל ניסוך היין נשמעין שירי דוד, ובאמת ליהודא במעשה דתמר וכן בכל המעשים משבט יהודא הדומין לזה נתן בהם השם יתברך כח התאוה כל כך עד שלא היה באפשרותם להתגבר וכמו שמבואר (בראשית רבה פרשה פא הא, טית) שמלאך הממונה על התאוה הכריחו, ולכן לא עליו האשם במה שלא היה יכול להתגבר על יצרו, וזה פירוש בדחנא דמלכא היינו שמניח את עצמו להנצח מהשם יתברך כמו שאמר דוד המלך עליו השלום (תהלים נון אלף, ואו) "למען תצדק בדבריך" למי נאה שיוצדק אני או אתה.
records.targetEnglish: Judah corresponds to the cupbearer, for David is called the King's entertainer, and David's songs are heard over the wine libation. In Judah's act with Tamar and the similar acts of his tribe, Hashem placed in them such a power of desire that they were unable to overcome it, as the Midrash explains that the angel appointed over desire compelled him. He is therefore not held guilty for what he could not overcome. This is the meaning of the King's entertainer: he allows himself to be overcome by Hashem. As David said, “So that You be justified in Your words”: whom does it befit to be justified, me or You?
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The Night of Shabbat Chol HaMoed Pesach 16:1
records.themeTitle: Teaching as generosity of eye
records.themeSummary: The wish to teach is a wish that Torah's light reach another person.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim distinguishes giving light from withholding it, even when both may outwardly be called “free.” This illuminates the siman's explanation of the request “to learn and teach”: the desired good is that another receive what one knows and be able to stand equally. It is this generosity, rather than the pursuit of the status of a teacher, that reverses narrowness of eye.
records.originHebrew: וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כד.): "עֵילָם זָכְתָה לִלְמוֹד וְלֹא לְלַמֵּד". פֵּירוּשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "לִלְמוֹד וּלְלַמֵּד", דְּאֵיךְ מְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רַב? רַק רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן שֶׁאַחֵר יֵדַע גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ וְיִהְיֶה כְּמוֹתוֹ. וְעֵילָם לֹא זָכָה לְלַמֵּד, שֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ לְטוֹבַת עַיִן כָּזֶה
records.originEnglish: And so it appears from what is written in Sanhedrin (24a): “Elam (Persia) merited to learn, but not to teach.” The explanation is as I heard concerning “to learn and to teach,” how can a person pray to become a master over others? Rather, it means to say: that he should possess a generous, good eye so that another will also know what he knows and become like him. And Elam did not merit to teach, because they did not merit such a generous eye
records.targetHebrew: שמן תורק שמך וגו' היינו שדברי תורה המה תמיד בגודל נדיבות ומבקשים תמיד למסור א"ע להלב נקי של ישראל כדכתיב ובלא מחיר יין וחלב ההיפך מסטרא אחרא שהוא בצרות עין מאוד אף שס"א נקראים ג"כ חנם כדאיתא בזוה"ק (בהר ק"ח.) כתיב זכרנו את הדגה אשר נאכל במצרים חנם. בלא ברכה. דלא הוה עלנא במצרים עול דלעילא וכו' אכן זאת בעצמו שהס"א חפצה להסתיר את האור למען שיהי' הויות הבריאה בחושך אין לך צרות עין יותר מזה אבל ד"ת מנהיר תמיד את אורה בגודל נדיבות.
records.targetEnglish: “Your name is oil poured out”: words of Torah are always greatly generous and seek to give themselves to Israel's pure heart, as in “wine and milk without price.” This is the opposite of the other side, which is extremely narrow of eye. Though it too is called “free,” as the Zohar interprets the fish eaten in Egypt without blessing or the higher yoke, its wish to hide the light and leave creation in darkness is the greatest narrowness of eye. Torah, however, continually shines its light with great generosity.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Protective repentance concerns the person needing repair
records.themeSummary: The same act can require extra personal restraint when it revives a particular defect.
records.explanation: Takanat HaShavin names the precise category used here: teshuvat ha-geder, repentance through a protective boundary, with the same examples of gambling and lending. This explains why the siman distinguishes this person from someone else for whom the act could be a mitzvah. Its explicit condition remains essential: the proposed abstention must not itself involve a transgression. The note concerns the extra boundary needed for repair, rather than a general cancellation of obligations.
records.originHebrew: בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָאָדָם חָסֵר בּוֹ וְצָרִיךְ תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי הִתְנַהֲגוּת בַּהֵיפֶךְ, הוּא אֲפִילּוּ בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה אֵצֶל אָדָם אַחֵר מִצְוָה, כִּדְשָׁמְעִינַן (סַנְהֶדְרִין כה:) בְּמַלְוֶה בְּרִבִּית דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְעַכּוּ״ם לֹא, הֲגַם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִצְוָה דְּ"לַנָּכְרִי תַשִּׁיךְ", כָּל שֶׁאֵין עֲבֵירָה בִּמְנִיעָתוֹ צָרִיךְ לִמְנוֹעַ.
records.originEnglish: In a matter where a person is deficient and requires rectification by means of behaving in the opposite extreme, this applies even in a situation that would be considered a mitzvah for someone else, just as we learn (Sanhedrin 25b) regarding one who lends on interest that even to a gentile he may not lend on interest, even though there is a mitzvah that "to a foreigner you may lend on interest" (Deuteronomy 23:21), as long as there is no active transgression in withholding it, he must withhold.
records.targetHebrew: ו״תשובת הגדר״ הגם דהוא לא מייתי מגמרא, הוא מבואר בפרק ״זה בורר״ (סנהדרין כ״ה עמוד ב׳) במשחקי בקוביא דאפילו בחנם לא עבדי, ומלוה ברבית אפילו לגוי לא מלוה, ומפריחי יונים אפילו במדבר לא עבדי, עיין שם
records.targetEnglish: Protective repentance, although he does not cite it from the Gemara, is explained in “This One Selects”: dice players do not play even without stakes; an interest lender does not lend even to a non-Jew; and pigeon racers do not do it even in the wilderness. See there.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The timing of the inner clarification matters
records.themeSummary: The rescue disclosed an inward attachment that had not been evident during concealment.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim places an explicit limit on retrospective recognition: only after Hashem opened the deliverance did they know clearly that their outward act had not severed the inward bond. Beforehand, they feared that they had become estranged. This sharpens the siman's movement from hidden loyalty to visible rescue and guards against treating a person's advance assertion of a hidden good intention as the same thing as that later clarification.
records.originHebrew: וְהוּא מַבִּיט רַק עַל הַנִּגְלֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵשָׂו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה): "פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְכוּלֵי", וְהַנִּגְלֶה רַע. אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת "אִם יִסָּתֵר וְגוֹמֵר וַאֲנִי לֹא אֶרְאֶנּוּ", וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ הַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים.
records.originEnglish: And he gazes exclusively upon what is external, as written concerning Esau (Bereishit Rabbah 65): "he spreads out his split hooves, etc.," and the outward appearance was evil. Yet in truth: "Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him?" (Jeremiah 23:24), and afterward all the ends of the earth witnessed their inward holiness, seeing that in truth they had acted only outwardly.
records.targetHebrew: כי מה שנתברר שהם לא עשו אלא לפנים זה הבירור נתוודע להם אחר שפתח השי"ת את הישועה אבל טרם הישועה הי' נדמה להם שנתרחקו ח"ו לגמרי כי בירור כזה א"א כי אם אחר הישועה
records.targetEnglish: The clarification that they had acted only outwardly became known to them after Hashem opened the deliverance. Before the deliverance, it seemed to them that they had become entirely estranged, Heaven forbid; such a clarification is possible only after the deliverance.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:38
records.themeTitle: Bodily reception can join spiritual reception
records.themeSummary: Adar and Nissan illustrate the mutual need of body and soul.
records.explanation: Likkutei Maamarim develops the same contrast between the letters qof and he through bodily and spiritual reception. It explains that the body can share in holiness through its bond with the soul, while the soul becomes manifest in this world through the body. This helps explain why the siman proceeds from suppressing desire to transforming permissible enjoyment for holiness. The two passages use different tribal associations in developing their particular arguments; the comparison concerns the reception and body/soul structure.
records.originHebrew: רַק בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם הַקּוֹ״ף מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת, וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר הִתְגַּלּוּת הַהֵ״א, תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אָז גַּם הֲנָאַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.  וְזֶה טַעַם הַכְלָלַת קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה לִפְעָמִים כַּיָּדוּעַ, דְּאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים הוּא קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, הֲגַם דִּלְפָנִים הוּא חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אֵין נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בְּחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל, וּמַה שֶּׁלּוֹקֵחַ מֵחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק לְתַשְׁמִישׁ דִּקְדוּשָׁה.
records.originEnglish: Yet in truth, the letter Kuf is likewise among the holy letters, and that is attained after the disclosure of the Hei, the sheer intensity of longing for Hashem, blessed be He; then even the worldly enjoyment of the Jewish people is consecrated unto Hashem.  And this explains why the shell of Nogah is sometimes subsumed into holiness, as is known, for the wayward woman represents the shell of Nogah; even though outwardly it looks like mundane pleasure, nonetheless at the inner root no Jewish soul is attached to worldly desire at all, and whatever he partakes of physical pleasure is solely for holy usage.
records.targetHebrew: אולם בקדושה הוא נגד נפתלי המחבר כל ישראל יחד; ואדר הוא סמוך לניסן, כי בישראל הקו"ף רומז "קדוש", שיש גם בגוף קדושה על ידי התחברותו עם הנפש, שעיקרה הוא כח החכמה, כידוע דנפשות ישראל הם מאותיות התורה. והם ששים רבוא נפשות דדור המדבר, ונפשות שאר הדורות הם מהתחדשות תורה שבעל פה שבאותו הדור; ועל כן עיקר קבלת העבור האמיתי מצד הנפש החיה הוא באות הה"א דניסן; אבל אות קו"ף הרומז לעבור גופני ישנו גם באמות העולם; אלא דבישראל קבלתם העבור הוא רק מהשם יתברך, ואין עבור גופני בלא עבור רוחני כלל, ושניהם צריכים זה לזה, כמו שאמרו זכרונם לברכה בפרק חלק (סנהדרין צא:) במשל דגוף ונפש באים לדין לענש, וכן לענין השכר. וחיות הגוף הוא הנפש, והתגלות ביאת הנפש לעולם הזה הוא על ידי הגוף; וכן ביאת ניסן בזמן אביב הוא על ידי עבור אדר.
records.targetEnglish: Within holiness this corresponds to Naftali, who joins all Israel, and Adar stands beside Nissan. In Israel, qof hints at “holy”: the body too has holiness through its connection with the soul, whose principal power is wisdom. Israel's souls derive from the letters of Torah. These are the six hundred thousand souls of the wilderness generation; the souls of other generations derive from the renewed Oral Torah of their own generation. The true reception of new life on the soul's side is therefore in the he of Nissan. The qof of bodily reception exists also among the nations, but Israel receives from Hashem, and bodily reception is never without spiritual reception. Both need one another, as the Sages' parable of body and soul explains regarding judgment, and likewise reward. The soul is the body's life, while the soul's manifestation in this world is through the body. So too Nissan comes in the spring through Adar's intercalation.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The remaining impulse can deepen the praise
records.themeSummary: The person acknowledges unity while bodily desire still remains.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik explains the same images of a little leaven and a little foolishness through the quietly spoken declaration of lower unity. The added praise comes from recognizing Hashem while an opposing impulse remains, rather than from expanding that impulse. This fits the siman's own qualification that the remaining foolishness should be as little as possible, and its turn toward blessing over permissible enjoyment.
records.originHebrew: וְאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת לד.): "שְׂאוֹר, רוּבּוֹ קָשֶׁה וּמִיעוּטוֹ יָפֶה", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל יוֹתָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב כז, ב): "רַק לֹא בָא אֶל הֵיכַל ה' וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁזֶּה נֶאֱמַר לְחִסָּרוֹן עָלָיו, לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן כְּלָל. וּבֶאֱמֶת נֶאֱמַר: "יָקָר מֵחָכְמָה וּמִכָּבוֹד סִכְלוּת מְעָט", דְּצָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּכָל אֶחָד סִכְלוּת מְעַט עַל כָּל פָּנִים, וְזֶהוּ הַשְּׁלֵימוּת. רַק שֶׁזֶּה טוֹב לָאָדָם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אוֹתוֹ הַסִּכְלוּת כַּמִּיעוּט הַיּוֹתֵר אֶפְשָׁרִי. וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (ר״ג עַמּוּד ב): "דְּנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב וְלָא לְאַנְהָגָא בֵּיהּ קְלָנָא", כִּי "יִתְרוֹן אֶרֶץ בַּכֹּל הוּא", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "אֲפִילּוּ וְכוּלֵי" (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כב). כִּי מִכָּל דָּבָר יֵשׁ יִתְרוֹן בֶּאֱמֶת, וְגַם מִצַּד הָרַע עַל יְדֵי הַקִּילוּס וְהַהוֹדָאָה הָעוֹלָה מִכּוּלּוֹ, וְ"כָל עַצְמוֹתַי תֹּאמַרְנָה ה' וְגוֹמֵר", בָּזֶה נִתְעַלֶּה הַכֹּל. וּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ נִכְלֶלֶת בִּקְדוּשָׁה עַל יְדֵי הַבְּרָכָה וְהַהוֹדָאָה עַל כָּל הֲנָאַת הָרְשׁוּת, כִּי הֵם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.originEnglish: And they taught (Berakhot 34a): "Leaven: too much is harmful, but a little is beneficial," and as I heard concerning Jotham of whom it is written (II Chronicles 27:2): "only he did not enter the temple of Hashem, etc.," that this was stated as a critique against him, indicating that he had no human flaw whatever. And in truth Scripture declares: "A little folly is more precious than wisdom and honor" (Ecclesiastes 10:1), for each person must contain at least a measure of folly, and this constitutes true wholeness. Only that it is good for man that this folly be kept to the smallest possible minimum. Therefore it is stated in Zohar Vayakhel (203b): "and a brightness (Nogah) was round about it, and one must not treat it with contempt," for "the advantage of the earth is in all things" (Ecclesiastes 5:8), and the Sages expounded: "even creatures that appear useless, etc." (Vayikra Rabbah 22). For from everything there is indeed an ultimate advantage, even from the side of evil through the praise and thanksgiving arising from the whole, and through "All my bones shall declare: Hashem, who is like You" (Psalms 35:10), all becomes elevated. And the shell of Nogah is subsumed into holiness through blessing and thanking Hashem for every permitted pleasure, acknowledging they stem from Him.
records.targetHebrew: ועל כן אמרו בחשאי (פסחים נו.), ומשלו לבת מלך שהריחה ציקי קדרה דיש לה גנאי; כי דבר זה גנאי לכנסת ישראל כשאין לבם נקי לגמרי. אבל באמת "יקר מחכמה מכבוד סכלות מעט" (קהלת י׳:א׳), כי שאור מעוטו יפה (ברכות לד.); כי קילוסו וכבוד מלכותו עולה יותר כשיש עדין יצר בלב ועם כל זה לבבו מכיר יחודו יתברך ודאין עוד מלבדו.
records.targetEnglish: Therefore they said it quietly and compared it to a king's daughter who smelled a dish's seasoning and would feel ashamed to ask for it. It is a disgrace to the congregation of Israel when its heart is not completely pure. Yet “a little foolishness is more precious than wisdom and honor,” and a little leaven is beneficial: His praise and the glory of His kingship rise still more when an impulse remains in the heart and, despite it, the heart recognizes His unity and that there is none besides Him.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Receptivity is clarified toward the good
records.themeSummary: Yisro's openness becomes attachment to truth when good and evil are distinguished.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef places the same verse about Amalek and Yisro within an account of separating the good from the evil mixed with it. This clarifies why the siman can distinguish the simple person's misdirected belief from the scoffer's obstruction of belief: openness has something that can be redirected, but it still needs clarification toward truth. The surrounding incense discussion preserves the good capable of giving fragrance rather than identifying every existing mixture with its final condition.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה טַעַם "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק", כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז) עַל פָּסוּק "לֵץ תַּכֶּה" – זֶה עֲמָלֵק, "וּפֶתִי יַעְרִם" – זֶה יִתְרוֹ. וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּפֶתִי הוּא הַמַּאֲמִין בַּכֹּל, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "פֶּתִי יַאֲמִין לְכָל דָּבָר", וְיִתְרוֹ לֹא הִנִּיחַ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמְּכִילְתָּא) שֶׁהֶאֱמִין בַּכֹּל; וְלוֹ יֵשׁ תַּקָּנָה שֶׁיַּעֲרִים לְהַאֲמִין בַּה' אֱמֶת עַל יְדֵי הַכָּאַת הַלֵּץ, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁאֵין מַאֲמִין כְּלָל.
records.originEnglish: And this explains why "Amalek was the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20), as expounded in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 27) on the verse "Smite a scorner" (Proverbs 19:25)—this is Amalek; "and the simple will become prudent"—this is Jethro. And I heard that a 'peti' (simple one) is one who believes anything, as it is written: "The simple believes every word" (Proverbs 14:15), and Jethro left no idol unworshiped (Mekhilta) because he believed in everything; and for him there is remedy—that he become wise to believe in the true God through the smiting of the scorner who believes in nothing.
records.targetHebrew: וכמו שאיתא במדרש (תנחומא יתרו ג') לץ תכה ופתי יערים (משלי י״ט:כ״ה) לץ תכה זה עמלק ופתי יערים זה יתרו, היינו, כי אחר יציאת מצרים וקריעת ים סוף נפרד הרע מן הטוב. ועמלק נפרד לגמרי לרע ויתרו נכלל בישראל.
records.targetEnglish: As the Midrash says: “Strike a scoffer, and the simple person becomes discerning.” The scoffer is Amalek, and the simple person is Yisro. After the Exodus and the splitting of the sea, evil was separated from good: Amalek became separated entirely toward evil, while Yisro became included within Israel.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 11:1
records.themeTitle: The future disclosure follows present restraint
records.themeSummary: Fixed holiness does not make the work of this world dispensable.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim explains the same promise that even the horse's bells will be holy by first insisting that Israel not rely on an already fixed holiness. Present restraint and work prepare its disclosure. This makes the siman's concluding boundary precise: its future account of everything becoming holy is not a reason to erase the intention and discipline it requires of laughter in this world.
records.originHebrew: כָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה כַּוָּנָה לְמִצְוָה וְהַרְחָבַת לֵב דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, רַק כִּשְׂחוֹק וְהוֹלֵלוּת בְּעָלְמָא אָסוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁלִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע. וְהוּא דַּרְגָּה לַשְּׂחוֹק הַב' דְּלֵיצָנוּת וְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ וּפְרִיקַת עוֹל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְפַּנֶּה לִבּוֹ לְבַטָּלָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. רַק "אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק וְגוֹמֵר", כִּי אָז לֹא יִהְיֶה בַּטָּלָה כְּלָל, כִּי כָּל דְּבַר בַּטָּלָה גַּם כֵּן קֹדֶשׁ לַה', כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "מְצִלּוֹת הַסּוּס וְגוֹמֵר", וְהוּא הָאוֹהֵב זִמָּה כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים קיג:) גַּם כֵּן קֹדֶשׁ.
records.originEnglish: so long as it lacks intention for a mitzvah and mental relaxation for Torah study, being mere empty sport and frivolity— it is forbidden in this world where the evil inclination holds sway. For it serves as a steppingstone to that other laughter of mockery, levity, and casting off the yoke, Heaven forbid, for through this one's heart turns to vanity, Heaven forbid. Only "Then will our mouth be filled with laughter" (Psalms 126:2), because then there will be no vanity at all, for even all idle matters will be holy unto Hashem, as written "the bells of the horses shall be holy unto Hashem" (Zechariah 14:20), and the horse loves licentiousness, as our Sages taught (Pesachim 113b), yet it too will become holy.
records.targetHebrew: היינו עי"ז שהישראל אינו סומך עצמו על התקופות מקדושה הקבועה שבו רק מצמצם א"ע מצדו בעבודה בעוה"ז בההיקף שבעה ומבטל א"ע להשי"ת כסוס שטפלה לרוכב וכדאי' בזה"ק (צו כ"ט:) ויהון כסוסיא דרכיב מאריה עלייהו יזכו ליום ההוא שיהי' על מצלות הסוס קדש לה' שהשי"ת יאיר אז שישראל הם קדש לה' בלא ו'
records.targetEnglish: Through Israel's not relying on the assurance of the holiness fixed within them, but instead restraining themselves in the work of this world within the cycle of seven and submitting to Hashem like a horse to its rider, they will merit the day when even the horse's bells will be holy to Hashem. Hashem will then illuminate that Israel is kodesh to Hashem, without the letter vav.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1
records.themeTitle: The question within Avraham's heart
records.themeSummary: The unique inward awakening itself reveals a personal divine address.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach offers a related reading of the same Midrash: Hashem answers Avraham through the very fact that his heart asks what the surrounding world does not. This illuminates the siman's question about why the light burns in this particular heart. The readings differ in how they describe the burning palace, but both move from a general observation of the world to recognition of the Creator's particular awakening of the person.
records.originHebrew: שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֶךְ לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה לוֹ זֶה אַחַר שֶׁרָאָה בִּירָה דּוֹלֶקֶת, פֵּירוּשׁ, שֶׁדּוֹלֵק בְּלִבּוֹ אוֹר זֶה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. אָמַר: אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁזֶּה מֵעַצְמוֹ? וְלָמָּה מֵאִיר זֶה בְּלִבּוֹ וְכָל הָעוֹלָם בְּתֹהוּ וַאֲפֵלָה? וַדַּאי יֵשׁ מַנְהִיג בִּפְרָטוּת לְכָל פְּרָט נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי הַטֶּבַע הַכְּלָלִי.
records.originEnglish: Concerning this it was said: "Go forth, etc." (Genesis 12:1), which was revealed to him after he saw the burning palace, meaning that this light of Hashem burned within his heart. He said: Is it possible that this burns on its own? And why does this shine in his heart while the entire world is in chaos and darkness? Surely there is a specific Guide for each individual soul, beyond general natural laws.
records.targetHebrew: ועל זה נאמר במדרש (בראשית רבה פרשה לט, א): "מי הוא בעל הבירה? הציץ עליו בעל הבירה", וכפי הנראה היה לו לכתוב "הציץ אליו" ולא "עליו"; אך בראות אברהם אבינו עליו השלום את עסק דור הפלגה, זאת יקרא בשם "בירה דולקת", כי היה בעיניו לפלא מאד והרעים בנפשו: מי ברא אלה?! "הציץ עליו בעל הבירה" – היינו שהשיב לו הקדוש ברוך הוא: הלא תראה בעצמך, כי לכל העולם לא יקשה ואין אחד מהם שם על לב לאמר: מי עשה זאת? ואך בעיניך יפלא! ומהרעמות לבך תוכל לשער אשר בודאי נמצא בורא הסובב כל עלמין וממלא כל עלמין, והוא העיר לבך ונפשך לזה; וזה לשון "עליו", היינו על קושיתו, שזה בעצמו הוא תירוץ מספיק לפניו.
records.targetEnglish: The Midrash says, “Who is the owner of the palace? The owner of the palace looked upon him.” It might have said “looked toward him.” Avraham saw the activity of the generation of dispersion as a burning palace; he wondered greatly and his soul cried, “Who created these?” The Holy One answered him: see for yourself that this does not trouble the rest of the world and none of them asks who made it, while you find it astonishing. From the stirring of your heart you can discern that there is certainly a Creator who surrounds and fills all worlds, and that He awakened your heart and soul to this. “Upon him” refers to his question: the question itself is a sufficient answer for him.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 46:6
records.themeTitle: Fear prepares the vessel for the secret
records.themeSummary: Avraham's inward disclosure comes after his service has become established.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov interprets the same verse, “The secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him,” through the revelation of the covenant to Avraham after years of service. The secret is received when that service begins to become settled within him. This provides a concrete counterpart to the siman's distinction between enjoying Torah as an intellectual subject and receiving it as the completion of a felt lack before Hashem.
records.originHebrew: רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הָעוֹנֶג מִצַּד שֶׁהִיא תּוֹרַת ה' וְשֶׁדָּבוּק עַל יָדָהּ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ רַק "לִירֵאָיו". פֵּירוּשׁ, יָרֵא הוּא הֶחָסֵר כַּנּוֹדָע, דְּהַיִּרְאָה מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן, וְהַתּוֹרָה מַשְׁלֶמֶת. וְזֶהוּ "יִרְאַת ה' אוֹצָרוֹ", שֶׁהִיא אוֹצָר וּכְלִי קִבּוּל שֶׁבּוֹ מְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה הוּא רַק בְּאוֹצַר הַיִּרְאָה, פֵּירוּשׁ לְהַשְׁלִים חֶסְרוֹנוֹ וּלְיַשְּׁרוֹ, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּסוֹדוֹ.
records.originEnglish: Only when the delight is because it is Hashem's Torah and through it one clings unto Hashem, and this belongs exclusively "to those who fear Him." The explanation is: one who fears is one who feels deficient, as is known, for fear arises from a sense of lack, and Torah brings completion. And this is "the fear of Hashem is his storehouse," (Isaiah 33:6) that it is a storehouse and receptive vessel; receiving the Torah occurs only through the vessel of fear, meaning to repair his deficiency and make him upright, then Hashem, blessed be He, shares His intimate secret with him.
records.targetHebrew: ולזה, כשנשלמו צ"ט שנה לאברהם אבינו, שהיה עובד את השם יתברך כל ימיו, מעתה הגיע העת שהתחילה להקבע בו העבודות שפעל ועשה עד עתה, אז גילה לו השם יתברך רז זה, כדכתיב (תהלים כה, יד): "סוד ה' ליראיו, ובריתו להודיעם", שזה הכתוב נדרש (ויקרא רבה פרשה מט) על המילה; והיה זה המאמר בסוד עד צ"ט שנה, כל הימים שהיה בו כח עוד לקנות קדושה על ידי עבודותיו.
records.targetEnglish: When Avraham had completed ninety-nine years of serving Hashem throughout his life, the time came for the services he had performed to begin to become established within him. Hashem then revealed this secret to him, as it says, “The secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him, and His covenant is to make it known to them.” The Midrash interprets this verse concerning circumcision. This word remained secret until ninety-nine, throughout the years in which he still had strength to acquire holiness through his service.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Repentance is open; total root repair is a further claim
records.themeSummary: The limit discussed here concerns the complete removal of mortality, not the possibility of returning to Hashem.
records.explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains this very qualification of the Zohar. It defines the negation as complete repair that would remove the guard of the tree of life and allow endless bodily life, then explicitly states that nothing stands in the way of repentance. Reading it beside the final siman prevents “repentance does not help” from being detached from the immediately stated meaning of total repair. The siman itself ends by placing that final root repair in divine aid.
records.originHebrew: שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כִּי עַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּנָהּ הוּא בִּילּוּעַ הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח שֶׁהוּא מִכֹּחַ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ. וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵץ חַיִּים, שַׁעַר קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, דְּכָל טִיפַּת קֶרִי הוּא בִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וּתְשׁוּבָה הוּא לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי, אִם כֵּן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בִּילּוּעַ הַמָּוֶת.
records.originEnglish: which is impossible to rectify completely in this world, for through its complete rectification comes the swallowing up of death forever, which derives from the serpent's counsel. Therefore they said in the Zohar (I 219b) that standard repentance is ineffective for emitting seed in vain, as written in Etz Chayim, Sha'ar Kelipat Nogah, that every drop of nocturnal emission is bound to Kelipat Nogah, see there. And complete repentance rectifies totally; thus it requires the total eradication of death.
records.targetHebrew: ועל כן אמרו [בזוהר] דאין מועיל תשובה היינו שיועיל לגמרי כמשפט התשובה הגמורה דזדונות נעשו כזכיות, שמתקן הקודם לגמרי ועד שישב עוד לזכות, ועדיף מצדיק גמור דבמקום שבעלי תשובה כו׳ דזה אי אפשר בעון זה, דאם כן היה מסתלק ממנו השמירה מדרך עץ החיים והיה יכול אוכל וחי לעולם ואין רצון השם יתברך בעולם הזה בזה, ושם שומרים שלא יוכל להגיע לזה, היינו שלא יוכל לתקן כל כך ולשוב לגמרי עד שיוכל לחיות לעולם אבל מכל מקום ״אין לך דבר שעומד בפני התשובה״, והתשובה שבמדת היסוד ברית קודש זוכה [מ]מיתה להארכת ימיו ושנותיו
records.targetEnglish: Therefore the Zohar says that repentance does not avail: this means availing completely, according to the full measure of repentance in which deliberate sins become merits, the past is entirely repaired and even becomes a merit. If this were attained here, the guard of the tree of life would be removed and the person could eat and live forever; this is not Hashem's will in this world. The guards prevent a repair and complete return extending to living forever. Nevertheless, “nothing stands in the way of repentance,” and repentance concerning the holy covenant brings a person from death to length of days and years.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The weakness is repaired through the return to Torah
records.themeSummary: Rephidim shows a failure that the ensuing reception of Torah can repair.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same journey as disclosure that Torah can repair earlier failures. Its full discussion also identifies the error of imagining that divine favor makes human service unnecessary. Read beside the siman's explicit crying out, the parallel describes how a failure becomes the occasion for return and greater reception, rather than recommending weakness or delay as a spiritual technique.
records.originHebrew: קנא] עִתּוֹת הַיְּרִידָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם חֵשֶׁק לְאוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה – זֶהוּ הֲכָנָה לַעֲלִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה, וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַצְּעָקָה שֶׁצּוֹעֵק כְּשֶׁמִּתְבּוֹנֵן עַל דְּרָכָיו וְרוֹאֶה שִׁפְלוּתוֹ וִירִידָתוֹ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּסְעוּ מֵרְפִידִים וַיָּבֹאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינַי" (שְׁמוֹת יט, ב), וְיָדוּעַ דְּרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו.) עַל "רְפִידִים" – שֶׁרָפוּ יְדֵיהֶם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה; וְזֶה הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַחִיזּוּק יָדַיִם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
records.originEnglish: Periods of spiritual descent which a person experiences, wherein he feels no desire for light and divine service, are the preparation for a great ascent. And that is achieved through the heartfelt outcry he raises when he contemplates his ways and beholds his lowliness and descent. As it is written: "And they departed from Rephidim, and came to the wilderness of Sinai" (Exodus 19:2), and known is the exposition of our Sages (Sanhedrin 106a) on Rephidim—that they slackened their hands from words of Torah; and this very slackening was the preparation for the Giving of the Torah, which is the ultimate strengthening of hands in words of Torah.
records.targetHebrew:
ויסעו מרפידים ויבאו מדבר סיני וגו' (שמות י״ט:ב׳).
ואיתא בש"ס (בכורות ה:) מה רפידים שריפו עצמן מן דברי תורה. והענין הכשלון הזה שהיה קודם מתן תורה שבזה הראה להם השי"ת, שכל מיני כשלונות שנמצא לפעמים אצל ישראל ע"י דברי תורה יוכלו לתקן הכל. וכמו שאנו רואים שיש כמה וכמה דברי תורה שלא יכול האדם לבוא עליהם בלתי הכשלון שמקודם, כמו שאיתא בש"ס (גיטין מג.) על הפסוק (ישעיהו ג׳:ו׳) והמכשלה הזאת תחת ידך, אין אדם עומד על ד"ת אלא א"כ נכשל בהן. ובזאת הראה להם השי"ת שע"י דברי תורה יוכלו לתקן הכל.
records.targetEnglish: “They journeyed from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai.” The Gemara explains Rephidim as their weakening themselves from Torah. Through this failure before the giving of the Torah, Hashem showed them that the different failures sometimes found in Israel can all be repaired through Torah. We see that there are teachings a person cannot attain without first stumbling, as the Gemara says of “this stumbling block is under your hand”: a person does not grasp words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them. Hashem thus showed them that through Torah they could repair everything.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The apparently reversed metaphors describe successive entries
records.themeSummary: Torah and fear each open the way to a deeper reception of the other.
records.explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim explicitly asks why fear is called the outer key to Torah while elsewhere Torah is called the gate into fear. Its answer distinguishes the inherited Torah that permits entry from the fuller wisdom received through developed fear. This gives the siman's repeated movement a concrete structure: an initial opening does not exhaust either fear or wisdom, and each prepares a deeper reception of the other.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: אִם אֵין יִרְאָה אֵין חָכְמָה, אִם אֵין חָכְמָה אֵין יִרְאָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג, יז). חָכְמָה הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְיִרְאָה הוּא מִן הַחֵטְא, וְהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּי. וְיִרְאָה נִקְרָא "אוֹצָר" וּכְלִי קִבּוּל, שֶׁהַלֵּב מִתְפַּנֶּה מִכָּל מִינֵי תְּשׁוּקוֹת וַחֲמוּדוֹת, וּמִמֵּילָא הוּא כְּלִי פָּנוּי לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
records.originEnglish: And concerning this they taught: "If there is no fear, there is no wisdom; if there is no wisdom, there is no fear" (Avot 3:17). Wisdom is the perception of the Blessed Name, while fear is dread of sin, and neither can function without the other. And fear is termed a "treasury" and a receptive vessel, wherein the heart empties itself of all base longings and lusts, automatically becoming a cleared vessel to receive words of Torah,
records.targetHebrew: כי על ידי שלימות היראה נשלמה גם החכמה והתורה בשלימותה, דהא בהא תליא כמו שאמרו באבות (פרק ג׳ משנה י״ז): ״אם אין יראה — אין חכמה; אם אין חכמה — אין יראה״. ומצד הזה המשילו בשבת (ל״א ריש עמוד ב׳): יראה למפתחות חיצונות, ותורה למפתחות פנימיות וזה היפך המשל ד״תרעא״ ו״דרתא״ המזכר שם גם כן אחר כך. אבל שניהם אמת: דההתחלה צריך להיות קביעות התורה בלב שהיא מורשה לקהלת יעקב, וקבועה בקנין בלב כל אחד מישראל ועל ידי הכניסה בתרעא זו דתורה בפתח כחדה של מחט (שיר השירים רבה ה:ב) אז יוכל ליכנס אחר כך לעבודת השם יתברך ביראה שבלב, שהוא התכלית ד״ה׳ שאל מעמך״.
records.targetEnglish: Through the completion of fear, wisdom and Torah too become complete, for the two depend on one another: “Without fear there is no wisdom; without wisdom there is no fear.” Shabbat therefore compares fear to outer keys and Torah to inner keys, apparently reversing its other image of gate and dwelling. Both are true. At the beginning Torah must be fixed in the heart as the inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov, acquired within each Jew. By entering this gate of Torah through an opening like a needle's point, one can then enter service with fear in the heart, the purpose of “Hashem asks of you.”
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 3
records.themeTitle: The sender also works within the hearers
records.themeSummary: Trust in a meaningful task rests on Hashem's relation to both the messenger and the people.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach places Moshe's uncertainty about Israel's belief within his divine commission: the One who sends him can also turn hearts. Its surrounding argument questions Moshe's wish to possess an independent power of compulsion. This illuminates the siman's qualification of believing in oneself: the confidence is that one has a real place in Hashem's concern and service, while its power remains received from Him.
records.originHebrew: קנד] כְּשֵׁם שֶׁצָּרִיךְ אָדָם לְהַאֲמִין בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ אַחַר כָּךְ לְהַאֲמִין בְּעַצְמוֹ. רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵסֶק עִמּוֹ, וְשֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ פּוֹעֵל בָּטֵל שֶׁבֵּין לַיְלָה וְכוּלֵי, וּכְחַיְתוֹ שָׂדֶה שֶׁלְּאַחַר מִיתָתָם נֶאֶבְדוּ וְאֵינָם. רַק צָרִיךְ לְהַאֲמִין כִּי נַפְשׁוֹ מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְעַנֵּג וּמִשְׁתַּעֲשֵׁעַ בָּהּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ. וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ: "וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת יד, לא) פֵּירוּשׁ, "מֹשֶׁה" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּלַל שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּדּוֹר הַהוּא, הֶאֱמִינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ בָּהֶם וּמִמֵּילָא גַּם כֵּן בְּמֹשֶׁה, אֲשֶׁר הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵם, וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכא:) שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נְזוּפִים לֹא נִתְיַיחֵד הַדִּבּוּר לְמֹשֶׁה.
records.originEnglish: Just as a person is required to believe in the Blessed Name, so too must he subsequently believe in himself. That is to say, he must believe that the Blessed Name has purposeful dealings with him, and that he is not a pointless creature who sprang up overnight and perishes, or like wild beasts that after death vanish into nothingness. Rather, he must believe that his soul stems from the Source of Life, blessed be His Name, and that the Blessed Name delights and revels in it when it fulfills His will. And this is the inner meaning of: "and they believed in Hashem, and in Moses His servant" (Exodus 14:31)— "Moses" denotes the collective sum of the 600,000 souls of Israel in that generation; they believed that the Blessed Name desired them and automatically they believed in Moses, who was essentially identical with them; as our Sages stated in Bava Batra 121b that all the years Israel were under censure in the wilderness, divine communication was not granted uniquely to Moses.
records.targetHebrew: כי היה לך להבין הלא בידי לבות בני אדם להטותם כפי רצוני, אם שלחתי אותך היה לך להאמין כי אשלח בלבם שיוכרחו לשמוע לך.
records.targetEnglish: You should have understood: the hearts of human beings are in My hand, to turn according to My will. If I sent you, you should have trusted that I would place it in their hearts to be compelled to hear you.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The leaves can express the life of the cluster
records.themeSummary: Even ordinary speech can be formed by a person's sustained relation to Torah.
records.explanation: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet explains the same leaf verse through speech that has become an expression of Torah even when unplanned. It stresses that this is an attained direction of choice, rather than something automatic in a person's status. This makes the siman's garment image concrete: permitted activity can support and reveal the Torah within, while its different discussion of Rashbi remains an exceptional attained state.
records.originHebrew: וְכֵן הִמְשִׁילוּ בְּחֻלִּין (צב.) עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים לְעַלְיָא וְאִתְכַּלְיָא, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וְכֵן יֵשׁ בִּפְעֻלַּת כָּל אֶחָד בְּעַצְמוֹ: פְּעֻלּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם מַעֲשֵׂה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וּפְעֻלּוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ נִקְרָא עַם הָאָרֶץ. וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:) עַל "וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא יִבּוֹל" – אֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חוּלִין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁהֵם עַלְיָא לְאִתְכַּלְיָא דְּהַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְאִלְמָלֵא עַלְיָא וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (לה:): הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן וְכוּלֵי, בְּמָטוּתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ וְכוּלֵי, וְהַרְבֵּה וְכוּלֵי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ, דְּאִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי.
records.originEnglish: And so in Chullin 92a they compared simple folk and Torah scholars to the protective grape leaves (alya) and the clusters of grapes (itkalya), see there. And so it is within the actions of each individual: spiritual Torah actions are the deeds of a scholar, while practical mundane endeavors are termed simple labor. And so our Sages expounded (Sukkah 21b) on "and its leaf does not wither"—even the casual speech of scholars, which serves as the protective leaf for the cluster of Torah, and were it not for the leaf, the cluster could not endure, as written in Berakhot 35b: "Conduct yourself with them in the way of the world... I beg of you, etc., many did as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and did not succeed, because without the leaf, etc."
records.targetHebrew: יאמר זה, שאל תחשב שהבדלת שבט הלוי הוא חקה שהם נבראו כך כמלאכים שאין בידם שלא להיות מלאכים, שאם כן תסלק הבחירה מהם, רק כאשר התורה יוצאה מפיו; ואמר "יוצאה", כאלו יוצאה מעצמה, שכל כך נעשה פיו נרתק לדברי תורה עד שדברי תורה יוצאה מעצמה מפיו, כי אין שפתותיו דובבות אלא דברי תורה, וגם שלא במתכון; ועל דרך שאיתא (סכה כ״א עמוד ב׳): "'ועלהו לא יבול' — אפילו שיחת חלין וכולי", כי אין שפתותיהם רוחשות כלל דברים שאינם דברי תורה, אז הוא כמלאכי השרת, שמתיחד בשליחות השם יתברך, שכל מחשבות לבבו בעולם הזה רק לזה, ואם לאו וכולי.
records.targetEnglish: Do not imagine that the tribe of Levi was set apart by being created like angels, unable to be otherwise, for that would remove their choice. It is when Torah comes out of his mouth. “Comes out” suggests that it emerges almost of itself: his mouth has become such a receptacle for Torah that his lips utter only Torah, even without specific intent. This is like “its leaf does not wither,” interpreted even of a scholar's ordinary conversation. When his lips do not move with things that are not Torah, he resembles a ministering angel, wholly directed toward Hashem's mission, with the thoughts of his heart in this world directed to it. If not, the opposite holds.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua 23
records.themeTitle: Divine forgiveness and human recognition remain distinct
records.themeSummary: The returning person recognizes the failure while Hashem discloses the forgiving perspective.
records.explanation: Likkutei Maamarim addresses the boundary within this teaching directly. The forgiving disclosure comes from Hashem; the human response still recognizes sin, deficiency and dependence on Him. This supplies a necessary companion to the siman's retrospective account of providence. The claim is not converted into a prior authorization to transgress or a self-issued verdict that no return is needed.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁאֵין מִקְרֶה, מַמְתִּיק כָּל הַדִּינִים וּמְתַקֵּן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת, כִּי אִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ כֻּלָּם לֹא הָיוּ יוֹצְאִים מִן הַסֵּדֶר, וְהָיָה מְסוּדָּר כָּךְ וְלֹא בְּמִקְרֶה, וְאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ עֲבֵירָה, וְעַל עָוֹן הַנִּזְכָּר הוּא תִּיקּוּן בְּיִחוּד:
records.originEnglish: And by believing that there is no chance, he sweetens all strict judgments and rectifies all sins; for if so, perforce none of them truly departed from divine order, but all was so orchestrated and not by chance, and if so, it was not an absolute rebellion, and for this aforementioned sin of seminal emission it serves as a unique rectification.
records.targetHebrew: וזהו שנקרא השם יתברך "המרבה לסלוח", שמצדו הוא הסליחה; אבל מצד בני אדם הוא הכרת החטא והחסרון, וכמה שנאמר: "וחטאתי נגדי תמיד" [תהלים נ״א:ה׳], ואף על פי שהתודה ביום הכפורים זה, חוזר ומתודה וכולי (יומא פ״ו עמוד ב׳); כי אם האדם יכיר בעצמו שלא היה מכשול רק שהכל משלו וככל האמות אשר סביבותיו, הרי הוא באמת מכשול; שמצד האדם צריך להכיר שבאמת אין שום כח לאדם מעצמו, ונמצא הימים שהלך בחשך והיה נעלם ממנו שהשם יתברך הוא הנותן לו כח לעשות חיל [דברים ח׳:י״ח] היה חטא ומכשול, ואז השם יתברך יאמר שלא היה מכשול כנזכר לעיל.
records.targetEnglish: This is why Hashem is called ‘the One who abundantly forgives’: forgiveness comes from His side, whereas from the human side there must be recognition of the sin and deficiency, as it says, ‘My sin is before me always’ (Psalms 51:5). Even though one confessed on this Yom Kippur, one confesses again on the next (Yoma 86b). For if a person decides for himself that there was no stumbling, but that everything was his own achievement, as do the nations around him, that itself is truly a stumbling. From the human side, one must recognize that a person has no independent power. The days when he walked in darkness, unaware that Hashem gives him the strength to act (Deuteronomy 8:18), were therefore sin and stumbling; then Hashem says that it was not a stumbling, as explained above.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Sincerity is measured by the work actually available
records.themeSummary: No deceit in the spirit means doing the clarification that is within one's power.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef interprets the same Zohar passage through the responsibility to clarify oneself to the limit of one's ability. The surrounding discussion warns that believing one has done everything is not sufficient if further clarification remains possible. This explains why the siman rejects an acceptance secretly adopted merely as a device for obtaining life: the condition concerns the reality of the heart's service, rather than the wording of a declaration.
records.originHebrew: וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בַּמִּדְבָּר (קכא עַמּוּד א): שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה בְּלֹא רַמִיָּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית (ח:) מִקְּרָא דְּדָנִיֵּאל, דְּקַבָּלַת הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת הָוֵי כְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְחַיִּים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אַךְ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת, כִּי אִם יַחְשׁוֹב עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִזְכּוֹת בַּחַיִּים – אֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת, וְאָז אַדְּרַבָּה סַכָּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר.
records.originEnglish: And the counsel for this is in the Zohar (end of Bemidbar 121a): that he surrender his soul unto death without deceit, see there. And that matches what is stated in Ta'anit 8b from the verse in Daniel, that the sincere acceptance of the heart is legally equivalent to action, and through this he merits eternal life as noted above yet it must be in total sincerity, for if he calculates through this to attain life, it is not genuine truth, and then on the contrary it invites mortal danger as written in the Zohar.
records.targetHebrew: אבל מי שבירר עצמו באמת בלי שום רמיה עד מקום שידו מגעת, ואם לאדם הזה יזדמן פעולה שאינה מבוררת, לא יחשוב ד' לו עון, כי הוא ודאי כיון לעומק הרצון של השי"ת.
records.targetEnglish: But one who has truly clarified himself without any deceit, to the full extent of his ability—if an unclarified act should then come before him, Hashem will not reckon it to him as deliberate sin, for he certainly directed himself toward the depth of Hashem's will.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The removal of the impulse had a corresponding cost
records.themeSummary: Open prophecy withdrew when the struggle against idolatry was abolished.
records.explanation: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet develops what was included in “neither it nor its reward.” Overcoming the impulse toward idolatry had been a setting for open recognition of the Shechinah; when the impulse was abolished, that form of prophecy and open miracle also receded. This makes the siman's contrast of the two impulses more precise: their histories and place in the world differ, so removing one cannot simply be made the model for removing the other.
records.originHebrew: רַק דְּמִיּוֹסֵף יָצָא יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהוּא יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם לְתַקֵּן רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּלוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בְּטַעֲנַת "לָא הוּא וְלָא אַגְרֵיהּ". מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה צָרִיךְ בָּעוֹלָם כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם, וּלְכָךְ אֵין מַגִּיעַ הַמִּיתָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ. וּלְכָךְ זָכָה דָּוִד לְדַרְגָּא דִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה בַּחַיִּים, שֶׁהוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּל יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶצְלוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם כֹּחַ זוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ כֻּלּוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד
records.originEnglish: only that from Joseph issued Jeroboam who personified the inclination for idolatry, which was impossible for human effort to rectify except through its complete eradication by the Men of the Great Assembly claiming: "Neither it do we desire, nor its reward" (Yoma 69b). In contrast, the inclination for unchastity is necessary for the world's survival, which is why actual death is not mandated, and this is not the place to elaborate. And therefore David merited the level of surrendering his soul unto death during physical life, achieved solely through utterly nullifying the inclination for idolatry within himself, recognizing no power other than Hashem and surrendering himself entirely to the Blessed Name
records.targetHebrew: וְדָבָר זֶה גָּרַם הַחֵטְא אָז שֶׁיֵּעָלֵם עַל יְדֵי בַּקָּשַׁת אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה, לְפִי רְאוֹתָם גֹּדֶל הַחֲטָאִים אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא ס״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): לָא אִיהוּ בָּעֵינַן וְלָא אַגְרֵיהּ בָּעֵינַן, שֶׁבִּטְּלוּ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (עַל פָּסוּק: "אֶעֱלֶה בְתָמָר" [ז׳:ט׳]) שֶׁהָיָה זֶה בִּימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר. וְעַל יְדֵי כְּפִיַּת הַיֵּצֶר דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁהוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מֵהַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר כָּפוּ לוֹ הִשִּׂיגוּ גִּלּוּי הַשְּׁכִינָה; וְכֵן כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׁמְעוּ לוֹ, אָז הֻשְׁדַּד הַטֶּבַע לְהָרַע לָהֶם כְּמִדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם אָמְרוּ: "אֵין ה' רוֹאֶה", לָכֵן הֶרְאָם כִּי הוּא רוֹאֶה כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם. אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר נִתְבַּטֵּל יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁזֶּה גָּרַם הַחֵטְא שֶׁהֻצְרַךְ לְהִתְבַּטֵּל, אָז מִמֵּילָא נִסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה וְהַשְּׁכִינָה גַּם כֵּן מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם דָּבָר שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יַשִּׂיגוּ גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶצְלָם, רַק הָיָה הַכֹּל בְּהֶעְלֵם. וּלְכָךְ אֶסְתֵּר, שֶׁהִיא סוֹף גָּלוּת בָּבֶל, הוּא סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים הַנִּגְלִים שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב, שֶׁמִּן אָז וָהֵלְאָה הָיוּ נִסִּים נִסְתָּרִים שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב.
records.targetEnglish: Sin caused this to be hidden through the request of the Great Assembly. Seeing the greatness of the sins, they said, “We want neither it nor its reward,” and abolished the impulse to idolatry; the Midrash places this in the days of Mordechai and Esther. By subduing that impulse, the opposite of recognizing Hashem, they had attained revelation of the Shechinah. Even when they followed it, nature was disrupted against them measure for measure: saying “Hashem does not see,” they were shown that He sees all their acts. But when the impulse was abolished, prophecy and the Shechinah's open presence withdrew as well, because the setting through which they attained that revelation was gone. All was then concealed. Esther, at the end of the Babylonian exile, therefore marks the end of the open miracles given to be written; thereafter the miracles were hidden and were not given to be written.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Possessions and the person have related powers of life
records.themeSummary: The relation is a connection between corresponding levels, whose differences remain real.
records.explanation: Kometz HaMinchah begins from the marks by which a lost possession is recognized as belonging to a person and develops the relation through the divine life sustaining each. It explicitly distinguishes an inanimate power in an object from the corresponding power in a human being. This clarifies the siman's extension of a person's faculties into possessions and food: relation and correspondence are intended, without making the levels identical.
records.originHebrew: וְכֵן כָּל הַחֲפָצִים, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁל הָאָדָם, הוּא מֵהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחַ נַפְשׁוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ בָּהֶם, וּמִזֶּה הוּא חַיּוּתָם כַּיָּדוּעַ. וּמִמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא טוֹב, כָּךְ כָּל כֵּלָיו הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים מֵאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ, וְכֵן הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁמֵּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ יֵשׁ בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה גְּדוֹלָה.
records.originEnglish: And so with all possessions, and it goes without saying a person's food, which derive from the extension of his soul-power and vitality within them, from which they receive their vitality as is known. And from whatever source within him is good, so are all his utensils extending from that power, and likewise the food deriving from that power contains immense holiness.
records.targetHebrew: הרכוש שייך לאדם, שהרי גם כשנאבד מידו צריך להחזיר כשיש לו סימן או טביעות עין, שרצה לומר: איזה שייכות, הכרה, ועדות שהוא שלו. והיינו כי הכל בדבר ה' המחיהו, ומסתמא יש לאותו חיים שלו שייכות באותם חיים; כי ד' ארבע מדרגות הם: דומם, צומח, חי, מדבר בעולם השפל, והחמישית הם העליונים; וכן ד' ארבעה יסודות: אש, רוח, מים, עפר, ושמים – גשם חמישי; וכן ד' ארבע נפשות: נפש, רוח, נשמה, ונשמה לנשמה חיה, והחמישית – יחידה, כמו שכתבתי כל זה במקום אחר. והיינו שבאדם מורכב כל דומם, צומח, חי, מדבר, וכח הדומם הוא כח הנפש וכולי; ובודאי שיש חילוק בין כח הדומם שבדומם לכח הדומם שבאדם, אבל מכל מקום יש להם חבור ושייכות.
records.targetEnglish: Property belongs to a person: even when it is lost, it must be returned when he has an identifying mark or recognizes it, indicating a relation, recognition and testimony that it is his. Everything lives through Hashem's word, and the person's own life presumably has a relation to the life within the possession. There are four levels in the lower world—inanimate, plant, animal and speaking human—with the upper realms as a fifth. Likewise there are four elements—fire, air, water and earth—with heaven as a fifth substance. Likewise there are four soul levels: nefesh, ruach, neshamah and the soul of the soul, chayah, with yechidah as the fifth, as explained elsewhere. A person contains the inanimate, plant, animal and speaking levels; the inanimate power is the power of the nefesh, and so forth. There is certainly a difference between the inanimate power in an inanimate thing and the corresponding power within a person; nevertheless they have a bond and relation.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Yosef turns the encounter toward his own repair
records.themeSummary: The frightening encounter becomes an occasion for examining the corresponding faults.
records.explanation: Chanukah applies the same Shabbat passage to Yosef in the pit. It describes how the encounter awakened his own need to clarify the reports he had made about his brothers, followed by repentance. This provides a concrete example of the siman's movement from fear to the repair and strengthening of a particular faculty, rather than stopping at the fear itself.
records.originHebrew: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַק כְּפָתוּהוּ וְכוּלֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַכּוֹת (שָׁם), וְכִדְבָרֵי שַׁמַּאי בְּשַׁבָּת (קכא:) בְּנָחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחֲרָיו, כִּי בָּזֶה יָצָא יְדֵי עוֹנְשׁוֹ וְיִסּוּרִין שֶׁלּוֹ בַּפַּחַד שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁיִּשְּׁכֶנּוּ; וְכֵן הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת דְּמִן הַשָּׁמַיִם נִזְדַּמְּנוּ וְכוּלֵי כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם,
records.originEnglish: and even if they merely bound him to be lashed, etc., as written in Makkot there, and as in Shabbat 121b regarding a snake that was pursuing a person, for through that alone he fulfilled his punishment and suffering via the mortal terror that it would bite him; and so it was in truth that from Heaven it was orchestrated, as brought there,
records.targetHebrew: וכאשר השלך לבור נחשים ועקרבים ולא הרגם, אז ידע יוסף שנזדמנו להרגו ונעשה לו נס, ואז הרגיש בנפשו שנצרך לו להתברר בשני הדברים: שהוציא דבה על אחיו שתולים עיניהם בבנות הארץ, ושחשודים על אבר מן החי, כי לענין זה נזדמנו לו הנחשים ועקרבים: כי הנחש שרש של פגם הברית, שהוא עטיו של נחש שהכניס לאדם הראשון בתאות האכילה, ועל ידי זה נענש ב"נחש עפר לחמו", שנטל ממנו הטעם של תאות אכילה; והעקרב הוא הממית בודאי, כמו שכתוב (ברכות ל״ג עמוד א׳): "אבל עקרב פוסק", והוא נגד פגם רציחה שנמשך על ידי קין, והוא נגד פגם של אבר מן החי, שנזהרים בזה גם אמות העולם מצד שהוא אכזריות גדולה, חוץ האסור שנאסר לבני נח, ולכן נתביש נבוכדנצר כשאכל ארנבת חיה (כמו שכתוב נדרים ס״ה עמוד א׳). וכאשר נזדמנו לפני יוסף הנחשים ועקרבים, הרגיש בנפשו שצריך להתברר בענין הוצאת הדבה, ובודאי עשה תשובה על שני הפגמים הנזכרים לעיל.
records.targetEnglish: When Yosef was thrown into the pit of snakes and scorpions and did not kill them, he knew that they had been brought before him to kill him and that a miracle had occurred. He then sensed that he needed clarification concerning two things: his report that his brothers looked at the daughters of the land, and that they were suspected of eating a limb from a living animal. For these matters the snakes and scorpions came before him. The snake is the root of damage to the covenant, the serpent's counsel that introduced the appetite for eating into Adam. It was therefore punished with “dust is the snake's bread,” losing the taste of that appetite. The scorpion certainly kills, as Berakhot 33a says, “For a scorpion he interrupts.” It corresponds to the damage of bloodshed extending through Kayin and to the fault of a limb from a living animal. The nations too guard against this because it is great cruelty, besides the prohibition commanded to the descendants of Noach. Nevuchadnezzar was therefore ashamed when he ate a live hare, as in Nedarim 65a. When the snakes and scorpions came before Yosef, he sensed his need for clarification concerning the evil report, and he certainly repented for these two faults.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The angel's awakening can lead to a transformation
records.themeSummary: The later siman distinguishes removing a bad effect from redirecting its underlying desire.
records.explanation: Siman 242 supplies the distinction implicit in this opening: repentance can nullify the angel, while return from love transforms the desire itself toward Torah. It later explains “repentance that covers all his deeds” as the general return from love. Together the passages describe an actual change in the person and the power produced by the act; the emergence of remorse is the beginning of that work, rather than its automatic completion.
records.originHebrew: מִכָּל עֲבֵירָה נַעֲשָׂה מַלְאָךְ רַע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, זֶהוּ לְטוֹבָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם, שֶׁהַמַּלְאָךְ הוּא חַיּוּת רוּחָנִי, וְהוּא מַכִּיר בַּאֲמִתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְחָפֵץ שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם לִתְשׁוּבָה.
records.originEnglish: From every transgression an evil angel is formed, as our Sages of blessed memory taught, and this is actually for the benefit of human beings; for the angel is spiritual vitality, and it recognizes the truth of Hashem, blessed be He, and yearns to be transformed into good, and through this the person is aroused to repentance.
records.targetHebrew: רמב] התשובה הוא כמו התרת חכם שעוקר הדבר למפרע, ונתבטל המלאך רע הנעשה מהעבירה לגמרי. ומאהבה – שנעשין כזכיות, היינו שלא נתבטל, רק שנתהפך לטוב; זהו ב' דרגין ד"לאתהפכא" ו"לאכפיא". פירוש: היראה הוא ההגדרה בלב מהרע, ואהבה הוא שמהפך המר, שהוא היצר והחשק שבאדם, למתוק, שמושכו לבית המדרש ולדברי תורה, שבזה היצר הרע "טוב מאד", כמו שכתוב במדרש הנעלם (זהר חלק א, קלח א) דחמידו דאורייתא על ידו. וזהו "התורה תבלין ליצר" – לתבלו להיות טוב.
records.targetEnglish: Repentance resembles a sage's release that uproots the matter retroactively, and the bad angel made by the transgression is entirely nullified. When repentance comes from love, sins become merits: the angel is not nullified but transformed to good. These are the levels of transformation and subduing. Fear establishes a boundary in the heart against evil; love turns the bitter—the person's impulse and desire—sweet, by drawing it to the study house and Torah. In this way the evil impulse becomes “very good,” since the desire for Torah comes through it. Torah seasons the impulse so that it becomes good.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The division into persons preserves each person's task
records.themeSummary: The shared unity does not make an individual soul replaceable.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same Hosea verse by distinguishing the countless whole from the significance of each counted individual. Each has a particular service that another cannot perform in his place. This gives a complementary explanation of the siman's division of the one rope into particular souls: the common root and the importance of individual work coexist. Its eventual inclusion in unity does not cancel that work.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל יְדֵי הַמְּשִׁיכָה בַּחֶבֶל, הַחֶבֶל מִתְפַּקֵּעַ וּמִתְאָרֵךְ, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁנִּתְרַבּוּ נְפָשׁוֹת – וְלֹא שֶׁנִּתְרַבּוּ, רַק שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ אֶחָד לִשְׁנַיִם. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (דַּף ה.): "אִלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ אָנוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי", אֶלָּא כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהָיוּ נִכְלָלִים בִּמְקוֹרָם. וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֲטָאִים מִתְרַבִּים נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וּלְפִיכָךְ מַתְחִיל בְּהוֹשֵׁעַ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר הָאַרְבַּע שֵׁמוֹת רָעִים וּמְכוֹעָרִים שֶׁקָּרָא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל פָּסוּק "וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם וְגוֹמֵר",
records.originEnglish: And through the pulling on the rope, the rope snaps open and lengthens, meaning that souls multiply—not that brand-new souls multiply, but that one divides into two. And this is what they taught in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (5a): 'Had our ancestors not sinned, we would not have come into the world, etc.,' meaning rather like one who had not entered the world, as they would have remained included in their unified source. And through sins, souls of Israel multiply, and therefore Scripture begins in Hosea (2:1), immediately after the four harsh and unsightly names applied to Israel, with the verse: 'And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, etc.,'
records.targetHebrew: ומחמת שהיה בכל בריאה ובריאה מישראל זה הרצון שחפץ להיטיב, לכן הציב השי"ת לכל אחד מישראל פרט אחד, אשר בזה הפרט כביכול אינו בשלימות בלי עבודת זה האדם. וזה, והיה מספר, היינו שיש לכל אחד מישראל פרט אחד אשר מוכרח מצידו להשלים את הכבוד שמים, כי מצד השי"ת לא שייך שיחסר ח"ו הכבוד שמים ורק הוא בתכלית השלימות, ורק מזה הרצון החפץ להיטיב לבריותיו, ובכל בריה ובריה היה זה הרצון החפץ להיטיב לו. ע"כ בזה הפרט שהציב השי"ת מצידו שכביכול אינו בשלימות מוכרח הוא להשלים ולא אחר. וזה שכל נפש ונפש מישראל הוא דבר חשוב בעיני השי"ת, היינו שיש לו פרט אחד אשר בזה הפרט הציב השי"ת שכביכול חסר כבוד שמים בלתי עבודת זה האדם דוקא, אבל בכלל הוא אשר לא ימד ולא יספר, היינו שבכלל נכללים כל הפרטים באחדותו ית' והכבוד שמים הוא בתכלית השלימות בלתי עבודת האדם ג"כ.
records.targetEnglish: Because Hashem's desire to benefit was present in the creation of every individual of Israel, He placed before each one a particular matter whose completion, as He presents it to us, requires that person's service. “There shall be a number” means that each has a particular task through which he must complete the revealed divine honor. From Hashem's own side nothing is lacking; the arrangement comes from His desire to benefit the creatures. The particular matter placed before this person must be completed by him and no other. Thus each soul is important to Hashem. But in the totality, “it shall not be measured or counted”: all particulars are included in His unity, and His honor is complete even without human service.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Leah's inward will differs from her outward association
records.themeSummary: The appearance that she belongs to Esav is not the truth of her heart.
records.explanation: Takanat HaShavin distinguishes the public claim “the elder for the elder” from Leah's inward rejection of Esav's ways. That distinction explains how the siman uses apparent ugliness and hidden fruitfulness: the inner relation of the returning heart is not fully legible from its outward position. The comparison develops this particular symbolism, rather than making visible failure itself a virtue.
records.originHebrew: וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהַתְּשׁוּבָה נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא, וְאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה לִבְנֵי אָדָם הַיְקָרוּת וְהַיּוֹפִי שֶׁבָּהּ. וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: "כִּי שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לא), וְעַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר הַטַּעַם. וְהַיְינוּ כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג.) שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: הַגְּדוֹלָה לַגָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵי, הַיְינוּ לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה שַׁיָּיכֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְחֵלֶק עֵשָׂו, וְהָיְתָה בּוֹכָה – זֶהוּ סוֹד הַתְּשׁוּבָה. מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רָחֵל: "יְפַת תֹּאַר וִיפַת מַרְאֶה", שֶׁהַכֹּל אוֹמְרִים: הַקְּטַנָּה לַקָּטָן, כִּי בְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא יֵשׁ בָּהּ יֹפִי מַעֲשִׂים. אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, עִיקַּר תּוֹלָדוֹת מִשֶּׁל לֵאָה, שֶׁעִיקַּר הַהוֹלָדָה, הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּנְפָשׁוֹת לִרְצוֹן ה', הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
records.originEnglish: And this is because repentance is termed the Concealed World (alma de-itkasya), and its inner preciousness and beauty are not visible to ordinary human beings. And of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the root of all Israel, it is stated: "that Leah was hated" (Genesis 29:31), and see the Zohar for the inner reason. That is, as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Bava Batra 123a) that people would say: the elder daughter is for the elder son, etc.; meaning according to outward appearance she seemed linked, Heaven forbid, to the portion of Esau, and she wept—and this weeping is the mystical secret of repentance. In contrast, Rachel was "beautiful of form and fair to look upon," where all said: the younger daughter is for the younger son, for in the Revealed World (alma de-itgalya) she possessed manifest beauty of deeds. Nevertheless, the primary offspring issued from Leah, for the essence of true spiritual generation—innovating words of Torah and birthing holy souls for the will of Hashem—is entirely through the spiritual rung of repentance.
records.targetHebrew: והבריות היו אומרים ״הגדולה לגדול״ דמצד ההתגלות היה נראה כאלו חס ושלום דומה אליו, אבל באמת שנואים מעשה דעשו בעיניה ובזה נתעלית היא על רחל דזרעה הם רק שטנו של עשו, היינו מקטרגים בהיות הם טובים והוא רע אבל אם חס ושלום יחטא האדם, הרי חס ושלום נראה דומה לו אולם היא, שרש מעשיו שנואים אצלה והשנאה היא בלב שממאס הדבר ואף אם בפעל אינו כן רק למראית העין באתגליא, אבל השרש שבלב אינו כן ועל כן אמרו במגילה (יג.) ״הכופר בעבודה זרה נקרא יהודי״ דזהו שרש יהודה מזרעא דלאה, דאין לו אמונה בלב בעבודה זרה ושום כח נגד השם יתברך
records.targetEnglish: People said, “The elder for the elder,” because outwardly it seemed as though she resembled him, Heaven forbid. In truth, Esav's deeds were hateful to her. In this she rose above Rachel, whose children are Esav's accusers because they are good while he is evil. If a person sins, he can outwardly appear like Esav. But for Leah, the root of his deeds is hateful: hatred is the heart's rejection of the thing, even if outward action does not appear so. The root within the heart is different. Therefore “one who denies idolatry is called a Jew”: this is the root of Judah from Leah, whose heart has no belief in idolatry or any power opposed to Hashem.
