records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 26:5
records.themeTitle: What leaving a habit means
records.themeSummary: Torah must become active even in the body's ordinary responses.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim gives concrete meaning to the siman's work of departing from habit. The habit that seems impossible to leave is a personal Egypt; Torah is impressed through speech and action until even bodily response follows it. This illuminates why a later generation's apparently small task can still require real effort. Its explanation of habit does not replace the siman's separate account of aid from earlier souls.
records.originHebrew: כִּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוֹלְכִים מִמַּעְלָה לְמַטָּה, וְאָנוּ הַיּוֹם בְּעִקְּבוֹת מָשִׁיחַ מִן הָעִקְבִיִּים, עִיקָּר בַּעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו וּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית, וְכֵן הַמִּצְווֹת וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לָצֵאת מִן הַהֶרְגֵּל, יֵשׁ לוֹ סַיַּעְתָּא גְּדוֹלָה מֵאוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ,
records.originEnglish: for the generational levels descend from above to below, and we today in the footsteps of the Messiah stem from the heels, where the primary struggle lies in sins a person treads upon with his heels and guarding the Covenant, as well as breaking habitual routine in mitzvot, he possesses immense Heavenly assistance from those souls who have already lived,
records.targetHebrew: וזהו שאמרו ז"ל בכל דור ודור חייב אדם לראות א"ע כאילו הוא יצא ממצרים וכו' היינו שבכל דבר שאדם הוא משוקע בה עד שנדמה לו שאי אפשר לו לצאת מן ההרגל זה נקרא שעבוד מצרים ולזה מחויב האדם לראות שלא יהי' נמצא אצלו שום הרגל טבע כלל וכפי מה שהאדם משולל הימנו הרגל טבע כך מוצא בלבו חירות עולם וזה נקרא יציאת מצרים ובמה יכול האדם להוציא א"ע ממצרים זהו רק כאשר קובע בלבו שדברי תורה הם למעלה ומנושא מכל הדברים שבעוה"ז וכמאמרם ז"ל (אבות) המקבל עליו עול תורה מעבירין ממנו עול מלכות ועול דרך ארץ כי ד"ת הוא מנושא מעול מלכות וד"א וכפי מה שאדם קובע בלבו ד"ת כך נעשה האדם מנושא מכל ההרגלות שבעוה"ז וזה הכל צריך להיות בעובדא ובמלולא היינו שיהי' גם אמירה בפה כי פה גומר כד' בגמ' וזה מורה על הלבוש אחרון היינו שיהי' נקבע גבי האדם אף בהלבוש אחרון אף שלא מדעת כדאיתא בירשלמי מחזיקנא טובותא לרישא כד מטי למודים מנפשי' כרע היינו שהגוף נמשך אף שלא מדעת אחר רצונו ית':
records.targetEnglish: In every generation a person must see himself as though he left Egypt. Anything in which he is so immersed that he thinks escape from the habit impossible is called Egyptian bondage. He must work so that no fixed natural habit rules him; to the extent he is freed from it, he finds enduring freedom in his heart. How can he bring himself out? By fixing in his heart that Torah stands above the things of this world. One who accepts Torah's yoke is freed from the yoke of government and ordinary worldly occupation. As Torah becomes fixed in him, he rises above worldly habits. This must be through action and speech, for speech completes the matter, so that it is settled even in the final garment, without deliberate awareness. The Yerushalmi's bow at Modim illustrates the body following Hashem's will even without conscious direction.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The imperfect beginning is directed toward lishmah
records.themeSummary: The reason to continue includes what the study is meant to produce.
records.explanation: Peri Tzadik explains the force of continuing despite an imperfect beginning through the eventual movement toward lishmah. It also says that other severe formulations still require Tosafot's distinction, so the warnings are not simply dissolved. This complements the existing note's practical criterion of growing fear and care: the siman's acceptance of study now is joined to the commitment to let Torah change the heart.
records.originHebrew: אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת: וְכָל הָעוֹסֵק וְכוּלֵי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ דְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ נוֹחַ וְכוּלֵי וְנַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ כָּל זֶה, כִּי חָשְׁקָה נַפְשׁוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה, וּמַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אִם אֵין לִבּוֹ שָׁלֵם וּמְנוּקֶּה מִכָּל רַע וּפְנִיּוֹת וְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה עֲדַיִן? בְּאַהֲבָתָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה יִשְׁגֶּה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ הַסַּכָּנָה וְהָרָע שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק וְכוּלֵי, וִיקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ כָּל זֶה, לְפִי שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי, וְאָז יָשׁוּב הַכֹּל לְטוֹב:
records.originEnglish: But in truth both are truth: whoever engages in Torah, even though he knows that studying not for its own sake invites severe warnings, he nonetheless accepts all this upon himself because his soul passionately yearns for the Torah; and what shall he do if his heart is not yet completely whole and cleansed of all base motives and worldly desires? In the love of Torah let him be enraptured (Proverbs 5:19), even though he knows the spiritual danger involved; nonetheless, let him always engage in Torah and accept all this upon himself, because from not for its own sake he will come to its own sake, and then everything will be transformed to good.
records.targetHebrew: אבל באמת לשון זה "נוח לו שלא נברא" איתא על כל הבריאה, כמו שכתוב (עירובין יג:): נמנו וגמרו: נוח לו לאדם שלא נברא יותר משנברא; ותכלית הבריאה היה בשביל אדם שהוא כיעקב דעביד רק לשמיה דקודשא בריך הוא, וזה נוח לו שנברא. ומכל מקום שפיר אמרו בגמרא: לעולם יעסוק אדם בתורה ומצוות אפילו שלא לשמה, שמתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה, וזה נוח לו שנברא, ומיושב קשית תוספות על לשון הגמרא דברכות. אך תירוץ התוספות מוכרח משאר לשונות שבש״ס שהקשו בתוספות בשאר דוכתי.
records.targetEnglish: The expression “it would have been better not to have been created” was said about creation as a whole: they concluded that it would have been better for a person not to have been created. Creation's purpose is the person like Yaakov who acts for the Holy One's sake; for him it is good to have been created. Nevertheless, the Gemara rightly says always to engage in Torah and mitzvot even not for their own sake, because from this he comes to acting for their own sake, and then it is good for him to have been created. This resolves Tosafot's question concerning that expression in Berakhot. Their distinction remains necessary for the other expressions elsewhere in the Talmud.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Sweetening at the root turns toward divine aid
records.themeSummary: The felt limit of one's effort becomes a request for help from the source.
records.explanation: Dover Tzedek explains remembrance of mortality as requesting divine aid after effort has not yet achieved its purpose. Its conclusion explicitly defines sweetening through the soul's return to its source. This helps distinguish the siman's inner movement of repentance from merely being frightened: the direction of the heart is toward its source and the mercy sought there.
records.originHebrew: וְעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, אָז נַעֲשֶׂה הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁם, כִּי הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל בַּלֵּב, וְעִיקַּר תְּשׁוּבָה בַּלֵּב – זֶה נִקְרָא הַמְתָּקָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
records.originEnglish: And through repentance, the sweetening of judgments occurs at their very root, for the root of all is in the heart, and the essence of repentance is in the heart—which is termed sweetening at the root.
records.targetHebrew: ואחריהן "יזכור יום המיתה", היא בקשת הסיוע מהשם יתברך, כשרואה שיגע ולא מצא התועלת לזה לעורר רחמי שמים עליו, שמן השמים ירחמו ויעזרוהו והוא על ידי זכירת יום המיתה, שהנפש נפרדת מן הגוף ועולה למקורה ומתאחדת עם המקור וכידוע מהבעל שם טוב, כי המתקת הדינים הוא על ידי בטול נפשו למקורה, דשם היא תרעא דחירו, ואין כאן מקומו בבאור זה]
records.targetEnglish: After them comes “remember the day of death”: this means asking for help from Hashem when a person sees that he has labored without finding the needed result, so as to awaken heavenly mercy and assistance. It comes through remembering the soul's separation from the body and ascent to unite with its source. As is known from the Baal Shem Tov, the sweetening of judgments is through the surrender of the soul to its source, where the gate of freedom is found.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Miketz 1
records.themeTitle: The prayer is awakened before the gift
records.themeSummary: Yosef's cry lets the coming deliverance enter through his own service.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach describes Yosef's cry intensifying immediately before his deliverance, and explains that Hashem places such a cry in the heart so the gift may become the fruit of the person's own work. This supplies a concrete counterpart to the siman's call to turn an awakening into prayer before the matter fully emerges. The comparison concerns the sequence of awakening and response; it does not replace the siman's distinct explanation of Elul.
records.originHebrew: קסט] כַּאֲשֶׁר נוֹפֵל עַל אָדָם פַּחַד מֵאֵיזֶה דָבָר, אָז תֵּיכֶף יְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים לְהִנָּצֵל מִזֶּה, כִּי לְכָךְ עוֹרְרוּהוּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בְּפַחַד זֶה, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד:): לְעוֹלָם יַקְדִּים אָדָם תְּפִלָּה לַצָּרָה; וּמִנַּיִן יוֹדֵעַ קוֹדֶם מִן הַצָּרָה? רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד. כִּי יֵשׁ דִּינָא קַשְׁיָא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַמְתִּיק אַחַר צֵאתוֹ לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם, רַק צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּיקוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּעוֹדוֹ בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ.
records.originEnglish: When fear of something falls upon a person, let him immediately plead for mercy to be saved from it, for for this very purpose did Heaven awaken him through this fear, as our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 44b): "A person should always anticipate distress with prayer"; and whence does he know beforehand of the distress? The Blessed Name awakens him through fear. For there exists harsh judgment (dina kashya) which cannot be sweetened after it emerges into the world, but must be sweetened at its root while still in its formative gestation.
records.targetHebrew: כי בלילה ההוא גדלה צעקת יוסף הצדיק "שובה השם עד מתי" ותיכף השיג ישועה. ועל זה כתיב (תהלים פא חית, בית) "השם אלקי ישועתי וכולי צעקתי בלילה נגדך", כי כך הוא מדותיו של הקדוש ברוך הוא טרם אשר יתן הישועה מביא בלב האדם צעקה בזה למען אשר יקרא "יגיע כפיך".
records.targetEnglish: That night Yosef's cry grew: “Return, Hashem—until when?” Immediately he attained deliverance. Concerning this it says, “Hashem, God of my deliverance… I cried at night before You.” Such is the Holy One's way: before He gives deliverance, He places a cry in the person's heart, so that it may be called “the labor of your hands.”
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Day of Pesach 25:4
records.themeTitle: The breadth disclosed through the narrowness
records.themeSummary: The limit creates room for a person's service and relation to Hashem.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim interprets the same verse of calling from narrowness and being answered in breadth. Divine concealment gives Israel an actual part in the service; recognizing the connection made possible through that limitation is itself the breadth. This develops the siman's account of the good within a painful beginning without reducing its pattern to the outward pain alone.
records.originHebrew: וְהַתְחָלַת כָּל פְּעֻלָּה הוּא מִצַּד הֶכְרֵחַ הַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁחָסֵר לְאוֹתָהּ פְּעֻלָּה, אִם כֵּן הַהַתְחָלָה מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁהוּא חָסֵר וְדָחוּק לְכָךְ, וּ"מִן הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָּהּ" (תְּהִלִּים קיח, ה), שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַצַּעַר זוֹעֵק לַה', וְעוֹנֵהוּ בַּמֶּרְחָב,
records.originEnglish: And the start of every action stems from the necessity felt by the actor who lacks that outcome; thus the beginning emerges from deficiency, being pressured toward it, and "Out of the straits I called upon Yah" (Psalms 118:5), where out of distress he cries to Hashem, Who answers him with expansive relief,
records.targetHebrew: עזי וזמרת יה. עזי רומז על תקיפות. וזמרת רומז על צמצום. היינו שכל תקופות ישראל הוא רק מזה שהשי"ת צמצם גודל אורו וזה וזמרת י"ה וכדאי' בתקוני הזהר (תקון כ"א דף ס"ג) שבשם י"ה ברא עלמין סתימין ובשם ו"ה ברא עלמא דין ועלמא דאתי. היינו שהשי"ת צמצם גודל אורו והציב גוון בעוה"ז שאין שום שלימות בלתי עבודת ישראל ועי"ז הצמצום יש להשי"ת חיבור ואחדות עם ישראל ועל זה הצמצום נאמר (תהילים קי״ח:ה׳) מן המצר קראתי י"ה ענני במרחב י"ה שעי"ז הצמצום רואים ישראל החיבור שיש להשי"ת עמהם ואין לך גודל הרחבה מזה. לזה אומר ויהי לי לישועה שעי"ז החיבור נשפעים כל הישועות לישראל:
records.targetEnglish: “My strength and song is Yah”: strength indicates firmness, and song indicates limitation. Israel's strength comes from Hashem's limiting the greatness of His light. Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 21, page 63) says that with the name Yah He created the hidden worlds, and with Vav-He He created this world and the World to Come. Hashem limited His light and placed within this world a form in which completion requires Israel's service. Through this limitation there is a bond and unity with Israel. Concerning it the verse says, “From narrowness I called Yah; Yah answered me in breadth.” Through the limitation Israel sees its connection with Hashem, and there is no greater breadth than this. Therefore it says, “He became my deliverance”: all deliverances flow to Israel through this connection.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: Concealment prepares a fuller reception of Torah
records.themeSummary: The growth of Oral Torah after destruction makes the transformation concrete.
records.explanation: Matot develops the same twenty-two-day and alphabet structure by pointing to the expansion of Oral Torah through the Tannaim and Amoraim after the destruction. This supplies a concrete counterpart to the siman's movement from a powerful vision toward acquired Torah. The comparison concerns the capacity to receive and develop the light within concealment; it does not make the destruction itself the desired final state.
records.originHebrew: וּבְאוֹתוֹ זְמַן יוֹרֵד שֶׁפַע דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה, רַק שֶׁהוּא בִּרְאִיָּה כְּטַעַם מַרְאוֹת יְחֶזְקֵאל. וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נז:): הָרוֹאֶה יְחֶזְקֵאל יְצַפֶּה לְחָכְמָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דּוּגְמַת פֶּסַח "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי", וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁבוּעוֹת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בְּקִנְיָן, וְצָרִיךְ מ"ט יְמֵי סְפִירָה בֵּינְתַיִם. וְכֵן מִי' בְּאָב עַד רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֵם מ"ט יְמֵי סְפִירַת נְקִיִּים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַתְחִיל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּקִנְיָן כְּפִי תֹּקֶף הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּצָרִים:
records.originEnglish: and during that period an abundant influx of words of Torah descends, only that it occurs in vision, matching the visions of Ezekiel. And our Sages stated (Berakhot 57b): one who sees Ezekiel should anticipate wisdom, which mirrors Passover where "a maidservant saw at the Sea, etc.," and afterward Shavuot brings the Giving of the Torah in permanent acquisition, requiring forty-nine days of the Omer count in between. And so from the Tenth of Av until Rosh Hashanah are forty-nine clean days of counting, and afterward words of Torah commence in permanent acquisition commensurate with the intensity of the vision beheld during the Three Weeks of Bein HaMetzarim.
records.targetHebrew: וזה לשון בין המצרים כמיצר מכאן ומיצר מכאן שאין לההסתר התפשטות לא קודם המיצר וגם לא אחר ת"ב שכבר נתקן ונשלם הכל דייקא בימים הללו בתוך ההסתר כמו שראינו שדייקא אחר חורבן הבית התחיל התפשטות והתרבות תורה שבעל פה על ידי התנאים והאמוראים שעמדו אחר זה דוקא. וכמו שא' במד' (תנחו' ר"פ נח) שעיקר התגלות תורה שבעל פה הוא דייקא על ידי צער ויסורים ועליהם נאמר העם ההולכים בחשך ראו אור גדול.
records.targetEnglish: This is the meaning of “between the narrow straits”: there is a boundary on either side, so the concealment cannot extend before it or beyond Tisha B'Av. Repair and completion take place precisely within those concealed days. We see that after the Temple's destruction, Oral Torah began to spread and multiply through the Tannaim and Amoraim who arose afterward. The Midrash likewise says that Oral Torah is principally disclosed through pain and toil, and concerning them it says, “The people walking in darkness saw a great light.”
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.targetRef: Tiferet Yosef, Ha'azinu and Shabbat Shuvah 11
records.themeTitle: Each creature can supply a particular lesson
records.themeSummary: The powers distributed through creation can teach different aspects of human service.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same verse about learning from animals by naming distinct virtues in different creatures. Their particular powers may exceed a person's present achievement in that respect. This clarifies the siman's move from natural action to chosen learning: a person recognizes the lesson and brings it into his own service, while the siman itself supplies the conditions of necessary bodily life and sanctifying the Name.
records.originHebrew: קעג] כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הַטִּבְעִיִּים הֵם עוֹשִׂים רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כֹּל פָּעַל ה' לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ד) – לְקִילּוּסוֹ, וְאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ז.): בְּגִינַאי נַהֲרָא, אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנִי – מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּטִבְעוֹ כָּךְ וּלְפִיכָךְ גַּם הָאָדָם, כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשִׂים הַטִּבְעִיִּים שֶׁהוּא מֻכְרָח בָּהֶם מִצַּד טִבְעוֹ, נִקְרָא הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ וְיֵשׁ מִצְוָה בַּדָּבָר; וּבִכְלָל גַּם כֵּן אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה וְזִוּוּג, שֶׁהוּא בְּטֶבַע כִּבְכָל בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים הַטִּבְעִיִּים שֶׁאֵינָם בְּחִירִיִּים; וּבִלְבַד מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ, כְּגוֹן אֲכִילָה לְרַעֲבוֹן,
records.originEnglish: All natural phenomena fulfill the will of the Blessed Name, as it is written: "Hashem has made everything for His own purpose" (Proverbs 16:4)—meaning for His praise; and they stated in Chullin 7a regarding the river Ginai: "I am going to perform the will of my Maker," which is simply its natural flowing and therefore a human being as well, when engaging in natural actions to which he is compelled by his physical nature, is considered going to perform the will of his Maker, and a mitzvah resides in the matter; and this includes eating, drinking, and marital intimacy, which are natural as in all animals that do not possess free choice; provided it is done out of necessity, such as eating to satisfy hunger,
records.targetHebrew:
בהנחל עליון גוים בהפרידו בני אדם יצב גבולות עמים למספר בני ישראל כי חלק ד' עמו.
והיינו שהשי"ת מנחיל גם להאומות כחות גדולים, כי בכל מיני ברואים נמצא אצלם כחות יקרים, כמו שאיתא בש"ס (עירובין ק':) על הפסוק (איוב ל״ה:י״א) מלפנו מבהמות ארץ ומעוף השמים יחכמנו. אלמלא לא ניתנה תורה היינו למדין צניעות מחתול וגזל מנמלה ועריות מיונה ודרך ארץ מתרנגול. וכן אצל האומות נמצא ג"כ לפעמים כחות גדולות יותר מאצל ישראל, כי אצל ישראל כתיב (דברים ז׳:ז׳) כי אתם המעט מכל העמים ומכל שכן אצל צבאי מעלה נמצא כחות גדולים. וזה בהנחל עליון גוים בהפרידו בני אדם, אבל העיקר כי חלק ד' עמו יעקב חבל נחלתו והיינו שזה מורה שהעיקר הוא בשביל ישראל:
records.targetEnglish: “When the Most High apportioned nations… He set the boundaries of peoples according to the number of Israel, for Hashem's portion is His people.” Hashem grants great powers to the nations too, and precious powers are found in all kinds of creatures. The Gemara interprets “He teaches us from the beasts of the earth and makes us wise from the birds”: had Torah not been given, we would learn modesty from the cat, avoidance of theft from the ant, fidelity from the dove and proper conduct from the rooster. Great powers can likewise sometimes be found among the nations exceeding Israel's, for Israel is described as “the fewest of all peoples” (Deuteronomy 7:7); all the more are great powers found among the heavenly hosts. Yet the principal point is “Hashem's portion is His people; Yaakov is the rope of His inheritance”: the whole is directed toward Israel.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 6
records.themeTitle: Rule over oneself precedes rule over others
records.themeSummary: Authority requires governing the impulse rather than expressing it.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach interprets the same verse, “Through Me kings reign,” as self-rule preceding rule of others. This supplies a further condition beside the existing note on the Sanhedrin: the siman's royal exception is not an outlet for an uncontrolled impulse. The comparison describes a prerequisite of authority; self-confidence alone does not confer that office or its powers.
records.originHebrew: אַמְנָם מִדַּת מַלְכוּת הוּא דַּיְיקָא לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אַדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם – יָדֶיךָ חַדּוֹת וַחֲרוּצוֹת לִרְדּוֹת בָּהֶן עוֹלָמוֹ. וְנֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "אַדְמוֹנִי" כִּבְעֵשָׂו, רַק "עִם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם" – מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג), לְכָךְ זָכָה לְמַלְכוּת. וְשָׁאוּל נִסְתַּלֵּק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה רַחְמָן עַל הָאַכְזָרִים כַּנּוֹדָע, דְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּת הִיא מִדַּת הַדִּין הַקָּשָׁה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ", כִּי אוֹרַיְיתָא נָפְקָא מִגְּבוּרָה כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, פ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
records.originEnglish: however, the attribute of monarchy is specifically the reverse, as our Sages expounded concerning King David: your hands are sharp and decisive to rule His world with them. And of him it was said "ruddy" as of Esau, only "with beautiful eyes"—meaning with the consent of the Sanhedrin (Bereishit Rabbah 63:8), which is why he merited kingship. And Saul was removed because he showed mercy to the cruel, as is known, for the attribute of monarchy is the severe attribute of strict judgment, and it is stated: "By me kings reign" (Proverbs 8:15), because Torah issues from Gevurah, as brought in the Zohar (Part III, 80b),
records.targetHebrew: "ומלכי צדק מלך שלם הוציא לחם ויין, והוא כהן וכולי". כתיב (משלי ח, טו): "בי מלכים ימלכו", והנה כפי הפשט היה לכתוב: "בי ימלכו מלכים", אך רמז בזה שאין הקדוש ברוך הוא ממנה למלך רק מי שיוכל למלוך תחלה על עצמו, אותו ממנה גם על אחרים, כענין שנאמר (אבות פרק ד משנה א): "איזהו גבור? הכובש את יצרו". וזהו "בי מלכים ימלכו", היינו מי שמולך על עצמו ושכלו מושל על תאותו, אז "ימלכו", היינו יהיה מלך על כל,
records.targetEnglish: “Malki-Tzedek, king of Shalem, brought out bread and wine, and he was a priest.” The verse says, “Through Me kings reign.” In its plain word order it could have said, “Through Me reign kings.” Placing “kings” first hints that the Holy One appoints as king only someone able first to rule himself; such a person is then appointed over others, as in “Who is mighty? One who conquers his impulse.” Thus “through Me kings” means one who rules himself, whose mind governs his desire; then “they reign,” becoming king over all.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The two messianic stages have an order
records.themeSummary: The removal associated with Yosef precedes the completed kingship associated with David.
records.explanation: Divrei Chalomot develops the same future sequence through Adar and Nissan. The work associated with Yosef and Amalek precedes the full disclosure associated with Judah. This clarifies why the siman makes the order relevant to permanence. Its extension to a small sanctuary remains an analogy about preparing its foundations before personal elevation.
records.originHebrew: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד פָּסְקָה לְפִי שָׁעָה, לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה אָז קוֹדֶמֶת לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק. מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד, שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ אֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק, לְפִי שֶׁבָּא אַחַר כָּךְ. וְכֵן בְּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת מְעַט דְּמִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט שֶׁבַּגּוֹלָה: כְּשֶׁהַמְּחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק, הַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע, וְגַם קְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם קוֹדְמִים לְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת קְדוּשַׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ – אָז אֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק:
records.originEnglish: In contrast, the monarchy of the House of David ceased temporarily, because it originally preceded the total eradication of Amalek. Whereas in the future, the name of the Messiah will have no interruption, because it arrives afterward. And so it is regarding the miniature elevation of a miniature sanctuary in the Diaspora: when the blotting out of Amalek—namely the root of evil—and the sanctity of the place precede the elevation of the soul's sanctity, then it suffers no interruption.
records.targetHebrew: וכן יהיה לעתיד: משיח בן יוסף באדר, ומשיח בן דוד בניסן [דבו עתידין לגאל גאלה השלימה, ובאדר הוא מחית עמלק הקודמת לשלמות השם והכסא המתגלה בגאלה השלימה, שאינו נופל אלא ביד זרעא דיוסף שהוא הלהבה לשרף את בית עשו; ומשיח בן יוסף הוא יהיה הנלחם עם עמלק, וזהו הזמן באדר, ואחר מחיתו יזכה לשם שלם שהוא דרגא דיהודה דנקרא כלו על שמו של הקדוש ברוך הוא, מה שאין כן ביוסף רק שלש אותיות, וכמו שאמרו בסוטה (י׳ עמוד ב׳), וזהו כל זמן שעדין אין השם שלם].
records.targetEnglish: So it will be in the future: Mashiach son of Yosef in Adar, and Mashiach son of David in Nissan, when the complete redemption will take place. Adar is the removal of Amalek, which falls only through Yosef's descendants, the flame consuming the house of Esav, preceding the completed divine name and throne disclosed in redemption. Mashiach son of Yosef will fight Amalek then. After its removal he will merit the complete name, the level of Judah, who is called by the Holy One's whole name, while Yosef has only three of its letters, corresponding to the time before the name is complete.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: The same verse does not dispense with atonement
records.themeSummary: Recognizing providence and repairing an act remain distinguishable.
records.explanation: Siman 128 explicitly uses “In all your ways know Him” while retaining the need for atonement even for an act understood through a holy purpose. This is an important companion to the retrospective conclusion here. The knowledge that one's power came from Hashem is meant to weaken the urge to disobey and open return; it is not a self-issued exemption from the work of repair.
records.originHebrew: וְגַם בֶּעָבָר, עַל יְדֵי זֶה: "וְהוּא יְיַשֵּׁר אֹרְחֹתֶיךָ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, ו); "דֶּרֶךְ" נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְ"אֹרַח" הוּא מִן הַצַּד, וּכְשֶׁמְּקַיֵּים "דָּעֵהוּ" אָז נִקְרָא הַכֹּל "דֶּרֶךְ" שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ. אֲבָל גַּם "אֹרְחֹתֶיךָ" שֶׁכְּבָר עָבַרְתָּ וְהִטִּיתָ מִן הַצַּד וְחוּץ מִדֶּרֶךְ הָרָאוּי, אִם עַכְשָׁו מְקַיֵּים "דָּעֵהוּ", יֵדַע שֶׁגַּם זֶה הָיָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאִם כֵּן הוּא מְיוּשָּׁר:
records.originEnglish: And regarding the past as well, through this: "and He shall make your paths straight" (Proverbs 3:6); a "way" (derekh) denotes the king's highway, while a "path" (orach) is from the side, and when one fulfills "acknowledge Him," then everything is called a "way," which is the king's highway. But even "your paths" where you have already transgressed and strayed off to the side, outside the proper way—if you now fulfill "acknowledge Him," you will realize that this too was encompassed by the Blessed Name, and if so, it is made straight.
records.targetHebrew: [קכח] כשאדם עושה עבירה כענין "עת לעשות וגומר" (תהלים קיט, קכו) ו"בכל דרכיך דעהו]" (משלי ג, ו), מכל מקום צריך כפרה על העבירה שעשה,
records.targetEnglish: When a person does a transgressive act in the sense of “a time to act for Hashem” and “in all your ways know Him,” he nevertheless needs atonement for the act he did.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.

records.themeTitle: What Yaakov's completeness clarified about the gift
records.themeSummary: His distress concerned the right relation of the property to its root of life.
records.explanation: Vayishlach explains that Yaakov's distress was not merely the loss of a quantity: he feared that his already clarified property was still not rightly sorted. The later completeness disclosed that the portion sent to Esav had a relation to the work of extracting the holy sparks. This develops the siman's final link between restored money and restored bodily wholeness through the spiritual relation of the property, rather than reducing the passage to a financial calculation.
records.originHebrew: וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם" (שָׁם לג, יח), וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת לג:): שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה שָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ, שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּלֵּם לוֹ אוֹתוֹ דּוֹרוֹן, שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַן, מִמֵּילָא שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ בִּצְלִיעָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן:
records.originEnglish: And afterward: "And Jacob came whole" (Genesis 33:18), concerning which our Sages stated (Shabbat 33b): whole in his body, whole in his wealth; meaning that because he became whole in his wealth—that gift having been repaid to him and rectified—he automatically became whole in his body regarding his limping as well.
records.targetHebrew: וכן יעקב אע"ה נצטער על הדורון ששלח לעשו וכמ"ש (ב"ר פ' עו) ותעבור המנחה על פניו אף הוא בעקא והיינו שכבר היה לו העדרים מבוררין אצלו וכמ"ש בב"ר שהיה לו ס"ר עדרים והיינו כמספר שורש נפשות ישראל שמכל א' יהיה עדר שלם. וכאן ראה שהוצרך לשלוח מהם לעשו והיה לו צער מזה שמא אין רכושו מבורר עוד. ואח"כ נתברר לו שהוא שלם בממונו ולא חסר כלום מאותו דורון שזה היה שיייך לעשו שהיה לו שייכות בהם וע"י הדורון הוציא ממנו הני"ק וכמו שאמרנו.
records.targetEnglish: Yaakov was distressed over the gift he sent Esav: “the gift passed before him,” and he was in distress. He had already clarified his flocks: the Midrash says he had six hundred thousand flocks, corresponding to the number of the roots of Israel's souls, each root becoming a complete flock. Now that he had to send some to Esav, he feared that his property was not yet clarified. Later it became clear to him that he was complete in his property and nothing was lacking from that gift: the portion belonged to the relation with Esav, and through the gift he extracted the holy sparks from him.
records.translationProvenance: Akiva Publishing original English translation, checked against the complete cited Hebrew paragraph during the comprehensive Tzidkat HaTzadik review; source quotation is separate from the editorial explanation.
